title: Fear and fallout three months on from Northern Ireland's race riots
summary: Northern Ireland saw consecutive nights of violence following a knife attack - but how are victims faring now?
full_text:
Fear and fallout three months on from Northern Ireland's race riots
- Published
Daylight is still extending across the summer evening sky over Belfast when Maria looks out the window of the house she shares with her two teenage daughters and sees people across the road putting on balaclavas.
It is Tuesday 9 June and parts of Northern Ireland are engulfed in violence.
Buses are being hijacked and set on fire, with water cannon deployed by police to quell rioters, and people targeted because of the colour of their skin – these scenes will all be broadcast around the world over the next 48 hours.
Maria has lived peacefully in her home in a loyalist area of east Belfast for two years. Until now.
"I just panicked. I started to fill buckets of water. I even filled my [bath] tub," she said.
"That was my breaking moment.
"I thought: 'If a fire starts, how do I get out of this?'"
'The lions surround the sheep'
Henry, who has lived in Belfast for a year after leaving his home in Nigeria, remembers the night as "all of a sudden you're getting a hint that you're a stranger".
"How would I put it? It's like suddenly you see lots of lions surrounding the sheep.
"You know definitely the lions are stronger than the sheep. Definitely they would be devoured."
Why did the violence break out?
The rioting began after footage of a brutal knife attack was widely circulated on social media. The clip was shared by far-right activist Tommy Robinson, as well as by Elon Musk, racking up millions of views on his X platform.
A call for peaceful anti-immigration protests that evening gave way to violent scenes, mostly in loyalist areas.
Protesters were told to target the homes of refugees and asylum seekers, but any person of colour was at risk, with rioters shouting "foreigners out" as they broke down doors and windows in homes across Belfast.
Revisiting those dark nights almost three months later, it's clear the reverberations are still being felt among communities, particularly as officials continue to count the cost of supporting those displaced.
As the chaos spread, many were forced out of their homes with nothing more than the clothes they were wearing.
Northern Ireland's social housing authority, the Housing Executive, has said 76 households presented to it as homeless following 48 hours of violence, while community workers on the ground said that number was much higher, when including those who went to stay with friends or left the country.
'There was hysteria from the kids'
But, at the same time as social media posts were circulating organising the riots, something else was happening online.
A network of groups normally helping migrant communities with things like food banks and interpreter support got together on WhatsApp.
They helped more than 200 people, often rushing into areas of violence to take those targeted to safety.
Anne works for one of the groups and described messages as "coming in as fast as people could pick them up".
"And even then, when we were down town collecting people, we were then also being asked to go somewhere else, you know, to pick somebody else up.
"There's a lift needed to take somebody to work, lift needed to take somebody into the hospital for a shift. There's somebody coeliac, no food in the house, pick up such and such at an address."
Ciara, another community worker, responded to a call from four Sudanese women fearing that their home would be targeted.
"I was trying to reassure them. I don't speak Arabic and they were just coming along. It was blind trust. But then I was on adrenaline thinking: 'I have to keep these people safe'.
"Imagine you were being brought somewhere and you didn't know where you were going. I just thought: 'God, these poor people might not even understand what I'm saying'."
Then there was Carolyn, a community worker of 35 years experience. Her effort was gargantuan.
She has a large home 60 miles away from Belfast and, with the help of a coach driver and his vehicle, managed to take 22 people out of the city to her house in County Antrim, where they stayed for a week.
"It was dark, nearly midnight, when they got here, and there was a lot of crying and hysteria from the kids and the families, just not knowing where they were and stuff like that. They were traumatised."
Some of them, she recalled, didn't have a change of clothes. A mum with a baby didn't have nappies or formula.
"It was crazy. To think of how you would just flee your home, not able to take anything with you and try and protect you and your kids."
Michaela Rafferty, who works with the Anaka Women's Collective helping migrant women, said people arrive in Northern Ireland without an understanding of the complexity of division – or how housing is segregated along sectarian lines.
"They don't know that actually it's not safe for me to be in this street. And even when they do realise that they have no power to move out," she said.
A hotspot of violence
East Belfast, parts of which are loyalist, was one of the hotspots of violence.
Brian Anderson, a Methodist minister with the East Belfast Mission, said the narrative that loyalist communities are losing out to those in republican areas is deeply ingrained.
"It's perceived within loyalist communities that the other side are getting. And we are losing," he said.
"We're losing our culture. Houses are not being developed. We're losing our jobs. And, so, you put it into that context of them winning and the perception that we're losing. That's the green-orange issue."
"You then bring other colours of nationality into it," he added. "They, then sadly, have become the target for a small minority of people."
He said there had always been a "silent majority" against violence in Northern Ireland's recent history, but a "vocal minority who have been for violence, and they seem to hold sway".
"We still have a problem in loyalist communities whereby if we have something we're cross about or angry about or don't understand or feel threatened by, we seem to turn to violence," he said.
Has anyone been arrested?
The Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) said its officers helped many people to safety, including a two-month-old baby. It said officers worked around the clock to protect life and prevent further harm. It has so far arrested 39 people in connection with the rioting.
After the riots, Maria stayed inside her home for seven days, too frightened to leave. Her daughters didn't emerge for almost three weeks.
She feels there's been a subtle shift with people "sticking to their corners".
"I've been asking: 'Where is home?' I had been convincing myself that here was my home."
She's grateful for the support she received but still has worries about the future.
"We don't need to destroy things, they can't burn the entire thing down."

title: Baby whose parents feared had just days to live is 'thriving' after life-saving heart operation
summary: Doctors have told mum and dad Catrin and Dylan it could take years for a donor to materialise.
full_text:
Baby whose parents feared had just days to live is 'thriving' after life-saving heart operation
- Published
A baby, whose parents feared had just days to live, is "thriving" after having life-saving operations on his heart.
Macs Green, a previously "completely healthy baby" suffered two cardiac arrests and was diagnosed with dilated cardiomyopathy - which can lead to heart failure.
After a struggle to find suitable hospital beds, he has now had device called a Berlin Heart, external fitted, which takes over the function of his heart.
But he still needs a transplant and doctors have told his parents Catrin and Dylan they do not know how long the wait will be before he gets one.
But, after his operation in Newcastle's Freeman Hospital, Dylan said Macs was already "completely different" from how he was before.
Before surgery he had been in a specialist unit in Bristol Royal Children's Hospital on an extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, external (Ecmo) machine, which helped pump oxygenated blood around his body.
Town planner Dylan, 35, told Newyddion S4C, external: "There was talk of end of life at that point. We're so pleased he's on the Berlin Heart.
"It means he can come off the drugs which have been sedating him. Since then, he's a completely different baby.
"He's smiling, he's responding to us. Before now, he's just been a small baby lying on a bed."
Solicitor Catrin said, since the operation, it was like "having our baby back" for the couple, who have two other children, Caio, five, and Gruff, and that Macs had been "absolutely thriving"
After multiple surgeries, Macs' Berlin Heart was fitted on 7 August after leaving Bristol for Newcastle.
A Berlin Heart is a type of ventricular assist device, external - an air-driven pump that sits outside the body and takes over the job of the heart by pumping blood around the body.
The NHS Blood and Transplant team said 17 of these had been fitted in children across the UK in 2024-25.
Catrin, 32, said the family, from Cardiff, were now waiting for a real heart for Macs.
"They've told us... he's likely to have to wait 18 months for a heart. It could be two years, it could be more than that.
"But a heart could also turn up tomorrow.
"If we knew we were just waiting and living in a hospital that would be fine, but there are a lot of potential risks that come with being on a Berlin Heart and a lot of things which can affect him.
"We just hope now he can remain stable."
The family are now urging parents to consider organ donation should they lose a child and thanked the hospital staff and others who have supported them.
"We are extremely grateful," said Dylan.

title: Tropical Storm Moke advances towards Hawaii with heavy rain, strong winds
summary: For the second week in a row, Hawaii Island, also known as the Big Island, faces threats from an intensifying storm.
full_text:
Tropical Storm Moke advances towards Hawaii with heavy rain, strong winds
For the second week in a row, Hawaii Island, also known as the Big Island, faces threats from an intensifying storm.
Tropical Storm Moke is grinding towards Hawaii, bringing gusts of wind and heavy rain only a week after the islands faced similar conditions from Hurricane Lala.
On Saturday, Hawaii residents prepared for the latest storm, which is expected to pass south of Hawaii Island, the largest island in the Hawaiian archipelago, overnight and into the following morning.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3Hurricane Lala weakens to a tropical storm, but flooding persists in Hawaii
- list 2 of 3Storm Lala strengthens into a Category 1 hurricane as it nears Hawaii
- list 3 of 3Tropical Storm Lala leaves Hawaii flooded and without power
As of 11am Hawaii Standard Time (21:00 GMT), Moke was located about 684 kilometres, or 425 miles, south of Hilo, a city on the eastern coast of Hawaii Island. It was moving west-northwest at 19km/h (12mph).
The National Hurricane Center (NHC) in the United States reported that the storm’s maximum sustained winds were about 85km/h (50mph).
Moke, like Lala, is forecast to spare the Big Island a potentially disastrous direct hit. But the island is still recovering from Lala, a Category 1 storm that spurred heavy flooding and power outages.
At least one person died in last weekend’s storm.
Lala came close enough to Hawaii Island to dump more than 1,000mm (39 inches) of rain in some locations, causing rivers to burst their banks.
High winds also bent tall palm trees and downed electrical lines, forcing nearly 130,000 utility customers to lose power.
Hawaii Governor Josh Green and other state officials have urged people to prepare for Moke by restocking food, medicine and other daily essentials ahead of the storm’s passage.
“It could certainly have a big impact because we’ve already been hit hard,” Green said in a video statement. “We’re pre-positioning all kinds of additional equipment and people. I’ve also authorised 100 rooms, hotel rooms, for people to go to, in case they don’t have enough services or protection, safety.”
Green added that, while power had been restored to most of Hawaii Island after Lala, some remote areas were still experiencing outages. Power is expected to be fully restored by September 8.
After passing Hawaii Island during the night, Moke is projected to continue on a westward path near the islands through early Tuesday, according to Casey Oswant, a meteorologist with the Honolulu office of the US National Weather Service.
“There will still be impacts, especially to the windward and southeast sides of the Big Island, but it will probably be a little bit more limited than what we saw with Lala,” Oswant said.
The National Hurricane Center projects that Moke will bring roughly 130mm to 250mm (5 to 10 inches) of rainfall over the next two days on the southeast and windward sides of the Big Island. Some isolated areas could see as much as 380mm (15 inches).
Eastern Maui, meanwhile, is likely to receive 76mm to 150mm (3 to 6 inches), with smaller amounts of precipitation expected across the rest of the island chain.
Governor Green warned that the heavy rain is unlikely to end with Moke.
“Everyone be very careful,” he said. “This storm will be followed by another storm front about a week later, and we continue to see the impacts of these major weather fronts that have hit Hawaii.”

full_text:
India launches rescue mission as Panama-flagged cargo ship sinks off east coast
The vessel had 24 crew on board, including 20 Chinese nationals, 3 Myanmar nationals and 1 Bangladeshi, according to India’s coastguard
India’s maritime rescue agency lost communication on Saturday with a Panama-flagged cargo vessel that sank off the coast of eastern India, the Indian coastguard said.
The vessel had 24 crew on board, including 20 Chinese nationals, three Myanmar nationals and one Bangladeshi, according to Commandant Amit Uniyal, a spokesman for the coastguard.
The coastguard sent two vessels for the search-and-rescue mission from Sri Vijaya Puram, formerly known as Port Blair, Uniyal said.
The coastguard has rescued two people from life rafts. The search-and-rescue mission is under way for the seafarers on the vessel, the agency said.
The Ocean Winner was carrying iron ore to Singapore after departing from India’s eastern Paradip port on Thursday, according to government sources, adding that the ship sank around 240 nautical miles (448km) from the port.
The cause of the sinking was unknown.

title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?
summary: Prospectors have come to West Pokot county in the hope a gram of the precious metal can change their lives.
full_text:
Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?
- Published
A goat herder from a remote area of western Kenya has told the BBC his discovery of a golden nugget has sparked a gold rush, overwhelming his small village over the last few weeks.
When people found out that 33-year-old Manasse Lomachar had sold his three grams of gold for 36,000 Kenyan shillings ($280; £205) several weeks ago, he believes this led to thousands of prospectors arrived in Cheporor.
And it is true that what last month was just bushland and rough grazing ground near the village is now scarred by pits, mounds of earth and makeshift mining camps.
It is not clear if was Lomachar's lucky find or other recent discoveries that sparked the excitement. But local authorities estimate that about 10,000 people arrived at the height of the rush.
Even a small amount of the precious metal can transform the futures of these men and women - from Kenya and neighbouring Uganda - many of whose precarious lives rest on an unreliable farming income.
People do sometimes pan for gold in these parts - but rarely find anything significant.
Lomachar's says his discovery came about purely by chance. While he was searching for a missing goat he encountered a group of women panning along a riverbed.
"I joined them, and that's how [the village] realised there was gold in this area," he says.
Farmer and herder Patrick Lokolia, from neighbouring Napawoi village, joined the gold rush hoping to earn some extra money to support his family.
"I have children in school, and paying school fees has been a big problem for me," he tells the BBC wearing an old Chelsea football top and standing amid the mining activity.
Eighteen-year-old Abigael Chelengat says she had never mined before coming to Cheporor from a nearby district, but arrived hoping to find enough gold to pay her school fees and help keep her younger siblings in school.
Behind her hundreds of people work side by side, hacking into the rocky ground with hoes and shovels.
Others carry the earth to a nearby seasonal river, where mostly women crouch in the murky water, washing and sifting mud and sand hoping to detect a tiny trace of the element.
Some of the more experienced miners are deep in holes excavating the earth and drilling at rocks with the same goal.
Hope is kept alive by stories of those for whom the effort has paid off - like Lomachar.
Samuel Kiarie, the deputy commissioner of West Pokot county, says he thinks the rush began after two notable discoveries.
"Young men found what appeared to be a substantial amount of gold. The following day, women made another significant find in the same area," he tells the BBC.
Kiarie explains that women have been finding small quantities of alluvial gold along the same seasonal riverbed for years, typically earning $8-$23 a week.
But the uncovering of larger quantities at the beginning of August is what caught the attention of many people.
Kiarie reckons as rumours spread, the number and size of the discoveries were exaggerated - drawing in ever larger groups of people with little or no mining experience who hoped to replicate the reported early successes.
Since the initial rush, the number of prospectors has gone down to around 2,500 as some have given up the search.
While there is little doubt that some gold has been found in the area, questions remain about the size of the deposit in the earth and its commercial potential.
"I can confirm that small-scale gold traders told us they received an average of about 100 people every day," the deputy commissioner says - though whether the finds were actually gold is not known.
Individual discoveries reportedly range from amounts worth a few hundred Kenyan shillings to one find valued at approximately 78,000 shillings ($600).
West Pokot county borders Uganda, and communities on both sides have long-standing social and family ties.
Mugisha Godfrey, an artisanal miner from Busia in eastern Uganda, travelled to Cheporor after hearing about the discovery from a friend.
He immediately set out for the village spending about 100,000 Ugandan shillings ($27) to get there.
However, the living conditions in Cheporor are not favourable, he says.
"We sleep under the trees, and when morning comes, we continue working. Sometimes we work both day and night," Godfrey tells the BBC.
So far, he has found nothing. But he is not discouraged.
"We can't return unless we find something. Only when we have found what we need can we go back home," he says.
For others, the gold rush has created opportunities without requiring them to dig.
More than 200 businesses have emerged around the site, according to local officials, selling food, water and other essentials to the village's new population.
Irene Ameja travelled from neighbouring Baringo county to cater to the crowds. She sells bottled water, soft drinks, bread, milk and other foodstuffs.
"I am hoping that when I leave, I will have made enough money to continue with my business and expand it," she says.
But the rapid growth of the settlement has also exposed the area's lack of basic services.
"This is a forest and we are in the middle of the mountains," she says. "We don't have clean water to drink or even to bathe."
For women, she adds, the challenges become greater after dark: "You have to find somewhere safe to stay because most of the people sleeping here are men."
Local officials admit the influx has placed enormous pressure on an area with little infrastructure, no piped water and limited sanitation.
Public health officials have been deployed to monitor conditions and help prevent disease outbreaks.
The authorities say they have also increased security patrols amid concerns over sexual violence and the vulnerability of women and girls at the site.
Officials are also worried that children could be drawn into mining activities as schools prepare to reopen in September.
Measures are being put in place to discourage young people from remaining at the site once the new school term begins.
Those still searching are increasingly turning to deeper excavation.
Several truckloads of material have already been transported to nearby Ortum town for processing, with the authorities awaiting the results.
Until then, the size and commercial viability of any mining remain uncertain.
For Lomachar, the answer is not to stop the mining, but to make it more organised.
He wants the government to help local miners establish safer and more effective ways of finding and extracting the gold.
"We would ask the government to help us with things like metal detectors, which could help us find out whether there are other minerals here, so that our community can develop," he says.
He points to the homes nearby as evidence of the area's poverty.
"If you look around, there are hardly any houses with iron-sheet roofs; most are just thatched houses."

title: Iran warns nearby nations against joining US ‘economic war’ efforts
summary: The warning comes as US President Donald Trump threatens to isolate Iran economically to weaken its government.
full_text:
Iran warns nearby nations against joining US ‘economic war’ efforts
The warning comes as US President Donald Trump threatens to isolate Iran economically, to weaken its government.
Iran has threatened to treat nearby countries as enemies and target their interests if they join a United States campaign to cripple its economy.
Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, issued the warning in a Saturday interview with state broadcaster IRIB.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3Iranian president says time to end war with US from ‘position of strength’
- list 2 of 3Iran says new US sanctions violate sovereignty of other states
- list 3 of 3Iran grants permission for some Iraqi oil tankers to pass through Hormuz
“We’re telling all nearby countries not to join the US economic war. Otherwise, we will consider them as enemies,” Rezaei told IRIB.
His remarks come on the heels of escalating economic threats from the administration of US President Donald Trump.
On Wednesday, Trump announced his government would undertake the “most crushing economic operation” yet against Iran, as part of ongoing hostilities between the two countries.
The US and Israel have been locked in a war with Iran since February 28, when the two allies launched an initial volley of attacks against Tehran.
In addition to threatening Iran’s economy this week, Trump pledged “tremendous economic consequences” for any country that gives Iran “any type of lifeline”.
His Treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, echoed his threats the following day, saying, “You’re either with us or against us.”
In Saturday’s interview, Rezaei described Iran’s regional strategy as a three-stage sequence, which would start with efforts to de-escalate tensions with neighbouring countries.
“First we negotiate. Then, we try to separate them from America with pleasant language, because we are not really looking to expand the war,” he said.
Any countries that continue to side with the US would then be given time to reconsider, he said. “But in the third stage, we will definitely act.”
While the US has not stopped its military operations against Iran, Rezaei suggested that the Trump administration was betting that economic pressure would fracture Iranian society, forcing the war to come to an end.
“They hope that, if possible, they can break our unity with economic pressure and a group of protesters will take to the streets, and in a way, they will come to the aid of American F-35s,” he said, referring to a kind of military aircraft.
Negotiations to end the conflict have stalled in recent months, following the failure of a June 17 memorandum of understanding (MoU) that called for an “immediate and permanent termination of military operations”.
Control over the Strait of Hormuz, a major shipping lane off the coast of Iran, has become an enduring sticking point between the US and Iran.
Iran quickly moved to shut down traffic through the strait early in the war, sending the price of goods like oil and fertiliser skyrocketing.
Countries in the Middle East that were previously reliant on the strait for exports have started to pursue substitute trade routes.
But Rezaei warned that Iran would target those alternative oil-shipping routes out of the Gulf if regional states took part in the US’s plans of economic warfare.
Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Saturday also decried the incoming US measures as an assertion of “extraterritorial sovereignty” over United Nations member states.
Tehran has also reportedly considered widening its target list beyond the Middle East, with media outlets reporting it could strike US allies in Europe who have supported Trump’s operations.

One Nation MP ‘impressed’ with PM after rice factory rescue promise
Sarah Basford Canales
David Farley says he was “impressed” with Anthony Albanese after receiving an in-person guarantee from the prime minister that the Labor government would help out rice factories in his electorate.
Rice producer SunRice announced 78 workers would be sacked from mills in Leeton and Deniliquin this week, but ABC’s Insiders host, David Speers, says a funding package is being prepared to help out the producer and save those jobs.
Farley said:
I was impressed how Albanese at the Governor-General’s event the other night came straight up to me and said, ‘Look, I’m aware of it. I’m working on it. We’ll get it done’ ... even after, as we left the chamber the other day, we spoke all the way across to the Senate talking about it. How could it be done and put together? So you know, I tilt my hat to them.
Ben Carroll rejects Victorian Liberals’ proposal to split court of appealas ‘thought bubble’
Victoria’s premier Ben Carroll was asked this morning about the Liberal party’s proposal to split the court of appeal in two and appoint new judges if they win the election.
He says the Labor government has already reformed bail laws and is reviewing sentencing, leaving the Liberals “floundering”. Carroll went on:
The Liberal party are upset that we’ve captured the law and order agenda. And now they’re saying we’re going to skip that process and go to the court of appeal. That’s why they’ve had this thought bubble overnight, and they will not be able to explain it. That’s the simple truth … Let’s wait and see what all the legal stakeholders say about Mr Newbury’s new policy.
Carroll, who is trained as a lawyer, questioned how the Liberal party would reform a court that “has been around [for] 200 years, and rewrite case law overnight”. He said:
It shows you the Liberal party today have no legal expertise, but [are] totally at sea on having a policy agenda for the next election, and are floundering. We’ve seen today the Liberal party searching for a policy idea and not doing any homework.
Fur seal death ‘not unexpected’ asH5 bird flu spreads, federal agriculture minister says
The federal agriculture minister, Julie Collins, says the death of a fur seal in South Australia from H5 bird flu is “not unexpected” as the virus begins to spread through wild seabirds.
Speaking a short time ago in Hobart, Collins said the “distressing” news of the first confirmed case of a mammal on the mainland was anticipated and that it is “not possible to avoid significant losses”.
She said:
An infection of this individual animal is likely to have occurred due to exposure to infected wild birds or the environment that they share ... as I’ve been clear, we can’t stop it spreading in terms of, particularly, in wild birds, and where we see more dead wild birds, we do expect to see increased reports of marine mammals.
Collins said there had been 298 events across the country with 183 in South Australia, 86 in Victoria, 11 in New South Wales, 10 in Western Australia, seven in Tasmania and one in Queensland.

The Victorian premier, Ben Carroll, and health minister, Ingrid Stitt, have held a press conference this morning off the back of their announcement yesterday that the Labor government would open 10 free public dental clinics if re-elected in November.
Today, they’ve announced $12.9m to grow and retain the workforce required to operate the 10 clinics. The government estimates it will need 180 full-time equivalent workers to keep the 10 clinics running from 9am to 9pm on weekdays and 9am to 5pm on weekends.
Stitt said the funds will include $2.1m for relocation support for 20 dental clinicians for the three regional clinics, $3.8m to fund 30 dental assistant traineeships and 20 dental graduate placements for the next two years and $4.4m to attract and retain existing staff.
Carroll said that while some Victorians can access public dental care, the group is limited:
You can’t use a Medicare card for dental unless you’ve got a healthcare card or you are a category of a particular citizen, it is very difficult ... I’ve been visiting a lot of dentists over the past few weeks. There [are] waiting lists. People are in enormous, unbearable pain.
This will be a cost of living measure but it will also make sure that we deal with the healthcare of some of the most vulnerable Victorians. This is really going to fill the gap that’s been there for decades.
Concern Sydney Marathon medal may erroneously depict Munich stadium
Just a week away from the Sydney Marathon, speculation has been growing that a stadium in Munich may have been erroneously etched on to the event’s participation medal instead of a local Sydney landmark.
In an Instagram post on the official Sydney Marathon account earlier this week, revealing the design of the participation medal, runners were told they would “find the story of the course in the details” of the design:

But as the BBC reported on Saturday, the “landmarks” side of the medal appears to feature a stadium that looks like the Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany, rather than Allianz Stadium in Sydney (which the marathon route passes).
The reverse of the medal features an indigo and gold design by First Nations artist Ambrose Killian, representing kilometres of the course, and the eight global major marathons. Killian told the BBC he was not involved in the other side of the design.

full_text:
A long-nosed fur seal has died from H5 bird flu in South Australia, marking the first confirmed case in a mammal on the Australian mainland.
  The seal was found dead at Beachport on Wednesday on the state’s Limestone Coast.
  It marks a fresh escalation in the spread of the virus days after the South Australian premier, Peter Malinauskas, announced three mass mortality events on offshore islands involving more than 1,000 greater crested terns.
The federal agriculture minister, Julie Collins, said the seal death was “not unexpected” as the virus begins to spread through the country.
Speaking in Hobart on Sunday, Collins said the “distressing” news of the first confirmed case of a mammal on the mainland was anticipated and that it was “not possible to avoid significant losses”.
“An infection of this individual animal is likely to have occurred due to exposure to infected wild birds or the environment that they share,” she said.
“We can’t stop it spreading in terms of, particularly, in wild birds, and where we see more dead wild birds, we do expect to see increased reports of marine mammals.”
Collins said there had been 298 events across the country, with 183 in South Australia, 86 in Victoria, 11 in New South Wales, 10 in Western Australia, seven in Tasmania and one in Queensland.
The risk of human transmission remains low, but people are being urged to avoid sick or dead birds and report them to birdflu.gov.au.
The highly pathogenic strain of bird flu has killed millions of birds globally and crossed over into mammal species, including elephant seals.
  Long-nosed fur seals and the endangered Australian sea lion are among the mammal species the federal government has assessed as facing very high risk from the virus.
Jack Gough, the chief executive of the Invasive Species Council, said the virus spreading to Australia’s sea lion population could be an “extinction level event”.
“We are still just at the early stages of this devastating virus, and the bad news is going to keep coming for our wildlife as it spreads around the continent and between species,” he said.
 The SA government has also confirmed a little penguin found at Kangaroo Island this week tested positive for H5 bird flu.
Elsewhere, the Tasmanian government said 51 little penguins found on the state’s King Island were “assumed to” have died from H5 bird flu, but the deaths would not be declared a mass mortality event.
The state’s natural resources and environment department said a sample taken from one penguin found at the Port of Grassy tested positive for H5 bird flu, while a sample from a second penguin was inconclusive.
Wes Ford, the state’s incident controller for its bird flu response, said both samples had been sent to the Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness for further testing.
“The little penguin mortality event is not considered a mass mortality event, and the condition of the remaining deceased birds meant they were unsuitable for testing,” he said.
“As a result, the cause of death could not be confirmed, although it may be assumed to have been from bird flu.
“Our teams continue to monitor reports of sick and dead birds closely, with results from surveillance informing our response.”

title: Two years after launch, Walmart’s Flipkart is closing in on India’s quick-commerce leaders
summary: Flipkart's quick-commerce venture is delivering 1.1 million to 1.2 million orders a day, nearly triple its November volume.
full_text:
Indian startups spent years getting consumers accustomed to having groceries and everyday goods delivered within minutes. Now Walmart-owned Flipkart is rapidly closing the gap with those quick-commerce pioneers, as global rival Amazon mounts its own push into instant delivery.
Flipkart Minutes, which debuted in August 2024 as the e-commerce giant’s foray into quick commerce, is now delivering 1.1 million to 1.2 million orders a day, up from about 390,000 to 400,000 in November, people familiar with the matter told TechCrunch. That puts the two-year-old service close to Swiggy’s Instamart, which is delivering about 1.4 million orders a day, according to a person familiar with its operations.
The gap is notable as Flipkart is a relative latecomer to a market whose top ranks have been dominated by Instamart, Blinkit, and Zepto. Food-delivery giant Swiggy launched Instamart in 2020 and Zepto arrived the following year, both during the pandemic, while Blinkit traces its roots to online grocery platform Grofers, founded in 2013. The three have since established themselves as India’s top quick-commerce players.
Blinkit continues to dominate the market with around 3.4 million to 3.6 million daily orders, followed by Zepto at about 2.4 million to 2.6 million, per recent estimates from market research firm Datum Intelligence. Flipkart is now rapidly narrowing the gap with Instamart, the smallest of the three established leaders by order volume.
Instamart still has substantial scale. Earlier this month, Swiggy said the quick commerce service has more than 14 million monthly transacting users and operates over 1,200 dark stores across over 130 cities. The company has also been narrowing Instamart’s contribution-margin losses, with more than 45% of its dark-store network now contribution-margin positive.
Nonetheless, Flipkart has fueled that growth with an aggressive expansion of its delivery infrastructure. Minutes now operates about 1,020 to 1,050 micro-fulfillment centers — essentially small warehouses located close to customers specially to handle quick deliveries — up from 600 in January and about 340 a year ago, one of the sources told TechCrunch. The company is adding around 100 such facilities a month, the source said, aiming to have 1,500 by the end of 2026.
Flipkart’s advantage goes beyond adding dark stores. The company can tap an enormous pool of existing e-commerce customers it has already spent years and billions of dollars acquiring, giving Minutes a ready audience for faster deliveries, Satish Meena, an adviser at Datum Intelligence, told TechCrunch.
“Flipkart is already a serious player,” Meena said. “Once you open 1,000 dark stores and [are] doing a million orders per day, it’s serious enough.”
Minutes is also seeing customers return and shop more frequently. About 65% to 70% of customers making purchases on the service each month are repeat buyers, while transactions per customer have increased 50% to 60% from a year earlier, people familiar with the matter said.
Those customers are spending an average of about ₹400 to ₹500 (about $4.20–$5.20) per order, with fruits and vegetables, staples, dairy, and meat among the fast-growing categories, the sources said. Flipkart is also expanding its selection of higher-end gourmet products, including organic and artisanal items, as it looks to capture more of customers’ spending on Minutes.
Even as Minutes has expanded, its average delivery time has fallen to about 11 minutes, from 13 minutes a year ago, one of the sources told TechCrunch.
A battle for India’s shoppers
Flipkart’s growth comes as quick commerce takes a bigger role in how Indians shop online, even as broader consumer demand has shown signs of weakness. In a recent report, Bernstein analysts said while the country’s consumption growth softened in July, a shift toward quick commerce and e-commerce continued, with quick-commerce platforms recording healthy growth in monthly active users.
Similar to Flipkart, Amazon is striving to gain its share in the Indian quick-commerce market. The Seattle-based company has been expanding Amazon Now, its quick-commerce service, as it seeks to bring the instant-delivery model to its existing e-commerce customer base.
During CEO Andy Jassy’s visit to India in June, Amazon stated that Now became its fastest-growing business in India, with orders doubling every quarter since launch. The company also laid out plans to take the service to more than 300 cities and set up a network of more than 1,000 micro-fulfilment centers, alongside larger facilities aimed at expanding the range of products it can deliver within minutes.
Amazon, Flipkart, Swiggy, Zepto, and Blinkit parent Eternal did not respond to requests for comment.
The wuick commerce expansion is increasingly defensive as well as offensive for both Flipkart and Amazon, Meena told TechCrunch. As consumers grow accustomed to receiving certain purchases almost immediately, the e-commerce giants risk losing those transactions to specialist quick-commerce platforms if they cannot offer comparable speed.
“Can you go back to scheduled delivery now in grocery? No,” Meena said. “You will not go back.”

title: Ripple 殺入穩定幣放貸，合作 Clearpool、Cicada 推出 RLUSD 信貸基金
summary:
Ripple 攜手借貸平台 Clearpool 與信貸管理商 Cicada Partners 推出以 RLUS […]

〈Ripple 殺入穩定幣放貸，合作 Clearpool、Cicada 推出 RLUSD 信貸基金〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
Ripple 攜手借貸平台 Clearpool 與信貸管理商 Cicada Partners 推出以 RLUSD 穩定幣計價的機構信貸基金，向金融科技與支付業者放營運資金貸款；但底層的 XRPL 原生借貸功能（XLS-66、XLS-65）仍在網路投票中，商品尚未正式上線。
（前情提要：瑞波(Ripple)推出EVM相容側鏈XRPL Sidechain、新穩定幣$RLUSD：解鎖DeFi和RWA新機會）
（背景補充：Ripple 推出企業後臺管理 XRP 和法幣，瞄準年 13 兆美元企業數位資產金庫系統）
瑞波（Ripple）準備讓穩定幣 RLUSD 從「支付工具」跨進「放貸市場」。根據 Ripple 與合作夥伴的公告內容，公司將以有限合夥人身分，注資一個專放營運資金貸款的機構信貸基金，物件鎖定金融科技（fintech）與支付業者，貸款一律以 RLUSD 計價，並在 XRP Ledger（XRPL）上執行。
負責整條資金流程的，是兩家公司：以借貸池基建見長的 Clearpool 負責搭建並管理借貸池的技術與結構；信貸管理商 Cicada Partners 則負責找借款人、議定放款條件與盯信用風險。Ripple 與其他機構同條款參與投資、不保證虧損，基金規模與注資額均未揭露。
XLS-66、XLS-65 未過關，商品暫停在測試網
關鍵的前提還沒就位：這套貸款的底層，是兩項仍在 XRPL 升級投票中的原生功能，作為借貸協議的 XLS-66，負責在鏈上直接放款與還款；單一資產金庫的 XLS-65，則是多位投資人的資金集合，交由基金經理（此例為 Cicada）決定流向。目前 Clearpool 在開發網（devnet）測試整合，兩項功能尚未在 XRPL 主網生效。
執行細節上，借款方取得與歸還的都是 RLUSD，等於替 Ripple 的美元穩定幣創造需求，同時把借貸活動搬到鏈上。XRP 本身不涉及放貸，僅用於支付交易手續費與帳戶最低餘額，避免幣價震盪影響借貸雙方的結算。
穩定幣放貸，Ripple 的「第二曲線」
這套架構建立在既有成績上：Cicada 號稱已承做超過 8.6 億美元的授信，並將出任基金普通合夥人與資金池管理者；Clearpool 自 2021 年以來，也已促成逾 9.3 億美元的機構貸款。
Ripple 正在打一套「多頭戰」：以 RLUSD 卡位穩定幣市佔，同時把穩定幣推往借貸場景，將 RLUSD 的流通需求直接做實。
Ripple 官方的定位是「法幣兌換的美元快速通道」，而與 Clearpool、Cicada 結盟後，RLUSD 從「支付層」跨到「企業營運資金」的資產層。若 XLS-66 投票過關、主網放行，這會是鏈上跑起來的第一個「穩定幣授信」架構。
後續值得留意的兩個訊號：一是 XRPL 社群對 XLS-66、XLS-65 的升級投票結果；二是 RLUSD 能否以「機構信貸」為切口，在穩定幣市場吃到實際貸款需求，對照 Circle 的 USDC 以「持幣生息」主攻散戶，Ripple 這招明顯是想把穩定幣變成「可以放貸的資產」，而不只是「可以持有的資產」。

title: Anthropic 開放內部教育課程「Claude Academy」上線：26 門 AI 課免費看
summary:
Anthropic 於 8 月 20 日推出免費學習平台 Claude Academy，把課程整併擴充至 26 […]

〈Anthropic 開放內部教育課程「Claude Academy」上線：26 門 AI 課免費看〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
Anthropic 於 8 月 20 日推出免費學習平台 Claude Academy，把課程整併擴充至 26 門，涵蓋非工程師的 AI 流利度、開發者 API 與雲端整合三條路線。
（前情提要：Anthropic 出錢讓你學 Claude 還給你工作：媒合到全美非營利組織駐點一年）
（背景補充：Claude Code 邊做邊學：這免費網站用 11 堂課教你上手，免安裝直接練）
Anthropic 官方帳號稍早在 X 宣布，Claude Academy 正式上線。Claude Academy 是 Anthropic 教育版圖的重新命名與擴張，前身「Anthropic Academy」今年 3 月才剛上線，短短 5 個多月，課程數量從 16 門長到 26 門。免費、開放給任何人，沒有訂閱門檻，也不用付費才能拿證書。
這場教育卡位戰，OpenAI 與 Google 早就在打，Anthropic 只是把腳步再往前推了一步。
Claude Academy is now live.
Whether you're figuring out what AI is or already using Claude every day, there's a path that meets you where you are. The courses and tutorials are free and open to anyone at https://t.co/WRiSRAvK6l pic.twitter.com/llx2W0VIIy
— Claude (@claudeai) August 20, 2026
整套課綱分成三條路線
Claude Academy 的定位很直接，教人安全且有效地使用 AI。網域獨立於 academy.claude.com，也能從 Claude 個人檔案選單的「Learn more」進入，內容涵蓋課程、教學與實際應用情境庫，同時涉及 Claude 的專屬用法與通用 AI 概念。
整套課綱分成三條路線：一條給不寫程式的一般用戶，走「AI Fluency（AI 流利度）」；一條給開發者，教 API 與 Claude Code；一條給企業技術族群，教 Amazon Bedrock 與 Google Vertex AI 的雲端整合。
課程樣本能看出深淺分層。「AI Fluency：Framework and Foundations」是最基礎的一門，14 個單元加 1 份測驗，約 4 小時，教怎麼用 4D 框架跟 AI 有效、有效率、合乎倫理又安全地協作。
程度再深一點的「AI Capabilities and Limitations」會談到 next-token prediction，簡單來說就是，模型每次只是在猜下一個字最可能是什麼，這門課還會講模型的工作記憶、可導引性與脈絡長度限制，13 個單元約 3.5 小時，程度中階。
每門課上完都發結業證書，不需要付費訂閱 Claude，完全免費。
誰負責教你？
整套課綱背後的骨架，是 Anthropic 訓練自家員工用的同一套「4D AI Fluency」框架，由 Anthropic 與兩位學者共同開發，一位是 University College Cork 的 Joseph Feller 教授，另一位是 Ringling College of Art and Design 的 Rick Dakan 教授。
選擇把員工內部訓練教材直接對外開放，等於把 Anthropic 認為怎麼用 AI 才安全的標準，攤在陽光下讓所有人檢視，這也是一種話語權的爭奪，誰先定義什麼是好的 AI 使用方式，誰就掌握了教育市場的詮釋權。
平台功能上，用戶能直接跟 Claude 做互動練習，系統依興趣給個人化課程建議，還有進度追蹤與可累積的徽章，另外有一個「Claude Academy Skill」會推薦客製化學習路徑。Anthropic 表示，隨著模型能力提升，未來這套學習體驗會更個人化、更互動。
別人也在教同一批人
教育這條戰線，Anthropic 不是第一個進場的。Google 的 AI Essentials 掛在 Coursera 上，是 Google 目前修課人數最多的 AI 課程，累積約 180 萬名學習者、2 萬 2 千多則評價，平均 4.8 分，但影片旁聽免費，作業評分跟證書要付 49 美元才能拿到。
OpenAI Academy 也提供免費課程，今年 6 月起任何有 ChatGPT 帳號的人都能修三門免費課、拿免費結業證書，不過真正監考的正式認證目前只開放給企業試點客戶。
相較之下，Claude Academy 從頭到尾免費，連證書都不用另外付費，是三家目前教育布局裡最徹底開放的一個。
算力決定格局，模型決定應用，資本決定速度，但決定誰能留在牌桌上更久的，往往是誰先教會下一代怎麼用你的工具，而不是誰的模型跑分最高。

title: 輝達也扛不住？傳已通知代工廠，明年 AI 伺服器大幅調漲逾 15％
summary:
彭博報導指出，輝達近期通知代工客戶，明年出貨的 AI 伺服器價格將調漲逾 15%，起因是記憶體晶片成本飆升，輝 […]

〈輝達也扛不住？傳已通知代工廠，明年 AI 伺服器大幅調漲逾 15％〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
彭博報導指出，輝達近期通知代工客戶，明年出貨的 AI 伺服器價格將調漲逾 15%，起因是記憶體晶片成本飆升，輝達官方未回應置評請求。
（前情提要：輝達再對板卡廠發漲價通知：GDDR6/GDDR7 記憶體變配貨，顯示卡炒價再飆）
（背景補充：Nvidia 供應商 SK 海力士警告「輝達泡沫化」：AI 投資若不賺，產業會一夕崩盤）
全球毛利率高達 75% 的晶片巨頭，如今也扛不住記憶體漲價的壓力？彭博報導引述知情人士說法，輝達近期通知代工客戶，明年初出貨的 AI 伺服器價格將調漲逾 15%，明星產品 Vera Rubin 與 Grace Blackwell 系統全都在漲價名單上。
誰在漲，漲多少
知情人士向彭博透露細節時，因為溝通尚未公開而要求匿名。漲幅會依輝達晶片世代與記憶體配置而異，這次調漲將於明年初出貨的系統上生效，涵蓋旗艦款 Vera Rubin 與 Grace Blackwell。負責幫微軟、Google 與甲骨文等大型資料中心業者代工組裝伺服器的廠商，最近已陸續通知客戶即將漲價。輝達官方對彭博的置評請求並未回應。
這不是輝達第一次調整定價。本月稍早，科技媒體 Tom’s Hardware 報導，輝達已經調漲了面向遊戲玩家的 PC 顯示卡價格，漲幅最高來到 39%。目前頂規 AI 伺服器的單機售價已來到約 300 萬美元，這次企業級系統再漲價，等於又把門檻往上推了一截。
為什麼是記憶體說了算
DRAM，也就是動態隨機存取記憶體。簡單來說就是，輝達的加速晶片再強，沒有足夠的 DRAM 搭配，運算效能也發揮不出來。
三星、SK 海力士與美光三家，幾乎包辦了全球這類晶片的產能，即便近年不斷擴產，仍追不上 AI 基礎設施爆炸式的需求。這讓原本像大宗商品一樣定價的記憶體，價格被推上天際，也讓三家記憶體廠商在科技產業裡取得前所未有的話語權。
HBM，也就是高頻寬記憶體。簡單來說就是，專門為 AI 晶片設計、堆疊多層 DRAM 的高速記憶體，是輝達 GPU 效能的關鍵零件。市場先前已有預期，SK 海力士與輝達敲定的 2026 年 HBM4 供應合約，單價約落在 560 美元，較先前價格高出五成以上；業界估計，HBM4 未來在輝達次世代 GPU 的成本佔比，可能拉高到整體晶片成本的四分之一。
輝達目前的毛利率高達 75%，也就是每賣出 100 元的產品，扣掉生產成本後還剩 75 元。這麼高的毛利率，靠的是晶圓代工龍頭 TSMC 的產能長期供不應求，讓輝達得以對單顆晶片開出動輒數萬美元的價碼。輝達的加速晶片最早脫胎自售價僅數百美元的 PC 遊戲顯示卡，如今卻因為需求持續暴衝、市場上幾乎找不到替代品，價格一路墊高。
誰在真正受傷
蘋果與高通近期都表示，受晶片短缺影響，被迫調漲自家產品售價，顯示這波記憶體漲價的衝擊，早已不只侷限在 AI 伺服器這條產線上。
亞馬遜、微軟、Google 與 Meta 雖然都在推動自研晶片計畫，試圖擺脫對輝達的依賴，但目前資料中心的擴建仍離不開輝達的採購，而自研晶片能走多遠，同樣要看它們能不能從三星、SK 海力士與美光那裡搶到足夠的記憶體供應，說到底，主導權還是握在記憶體廠商手上。
漲價的衝擊還不只反映在採購成本上。市場先前已有預期，伺服器用記憶體晶片價格，有機會在 2026 年底前翻倍；輝達與超微被傳自今年初起分階段調高 GPU 售價，漲勢預期會貫穿全年。而 AI 資料中心原本就面臨工程延宕、人力短缺、資金收緊，以及周邊社群反對開發案等多重挑戰，如今再疊加成本上升，整個產業的擴張藍圖只會更複雜。
下週，輝達即將公布最新一季財報。這家全球市值最高的上市公司，每次財報都牽動整個科技產業與投資人的神經，畢竟外界砸進 AI 基礎設施的錢，賭的就是這場轉型能兌現承諾。這次調漲之後，外界會緊盯的不只是輝達自己的營收數字，更是記憶體供應商能不能持續坐穩談判桌的主導位置。

title: 渣打改口：比特幣年底有望重返12.6萬美元歷史高點，10萬目標恐低估
summary:
渣打銀行數位資產研究全球主管 Geoff Kendrick 在最新報告中指出，隨著現貨比特幣 ETF 資金迴流 […]

〈渣打改口：比特幣年底有望重返12.6萬美元歷史高點，10萬目標恐低估〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
渣打銀行數位資產研究全球主管 Geoff Kendrick 在最新報告中指出，隨著現貨比特幣 ETF 資金迴流，比特幣年底前有機會重返 12.6 萬美元的歷史高點，反彈可能於 10 月 6 日後加速。
（前情提要：渣打銀行喊「比特幣底部已到」！列兩大看漲理由：年底上看 10 萬美元不變）
（背景補充：投行 TD Cowen 最新預測：比特幣 2026 年底上看 14 萬美元！極端牛市可達 17.5 萬鎂）
渣打銀行數位資產研究全球主管 Geoff Kendrick 在最新報告中表示，比特幣年底前有望向 12.6 萬美元的歷史高點靠攏，且反彈可能在 10 月 6 日後加速。他指出，本波行情主要由空單回補（短暫清算）驅動，同時現貨比特幣 ETF 的資金流入也開始回溫，加上目前市場未平倉量偏低，意味著還有空間容納更多投資人在價格上漲後進場。
Kendrick 坦言：「今年第一次出現風險，我的年底預測（10 萬美元）可能太低。」
他在今年 2 月 12 日發布的報告中，曾將 2026 年底的比特幣目標價從 15 萬美元下修至 10 萬美元、以太幣目標價從 7,500 美元降至 4,000 美元；當時他預期比特幣將先回落至 5 萬美元、以太幣跌至 1,400 美元後，再於下半年緩步復甦。如今比特幣已在兩週內自低點反彈逾兩成，其下修的假設正在被市場推翻。
機構觀點大不同，比特幣築底了嗎？
渣打並非唯一為牛市底背書的機構。Swan Bitcoin 執行長 Cory Klippsten 先前即表示比特幣可能會在 10 月觸底；量化研究機構 10x Research 創辦人 Markus Thielen 則指出，若 8 月月線能收在 6.3 萬美元之上，就能確認熊市底部。
如今比特幣已遠超這個門檻，但市場仍對回檔風險保持警戒。
- 渣打 2026 年底新目標：12.5 萬美元
- 比特幣歷史高點：12.6 萬美元
- 10x Research 底部確認線：8 月收盤站上 6.3 萬美元
- 比特幣現價：約 7.7 萬美元
市場影響與後續觀察
此前多家投行在 2 月集體下修年底目標，如今在 ETF 資金迴流、比特幣單週大漲逾兩成的背景下，開始有人率先承認「可能估錯了」。
對投資者而言，值得留意的是此波反彈與現貨 ETF 流入形成的「正迴圈」，價格反彈吸引資金、資金迴流又強化價格，若迴圈延續，機構資金與散戶情緒將同步升溫；反之，若 ETF 流入再次熄火，12.6 萬美元的新高預期就只是紙上富貴。

title: 美國多州封堵 Kalshi、CFTC 逆風力挺：預測市場監管戰開打
summary:
華盛頓州法院裁定 Kalshi 構成非法賭博並下令停業，密西根、內華達使用者同遭封鎖，康乃狄克與紐約訴訟持續； […]

〈美國多州封堵 Kalshi、CFTC 逆風力挺：預測市場監管戰開打〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
華盛頓州法院裁定 Kalshi 構成非法賭博並下令停業，密西根、內華達使用者同遭封鎖，康乃狄克與紐約訴訟持續；同一週 CFTC 主席 Selig 力推預測市場全面監管框架，聯邦與州政府監管權之爭全面升溫。
（前情提要：美國法官擋下亞利桑那州對 Kalshi 的「非法賭博」刑事起訴，川普政府撐腰預測市場）
（背景補充：CME執行長嗆CFTC主席與Kalshi：預測市場易被操縱，現場交鋒成焦點）
華盛頓州使用者本週起無法再使用 Kalshi：當地法院在州政府指控其經營非法賭博業務的訴訟中，下令 Kalshi 停止向該州居民提供多數議題的預測合約。Kalshi 寄給使用者的電子郵件寫道：「華盛頓州政府封鎖了你在 Kalshi 自由交易的權利。」加上先前被封鎖的密西根與內華達使用者，這家美國最大預測市場平台正面臨多州圍堵。
州政府之戰：華盛頓、康乃狄克、紐約輪番對簿公堂
華盛頓州總檢察長 Nick Brown 表示：「Kalshi 靠著推銷體育、選舉、天災乃至與伊朗戰爭相關事件的賭注致富。根據這道命令，Kalshi 在華盛頓州多數此類主題都被禁止提供賭注。」州檢察長辦公室宣告指出，法院認定該平台在當地構成非法賭博。
Kalshi 週四向法院提出重新審議動議，主打「雙重標準」論點：法院下令六天後，州政府表示在上訴有結果前不會對 Crypto.com 執法，而 Crypto.com 提供的是同一套被禁止的商業模式。Kalshi 在動議中指出：「州政府認定 Kalshi 無法容忍的那些事件合約，現在華盛頓州居民卻能在州政府祝福下，從與 Kalshi 處境完全相同的競爭對手處自由取得。」
這場混戰不限於華盛頓：
- 康乃狄克州監管機關本週在聯邦法院與 Kalshi 來回攻防，試圖把賭博法套用於該平台
- 紐約持續質疑 CFTC 近期為保障 Kalshi 當地業務而採取的緊急行動
- 麻薩諸塞、明尼蘇達、俄亥俄、馬里蘭、猶他、亞利桑那均有法律衝突，多數聚焦體育博彩
CFTC 逆風力挺：Selig 推全面監管框架
產業護航者來自聯邦監管機關：CFTC 主席 Mike Selig 將捍衛其對預測市場的「唯一管轄權」列為任期優先事項，並著手製定一系列正式規則。在首屆創新諮詢委員會會議上，Selig 直言監管層過去「把頭埋在沙裡」或試圖直接禁止這類事件合約：「CFTC 從未建立完整的監管框架，來處理這些產品衍生的特殊政策考量。」
目前本應有五位委員的 CFTC 僅剩 Selig 一人，意味著他現階段可在政策決策上單方面行動。他透露，除了近期的規則提案，CFTC 很快會現代化事件合約監管並「建立消費者保護要求」，涵蓋產品治理、市場設計與激勵方案。
TD Cowen 政策分析師 Jaret Seiberg 在客戶報告中指出，CFTC 承諾消費者保護，可能降低參議員把預測市場限制條款夾帶進 9 月農業法案或其他立法的風險。
CME 執行長正面交鋒：「我們不是馬戲團攤販」
Selig 與 Kalshi 營運長 Luana Lopes Lara 在委員會現場與衍生品巨頭 CME Group 執行長 Terry Duffy 針鋒相對。
Duffy 直言預測市場「有很多事情容易受到操縱，這對我們的產業非常糟糕，我們不是馬戲團裡招攬生意的攤販」，凸顯華爾街傳統衍生品業者對這項新興業務的敵意。
聯邦與州政府管轄權之爭，決定預測市場命運
預測市場近來爆紅，吸引立法者注意，也招來傳統金融機構的敵意。此役勝負關鍵在於時間差：CFTC 若能在州禁令擴散之際快速端出消費者保護與事件合約規則，將強化「聯邦專屬管轄」論述，說服國會暫緩出手；反之若各州禁令持續蔓延、聯邦框架遲遲未定，產業將陷入碎片化監管。
Kalshi 的「Crypto.com 雙重標準」論點雖具說服力，最終仍待上訴法院裁定。
對亞洲市場而言，美國這場聯邦與州政府的權力拉鋸是最直接的監管風險教材：單一州法院即可一夜之間推翻平台合法營運基礎，凸顯在「聯邦框架＋州級執法」並存的環境下，合規成本將大幅上升，也預示各國若未先建立全國性框架，同類混戰可能在其他市場重演。

title: Restriction zone scheme for offenders to start in October
summary: Serious violent and sexual offenders may be confined to areas of just a few miles after leaving prison on probation.
full_text:
Restriction zone scheme for offenders to start in October
- Published
A scheme that could see serious sexual and violent offenders confined to areas just a few miles wide after leaving prison will be launched in October, Justice Secretary Alex Norris has announced.
Government ministers say this is designed to give victims greater freedom and further reduce the possibility of unwanted contact
The intention to introduce "restriction zones" for violent offenders who leave prison and who are on probation was first announced by the government last year.
Probation officers will be able to limit where serious offenders can go for as long as it is deemed necessary. Those who breach their new boundaries could be recalled to prison.
This would go beyond the current practice of imposing "exclusion zones" which ban offenders from specific locations such as a victim's home or place of work.
Norris is expected to come up with proposals to further restrict the early release of some prisoners when Parliament resumes next month.
But the Conservatives say that the best thing Labour could do to protect victims is to bring forward emergency legislation which would stop the early release of thousands of criminals.
There is a risk that serious sexual and violent offenders and victims could encounter one another outside exclusion zones.
The new scheme will specify confined areas for offenders in plans tailored to them and developed in consultation with victims.
Norris said the scheme would use GPS technology monitored by probation officers so that "those who step outside the boundaries can be quickly identified and face being sent back to prison".
"Offenders should carry the consequences of their crimes, not their victims," he added.
Amy Glover, director of domestic abuse services at Advance, a charity supporting women and girls who have experienced domestic abuse, praised the "change in focus".
However, she also called for reform to the criminal justice system saying many survivors of abuse chose "not to pursue a criminal conviction, and for those that do only 5% reach conviction."
A domestic abuse survivor named only as Kristina called the restriction zones a "fantastic concept" but noted that a perpetrator had continuously breached her indefinite restraining order "without consequence".
"The biggest challenge would be to gain victims' confidence in authorities to follow through their promises of protection," she added.
The announcement of the restriction zone scheme's start date comes after a change to the government's early release scheme following a backlash.
Introduced to ease prison overcrowding, on 4 August the policy was updated so people sentenced for rape, serious child sex offences and grooming would not be eligible for early release.
The Prison Governors' association warned this change to plans at a "very late stage" put further pressure on prison staff.
The restriction zone scheme was criticised when it was announced last year for potentially putting pressure on probation staff, something the government says it hopes to alleviate with more staff and a greater use of technology.
If you are suffering from domestic abuse, details of help and support in the UK are available at BBC Action Line

title: Cyber attack shut down small power plant
summary: The government says at no point was there a risk to the UK's energy system during the attack in July.
full_text:
Cyber attack shut down small power plant
- Published
A small power plant has been shut down during a cyber attack.
The government said that at no point was there a risk to the UK's energy system, but the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) has contacted power companies to advise them about the risk of cyber attacks.
The Daily Telegraph reported that the attack, which took place last month, was carried out by hackers affiliated to the Iranian regime.
For security reasons, neither the government nor the National Cyber Security Centre, which deals with attacks on critical infrastructure, would give further details of the site affected. However this was not an attack on an essential service such as a large power station.
According to the Telegraph, external, the power plant was shut down for four days.
DESNZ said the incident had affected a small-scale generator and at no point had there been a risk to the wider energy system.
The UK's power network has a number of smaller gas generators which provide short-term power when needed.
Protecting the country's supplies is key challenge for the government. It is updating its regulations for cyber security, and working on a new energy resilience strategy for later this year.
Iran has long been regarded as a capable cyber power but while the Western cyber-security world is braced for attacks either from the state or hackers linked to the state as a result of its conflict with the US this year, there has been little activity so far.

title: Swedish sword attack victim was 17-year-old girl, police say
summary: Two boys aged 12 and 17 were also injured in the attack, while an 18-year-old suspect has been detained.
full_text:
Swedish sword attack victim was 17-year-old girl, police say
- Published
The victim of a deadly sword attack at a high school in central Sweden was a 17-year-old girl, police have confirmed.
Two boys aged 12 and 17 were also seriously injured in the attack at Brinell School in Fagersta on Friday afternoon, according to local authorities, while a third person sustained minor injuries.
An 18-year-old man, who has not been named, was arrested and police said they were treating the case as murder and attempted murder.
Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson and opposition leader Magdalena Andersson visited the school, where flower tributes have been laid to honour the victims, on Saturday morning.
Students at the school had only just returned to the classroom following the summer break when the deadly attack unfolded on Friday afternoon.
The police later confirmed they fired shots after being called to the scene but did not say whether the alleged attacker was hit before he was detained.
Sweden's public broadcaster reported that the suspect was wearing a helmet. Local media also said he was a former student.
The region went into a state of emergency on Friday, but it had ended by Saturday.
The school has just under 500 students on its roster, according to SVT, and is located 170km (105 miles) north-west of the capital, Stockholm.
Investigators have already carried out two house searches in connection with the suspect, police said.
On Friday, Sweden's Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson described the attack as a "serious incident," and said "we do not know what lies behind the act, but we know that police are working very intensively", in a post on X.
Sweden's King Carl XVI Gustaf said he received the news "with dismay and sadness".

title: Canada to hit US with retaliatory tariffs as trade war escalates
summary: Mark Carney says Canada will impose tariffs starting September 8 on imports of US steel, electronics and other products.
full_text:
Canada to hit US with retaliatory tariffs as trade war escalates
Mark Carney says Canada will impose tariffs starting September 8 on imports of US steel, electronics and other products.
Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney has announced retaliatory tariffs on the United States after Washington imposed a 50 percent levy on $20bn worth of Canadian goods.
Carney, speaking in Ottawa on Saturday, said the new Canadian tariffs would target US steel, dairy and electronics industries among others and take effect on September 8.
Recommended Stories

- list 2 of 3US imposes 50 percent tariffs on $20bn in Canadian goods after talks fail
- list 3 of 3Europe, Canada condemn Israeli plans for new West Bank settlement
“Canada will match Washington’s new tariffs dollar for dollar in order to protect Canadian workers, farmers, families, and businesses,” Carney told reporters.
The announcement came after days of intense negotiations broke down late on Friday, worsening a delicate relationship between the longtime trade partners and allies.
US President Donald Trump’s new tariffs hit sectors including wine, furniture, dairy products, cement, clothing, fishing rods and hockey equipment, and cover some $20bn worth of goods, or 5.5 percent of Canadian exports to the US.
Carney said Trump set conditions that were ultimately unacceptable even though earlier talks had been positive.
“In recent days, the United States proposed new terms that were uneconomic, unfair and undermined the net benefits for Canada, and called into question the reliability of any deal,” Carney said, adding these demands included curtailing Canada’s ability to forge new trade deals.
“We cannot accept what they’ve offered, and we will not give what they’ve asked.”
He added that US negotiators also made unacceptable “threats” to the French language and “Quebec culture”, referring to the French-speaking province in eastern Canada.
No new talks planned
Carney is one of the few global leaders to retaliate against US tariffs and has pledged to forge new trade and military alliances, despite Canada’s dependence on the US for nearly 70 percent of its exports.
Canada will impose tariffs on US steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics, along with some products the US previously targeted in Canada, Carney said from Ottawa’s Parliament building. The government will release details on its response in the coming days, he said.
Carney said Canada would announce support measures next week for industries hit by the new US duties, adding these measures could last years.
There was no immediate comment from the White House.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told Fox News on Saturday that no new talks are planned with Canada.
“We’re moving forward with measures that respond to Canadian retaliation,” Greer said. “They’ve always had the best deal, and they still would have an even better deal, but they didn’t want that.”
The new US tariffs are expected to have a major impact on Canada’s economy.
“Costs are going to go up, prices are going to go up, unemployment is going to go up as well,” said Al Jazeera’s David Mercer, reporting from the Canadian city of Calgary. “And it’s been warned that business owners – small [and] medium-sized businesses – some of those will have to declare bankruptcy,” he said.
At the same time, Mercer said, Carney is selling the trade war as an opportunity for Canada to strengthen its trade relations with other countries.
“He’s been around the world, he’s been talking to countries in Asia, in Europe, shoring up new trade relationships, wanting to diversify Canada’s economy and Canada’s trade relationships with other countries around the world just to get away from that dependency that Canada has traditionally had on the United States,” he said.
Public opinion surveys in Canada show most Canadians back a “tougher approach” to the US in the trade talks. A poll by Leger last week said 56 percent of Canadians favoured a hard line and making no more concessions.
‘Bad deal’
Ontario Premier Doug Ford, one of the most vocal opponents of US tariffs, supported Carney’s decision to retaliate.
“I’m glad he didn’t sign that deal because it was a bad deal. It was a bad deal for Ontario. It was a bad deal for the auto sector, the steel sector, and manufacturing sector,” Ford told reporters on Saturday.
In Port Colborne, Ontario, resident Stuart Edwards said the trade war was going to “hurt everybody” and “it’s just sad”.
“We have a bully in Washington, and he’s just hitting us all with the big stick all the time,” he said. “And we’re not going to put up with it; Canada isn’t. We’ll fight back.”
But Pamela Coulis, from Fort Erie in Canada, was worried about rising prices.
“I think probably the gas will go up even more, and all products, from food to, I don’t know, wood, everything else,” she said.
Diamond Isinger, who served as a special adviser to former Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, said both countries will suffer from the trade war.
“It’s going to cause pain and challenge for Canadians and Americans alike, in terms of the actions that, unfortunately, the US has taken as well as Canada’s retaliation. But ultimately this was the way forward; this was the only realistic next step,” she said.
“Because the US administration responds best, of all the responses that they could have, to all the actions that a government like Canada could take, to strength,” Isinger added.
“So, we could not simply accept 50 percent tariffs going forward. We had to move forward with our own retaliatory package.”
In the US, the escalating trade war was met with anger by Democratic lawmakers and governors from border states including Minnesota, New York and Washington, who blamed Trump for triggering chaos that would raise costs for US businesses and families.
“Needlessly picking fights with our allies and raising prices here at home. That’s Trump’s economic policy in a nutshell,” New York Governor Kathy Hochul posted on X.
The Business Roundtable, a group of 200 chief executives of leading US corporations, also warned the new tariffs “risk raising costs for American businesses and families”, and urged both governments to resume negotiations.

title: China builds world’s first custom plant immunity system for epidemic response
summary:
Chinese scientists have created an AI-guided platform to engineer custom plant immune receptors to rapidly combat emerging diseases that threaten plants, including commercial crops vulnerable to devastating outbreaks.
Their programmable synthetic immune receptors can be introduced into plants to help them detect proteins made by specific bacteria, viruses and fungi, triggering an immune response to neutralise the threat, according to the team.
By leveraging protein design guided by artificial...
full_text:
China builds world’s first custom plant immunity system for epidemic response
Tailored biological tools could enable crops to quickly develop immunity against emerging viruses, bacteria and fungi, researchers say
Their programmable synthetic immune receptors can be introduced into plants to help them detect proteins made by specific bacteria, viruses and fungi, triggering an immune response to neutralise the threat, according to the team.
“This work establishes a versatile platform for efficient plant immunity engineering,” the team from the Chinese Academy of Sciences’ Institute of Genetics and Developmental Biology and biotechnology company Qi Biodesign said in a paper published in the peer-reviewed journal Science last month.
Around the world, essential crops are threatened by plant pathogens that can devastate agricultural yields and compromise global food security.
Plant breeding programmes often introduce resistance genes that encode receptors capable of recognising proteins secreted by pathogens. When these receptors bind to their protein target, it can trigger an immune response.
“However, this resistance is often rapidly overcome by fast-evolving pathogens, particularly in modern agricultural systems characterised by large-scale monoculture of genetically uniform crops,” the team said.
This biological vulnerability is what heightens the threat of agro-terrorism and plant bioweapons, or pathogens purposefully introduced or modified to target specific crops.

title: Sydney Marathon admits ‘unfortunate error’ as finisher’s medal depicts Munich stadium as race highlight
summary:
‘Landmarks’ side of the medal features the Allianz Arena in German city rather than Allianz Stadium in Sydney

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

In a week’s time, the proud runners finishing the Sydney Marathon will receive a medal showing the landmarks they have just sped past – plus one they definitely didn’t.

In what organisers have admitted was an “unfortunate error”, a stadium in Munich, Germany, was erroneously etched on to the event’s participation medal instead of a local Sydney landmark.

Continue reading...
full_text:
In a week’s time, the proud runners finishing the Sydney Marathon will receive a medal showing the landmarks they have just sped past – plus one they definitely didn’t.
In what organisers have admitted was an “unfortunate error”, a stadium in Munich, Germany, was erroneously etched on to the event’s participation medal instead of a local Sydney landmark.
In an Instagram post on the official Sydney Marathon account earlier this week, revealing the design of the participation medal, runners were told they would “find the story of the course in the details” of the design.
“A beautiful Sydney skyline brings the course to life, featuring the landmarks runners will experience along the way,” the post reads, “starting with the Sydney Harbour Bridge and finishing at the world-famous Sydney Opera House”.
However, one of the “landmarks” on the medal is the Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany, rather than Allianz Stadium in Sydney (which the marathon route passes).
“A little too much international flavour has found its way onto the back of the finisher’s medal, with an incorrect depiction of the stadium,” a TCS Sydney Marathon spokesperson said on Sunday.
“We’re not going to run from it, it was an unfortunate error, though it’s certainly given everyone something to talk about this weekend, mostly in good humour.”
The error was reported by the BBC and noted with amusement by several running blogs. The Munich stadium, which opened in 2005 and is home to the Bayern Munich football team, responded in the comments of one: “Oh wow, we didn’t have that on our bingo card!”
The reverse of the medal features an indigo and gold design by First Nations artist Ambrose Killian, representing kilometres of the course, and the eight global major marathons. Killian told the BBC he was not involved in the other side of the design.
The marathon will take place on 30 August. In 2025, about 35,000 marathoners from more than 120 countries participated in the event – its first year as a World Marathon major event.
Sydney Marathon organisers said it was “a beautiful medal, and now a little more unique”.
“What it represents does not change,” the spokesperson said. “Behind every one of these medals is months of early mornings, long runs and quiet determination, and having it placed around your neck at the Sydney Opera House is a moment our participants will never forget.
“We’re grateful to our participants and partners for taking it in such good humour, and our focus now is where it should be, on delivering a safe, spectacular and unforgettable weekend [event].”
It’s not the first time official medals have run into problems. In 2012, some of the 23,000 runners in the Edinburgh marathon remarked on the rather phallic profile of their finisher’s award.
Earlier this year, the Winter Olympics were plagued by reports of cracking and snapping medals. And in Paris in 2024 the bronze medals were replaced after they quickly discoloured.

title: 好魔幻》全球最大盜版書庫 Anna’s Archive 號召掃描書籍，控 AI 碎書是反人類罪行
summary:
很諷刺的情況是，全球最大盜版書褲 Anna’s Archive 號召全球志工搶救紙本書，控訴 AI […]

〈好魔幻》全球最大盜版書庫 Anna’s Archive 號召掃描書籍，控 AI 碎書是反人類罪行〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
很諷刺的情況是，全球最大盜版書褲 Anna’s Archive 號召全球志工搶救紙本書，控訴 AI 公司買書掃完就銷毀。
（前情提要：Anthropic 掃描 200 萬本書籍訓練 Claude 後，直接送入碎紙機銷毀）
（背景補充：Anthropic 以史上最高 15 億美元和解著作權訴訟：但作者與出版社不覺得贏了）
全球最大的影子圖書館 Anna’s Archive，在 8 月初於官方部落格貼出一篇署名志工「u」的投稿，標題直白：AI 公司正在銷毀實體書，讓我們搶在它們掃完之前，把書救出來。該文聲稱，多家 AI 公司透過中間商大量收購二手書，掃描之後直接銷毀，目的是取得 2022 年以前「未被機器汙染過」的訓練資料。
文中點名的主角，是 Anthropic 的「Project Panama」計畫。Anna’s Archive 主張，這項計畫是在一樁 15 億美元的著作權和解案中被揭露，2024 年初啟動，砸下數千萬美元買下數百萬本紙本書，掃描後用來訓練 Claude，再把原書全數銷毀。原文對此下的評語很重：法律上可行，但道德上是極其嚴重的反人類罪行。
據了解，「Project Panama」計畫是由一位曾任職 Google 的前員工 Tom Turvey 主導，目標是建立一座收錄全世界所有書籍的中央書庫並永久儲存，再從中挑選版本乾淨的書用來訓練大型語言模型。
實際操作上，工作人員會先把書脊裁掉，讓書頁能高速連續進紙掃描，這是業界處理大量紙本掃描時常見的做法，只是也代表原書在流程結束後基本上無法復原。
銷毀，是為了壟斷
該文列出三個銷毀理由：防止競爭對手拿同一批書去掃描訓練、規避法律風險、以及銷毀本身比無損掃描更便宜。
邏輯推到底，掃描完成之後，全世界只剩 AI 公司自己手上握有數位副本，人類知識被永久鎖進企業私有伺服器。該文還點出一個悖論：AI 公司口口聲聲說要讓人類知識「可被取用」，動作上卻在拆解人類知識最堅實的載體，也就是紙本書本身。
面對這個局面，Anna’s Archive 開出的解方是全球志工總動員，號召大家把圖書館與檔案館裡的書籍、期刊、報紙、古籍與珍本掃描上傳，它開出了會員資格與費用補貼作為誘因，理由很簡單：如果每個人掃一本書，全球有 1,000 萬名志工，就能得到 1,000 萬份無價的財富。
該文還丟出一個更聳動的說法：自 2025 年初以來，AI 生成內容已佔新增網路內容的一半以上，儘管這句話沒有附上任何可查核的資料來源。但若順著這個邏輯，一旦 AI 吸收完人類寫在紙上的最後一句話，網路上剩下的，恐怕就只是 AI 自己說給自己聽的話。
不過把這場行動單純簡單讀成「正義志工對抗邪惡巨頭」，也忽略了兩個關鍵事實。
法院早就判過了
在 Bartz v. Anthropic 一案中，聯邦法官 William Alsup 認定，合法買進紙本書、裁切掃描成數位檔、再銷毀原件，屬於著作權法上的合理使用。
而那筆讓外界譁然的 15 億美元和解，賠的其實是另一批盜版書籍：約 500 萬本來自 LibGen，約 200 萬本來自 Pirate Library Mirror，跟買來裁切掃描的紙本書完全無關。最大的反諷藏在這裡：Pirate Library Mirror，正是 Anna’s Archive 自己的前身。
2022 年 9 月，這個計畫完成了 Z-Library 的整站複製；同年 11 月，美國執法單位查封 Z-Library 網域、逮捕經營者，數天後，其中一名成員 Anna 就創立了 Anna’s Archive。換句話說，Anthropic 之所以要付出 15 億美元，正是因為它拿了影子圖書館體系流出的書。這場看似對立的戰爭，兩造的資料其實同源。
批評者也對「銷毀等於毀滅文化」的說法提出反駁：被銷毀的書多半是出版商與通路賣不掉的庫存與二手書，本來就要進回收廠，不是什麼孤本珍本。但要額外補充的是：非破壞性掃描技術確實存在，只是速度較慢、成本更高。

title: 用軍隊能救債市？川普一句話讓交易員滿頭問號，殖利率叩關 5.3%
summary:
川普 21 日放話「終極干預就是我們的軍隊」，可是白宮至今說不清這句話什麼意思；同一週財政部才砸 40 億美元 […]

〈用軍隊能救債市？川普一句話讓交易員滿頭問號，殖利率叩關 5.3%〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
川普 21 日放話「終極干預就是我們的軍隊」，可是白宮至今說不清這句話什麼意思；同一週財政部才砸 40 億美元回購救債市，殖利率一度從 19 年新高回落，但很快又彈了回去。
（前情提要：救債市只撐一天！美長債殖利率彈回 5.2%、美股收黑，比特幣逆勢叩關 7.5 萬美元）
（背景補充：美財政部長債回購翻倍等於變相 QE？關鍵差在錢從哪來，三個差異一次看懂）
川普 21 日在登上空軍一號前，於停機坪回答記者提問。記者先問，是否曾指示財政部長貝森特（Scott Bessent）干預公債市場；川普否認「不，完全沒有」，稱貝森特非常有能力、非常擅長這件事。
記者追問：「可是殖利率之後又回升了，是否曾與他討論過另一種干預方式？」
川普先賣關子稱：「我們有很多種干預方式。」接著丟出一句讓交易員集體愣住的話：「最終極的干預就是我們的軍隊，如果我們必須使用這手段，我們就會用。」
回購無效，殖利率跌幅全吐回
財政部 19 日率先出手，宣布 9 月起長天期公債單次回購「至少增加一倍」到 40 億美元，讓華爾街意外；30 年期殖利率應聲從 19 年新高 5.34%（2007 年海嘯前夕以來最高）滑落到 5.18%。隔天貝森特接受 CNBC 專訪，宣稱手握一個「大工具箱」，卻拒絕透露箱子裡裝了什麼。
只是這波跌勢連一天都沒撐住，殖利率很快彈回 5.2% 以上，把跌幅幾乎吐回。記者追問川普還有沒有別招，結果逼出前面那句「軍隊說」。
軍隊要怎麼買債？工具箱最後一格是航空母艦嗎
軍隊到底要怎麼干預債市？把公債押上運輸機空投談判桌？還是派航艦戰鬥群開去證交所門口示威？白宮沒解釋，川普本人也沒進一步說明，「軍隊」兩字就這樣任由所有人腦補；被媒體要求釐清含意的白宮，至今也沒有正式回應。
笑歸笑，殖利率飆破 19 年高點是真的
不過調侃歸調侃，40 億美元回購相對美國逾 40 兆美元公債總額，杯水車薪，因而殖利率才會一天內就吐光跌幅。殖利率是風險資產的定價錨，如果沒能成功回若，甚至進一步走高，對股票、比特幣等風險市場來說，那可能不是好消息。
橋水創辦人 Ray Dalio 甚至在 22 日示警，美國只剩「三年時間」走向債務危機，建議拋售美債、轉向黃金與比特幣避險。

title: 特斯拉 9/3 揭曉無方向盤自駕車 Cybercab，馬斯克喊 3 萬美元內賣給你
summary:
特斯拉敲定 Cybercab 無人自駕車的公開登場時間，準備在奧斯汀對外展示這款外型特殊的自駕新車。預計先跑 […]

〈特斯拉 9/3 揭曉無方向盤自駕車 Cybercab，馬斯克喊 3 萬美元內賣給你〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
特斯拉敲定 Cybercab 無人自駕車的公開登場時間，準備在奧斯汀對外展示這款外型特殊的自駕新車。預計先跑 Robotaxi 車隊，最快 2027 年開賣給一般消費者。
（前情提要：特斯拉「沒方向盤」新車 Cybercab曝光！馬斯克：Robotaxi 駕駛成本小於人類十倍）
（背景補充：Waymo 自駕車反覆衝進淹水路段，Robotaxi 擴大停運至四城）
特斯拉（Tesla）近日在社群媒體發布預告，宣布 9 月 3 日將在總部所在地美國德州奧斯汀（Austin）舉行 Cybercab 無人計程車「獨家體驗」活動，讓這款無方向盤、無踏板的金色兩人座車型正式亮相，加入 Uber、Waymo 等業者的無人載客戰場。
— Tesla (@Tesla) August 22, 2026
抽獎搶名額，員工先上路試乘
特斯拉官網同步開放抽獎活動，一般民眾即使沒有搭過 Robotaxi，也有機會抽中入場資格，親臨奧斯汀現場觀看 Cybercab 發表。特斯拉並已開始寄發活動邀請函，準備迎接這場外界期待已久的公開亮相。
美國科技媒體 The Information 本週報導，特斯拉員工已接獲通知，Cybercab 將先在公共道路上讓員工試乘，之後才會正式併入奧斯汀的 Robotaxi 無人計程車車隊。近幾週，也有特斯拉車主在停車場拍到大量 Cybercab 新車待命，讓「即將登場」的傳聞不脛而走。
特斯拉表示，Cybercab 已於 2026 年在德州 Gigafactory 開始生產，這場 9 月 3 日的活動預期將標誌 Cybercab 正式併入 Robotaxi 車隊，目前該車隊主力仍是 Model Y 休旅車。
回顧規格，這款最初於 2024 年 10 月亮相的金色車輛可搭載兩名乘客，是特斯拉首款無方向盤、無踏板的量產車型。馬斯克當時表示，公司計劃於 2027 年前開始生產，售價不會超過 3 萬美元（約合新臺幣 96 萬元），並提供給一般消費者購買。
車隊規模現實
但發表會的聲勢，掩蓋不了車隊規模的懸殊差距。根據德州監理機關的申報資料，特斯拉目前在德州獲準提供無人載客服務的自駕車僅 42 輛，不到 Waymo 在德州 577 輛的十分之一。放大到全美範圍，Waymo 的商用車隊已逼近 4,000 輛，服務範圍涵蓋 11 座城市；特斯拉的無人載客版圖，眼下仍侷限在德州與加州的少數路段。
更關鍵的是，特斯拉真正做到「車上無安全監督員」運作的車輛數量，遠比對外聲勢低調。追蹤數據顯示，2026 年 5 月底至 6 月初，奧斯汀無監督員上路的車輛約 20 輛，加上達拉斯、休士頓，三城合計僅約 32 輛。特斯拉自 2026 年 1 月 22 日起在奧斯汀啟動無監督員營運，起初只有 1 輛車上路；到 6 月，無監督員車輛才緩步增加到約 30 輛，且早期階段仍安排安全監督員坐在前座副駕，另有護衛車隨行。
馬斯克曾表示，特斯拉正在等待 FSD v15 軟體重寫完成才會大規模擴張車隊，這意味著車隊實質放量恐怕要延後到 2026 年底、甚至 2027 年初。此外，根據各州法律規定，許多自駕車輛目前仍需配備隨時可接管的人工監督員或駕駛，不是掛上「無人」招牌就能立刻上路。

title: 幣安兩員工在阿聯機場遭攔查後獲釋，官方回應：例行詢問第三方金流
summary:
兩名幣安員工在阿聯機場遭警方攔查、配合說明第三方金流往來後已獲釋。官方強調員工並非調查物件，僅屬例行詢問，並稱 […]

〈幣安兩員工在阿聯機場遭攔查後獲釋，官方回應：例行詢問第三方金流〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
兩名幣安員工在阿聯機場遭警方攔查、配合說明第三方金流往來後已獲釋。官方強調員工並非調查物件，僅屬例行詢問，並稱正與杜拜警方等阿聯當局建立協調程式。
（前情提要：幣安再陷合規危機！Fortune：員工指證伊朗10億美元違規金流，卻遭Binance集體開除）
（背景補充：幣安執行長Richard Teng怒控《華爾街日報》誹謗！伊朗違規金流、解僱員工全屬不實描述）
幣安兩名員工日前在阿拉伯聯合大公國機場遭警方攔查，在配合說明第三方金流往來後已獲釋。幣安發言人表示，兩人是被「例行詢問」帶去說明，並非調查或指控的物件。
阿聯機場攔查：第三方金流成調查焦點
本起事件的起點是《紐約時報》週四的報導：兩名幣安員工在阿聯機場被攔下、遭到拘留，原因與幣安可能涉及金融犯罪的警方調查有關。交易所官方闢謠這是例行程式，員工接受的是一場針對「透過公司客戶帳戶的第三方金流」所作的說明。
- 涉事員工：幣安位於阿聯的兩名員工
- 攔查地點：阿聯機場
- 調查焦點：公司客戶帳戶中的第三方資金流動
- 結果：說明後已獲釋，未被列為調查目標
幣安發言人強調，「加密貨幣與機構客戶資金帳戶的運作機制在許多司法管轄區仍是新興概念」。官方正與杜拜警方及其他阿聯當局合作，建立清晰、適合的協調程式。
官方定調：例行詢問，員工非目標
「我們正與杜拜警方及阿聯其他地區當局建立清晰、恰當的協調程式。」幣安發言人在回應中重申，相關員工「不是被調查的目標或主體」，只是配合說明一筆公司客戶帳戶內的第三方金流。官方用「例行詢問」定調此事，試圖淡化外界對幣安在阿聯合規狀況的疑慮。
後續觀察
短期指標在三件事：其一，阿聯當局是否會對幣安的機構客戶帳戶金流展開更深入的調查；其二，杜拜作為幣安重要營運據點，合規協調程式的建立是否會牽動其當地業務；其三，這起事件是否與先前幣安內部關於第三方金流的爭議存在關聯。
對全球加密交易所而言，阿聯的例子顯示：即使司法管轄區對加密採相對友善的監管態度，涉及金融犯罪的例行盤查仍可能隨時落在員工身上。幣安的應對方式，強調例行性、淡化個案，後續的解監管發展，仍有待觀察。

title: Mayors to get powers to overrule local councils on planning decisions
summary: Housing minister Matthew Pennycook said the change was "essential" for helping mayors "effectively deliver new homes".
full_text:
Mayors to get powers to overrule local councils on planning decisions
- Published
Mayors across England will be given new powers to overrule local councils on some planning decisions.
The change would apply to proposals with more than 150 homes, more than 15,000 square metres of commercial space or buildings over 30 metres.
Mayors in 13 areas including Manchester, Liverpool, the West of England and the West Midlands will gain similar powers to Sir Sadiq Khan in London, who is already able to "call in" planning decisions.
Housing minister Matthew Pennycook said the powers were an "essential part of the toolkit that mayors need to effectively deliver new homes and regeneration".
The Conservatives questioned whether it was right for councils to lose the "ability to make planning decisions in their own communities".
The powers will also be available to mayors in the Combined Authorities in North East England, South Yorkshire, West Yorkshire, York and North Yorkshire, Hull and East Yorkshire, Greater Lincolnshire, Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, East Midlands, and Tees Valley.
Housebuilding has fallen in London in recent years, but Pennycook insisted the "call in" powers had helped the mayor "unblock strategic growth sites" in the capital.
In the 2024 general election, the Labour government promised to build 1.5 million homes in England by the end of the decade but housebuilders have warned the target could be missed.
Pennycook said the government was "absolutely determined to stick with that ambition".
He acknowledged the target was "really stretching" but said nearly 180,000 children were in temporary accommodation and "any smaller target wouldn't be commensurate with the scale of the challenge".
In addition to gaining the new "call-in" powers, mayors are set to be able to grant "up-front permission", which the government says will allow building to begin "without a developer having to apply".
A consultation on how the powers will work is due to be published next week.
The government has sought to stress that local councils will continue to decide the majority of applications and that all decisions must still follow planning rules.
It has also said mayors will get a "bigger say" over how housing funding is spent in their area, with the government directing national agency Homes England to focus on local mayors' priorities.
New Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who served as mayor for Greater Manchester for nearly a decade, has repeatedly expressed his desire to transfer more powers to local mayors.
"Challenge does need to be made to local decision-making and actually it cuts both ways," he told the Sunday Times.
"Sometimes it's the other way round. It's the local authority putting forward something that's unacceptable in terms of the impact on the community. It's a two-way street."
Last month, Burnham promised to give all mayors a share of income tax revenue, saying he wanted to "bring power home" to "every postcode".
Earlier this week, he announced a secondment programme to send high-performing civil servants to work in mayoral offices.
The approach has faced criticism from some in his own party and the Liberal Democrats, who fear it could create a "two-tier system" that discriminates against those areas that do not have an elected mayor.
- Affordable housing quota for London falls to 20% 
  - Published23 October 2025
Responding to the new powers for mayors, Sir James Cleverly, the shadow housing secretary, said the government was "simultaneously stripping councils across the country of their ability to make planning decisions in their own communities, while making it easier to build traveller sites against local wishes".
Sir James also suggested Labour mayors had failed to meet housing targets, adding: "The Conservatives are the only party with a plan to get Britain building and moving again with our plan to scrap stamp duty on the family home."
Gideon Amos, the Liberal Democrat housing and planning spokesperson, said "taking powers away from communities and local councillors is taking powers away from local people".
"Instead of silencing residents and handing mayors a blank cheque, the government should be empowering local councils with the resources to deliver genuinely affordable homes alongside the infrastructure to support them," he added.
Mothin Ali, deputy leader of the Greens, said "more powers for mayors to direct local councils" was "more tinkering from the Labour government when local authorities continue to be forced by government into austerity budgets".
Reform UK accused Labour of "centralisation in disguise", saying: "Westminster is stretching its tentacles outward instead of giving real power, resources and decision-making capabilities to devolved authorities."
