title: In rural Chad, solar kiosks bring healthcare closer
summary: Solar-powered telemedicine is helping rural Chadians overcome distance and limited access to doctors.
full_text:
In rural Chad, solar kiosks bring healthcare closer
Solar-powered telemedicine is helping rural Chadians overcome distance and limited access to doctors.
Bitkine, Chad – For Ache Kodo, seeing a doctor once meant saving money for the journey.
Living in Bitkine, in central Chad, she said a medical visit could mean paying for transport, the consultation and other costs of travelling to a larger town.
Now, she can consult a doctor remotely through a Telemedan kiosk closer to home.
“Telemedan changed how my family accessed healthcare services,” Ache told Al Jazeera. “It was difficult before, as it involved me saving money to travel just to see a doctor. Now I’m able to do it on time with fewer costs from where I am. It has also enhanced my economic status.”
For people in rural Chad, distance can be as much of a barrier to healthcare as the shortage of doctors themselves. Medical facilities and specialists are concentrated in larger towns and cities, leaving many communities far from basic services.
Abakar Mahamat grew up with that reality.
“The problem wasn’t only the lack of doctors,” he said. “It was also the distance between those doctors and the communities that needed them.”
In 2021, he launched Telemedan, a telemedicine initiative designed to bring consultations closer to communities where electricity, internet access and medical infrastructure are limited.
“Instead of asking people to travel hundreds of kilometres to find a doctor, I wanted to use technology to bring the doctor closer to them,” Abakar told Al Jazeera.
A clinic powered by the sun
The kiosks run on solar panels and batteries, allowing them to operate without reliable grid electricity.
A local operator registers the patient and takes basic measurements using equipment including blood-pressure monitors, glucometers, thermometers, pulse oximeters and electrocardiogram (ECG) machines.
The doctor joins remotely, appearing on a screen as the operator assists with the examination.
Telemedan says its kiosks can also be equipped with diagnostic tools including stethoscopes, temperature sensors and, in some cases, ultrasound equipment. A trained local operator helps patients use them.
The system is designed for places where internet access may be unreliable. Patient information can be stored locally and synchronised when connectivity returns. An Unstructured Supplementary Service Data (USSD) service allows people without internet access to book appointments and access health information.
Depending on the location, the kiosks can connect through mobile networks or satellite links.
“We want to see that the absence of reliable electricity or the internet should not mean the absence of healthcare,” Abakar said.
The cost of getting to a doctor
Abakar said some journeys for medical care can cost $200 or more once transport, accommodation, logistics and medical consultations are included.
Telemedan consultations cost between $2 and $15, depending on the service.
For Abakar, the issue is also about what families can afford to give up to obtain care.
“A patient should not have to choose between seeking medical care and being able to feed their family,” he said.
From pilot to wider network
Telemedan began as a pilot and has expanded with support from grants and institutional partnerships, including Chad’s Ministry of Public Health and Prevention.
Abakar said the initiative now has 37 kiosks across 11 provinces and has reached an estimated 143,000 people.
Telemedan has also begun using artificial intelligence to help screen for diabetic retinopathy, a complication of diabetes that can damage vision. The initiative says the technology is intended to assist healthcare professionals rather than replace them.
But a remote consultation has limits.
A kiosk cannot provide emergency treatment or perform every examination. Patients who need specialist care, laboratory tests, medicines or hospital treatment still have to reach the next level of the health system.
Can the kiosks last?
Telemedan’s expansion comes as Chad develops its wider digital health system.
Youssouf Silay, an assistant to the coordinator of Chad’s National Digital Health Programme, told Al Jazeera that the country’s National Health Development Plan for 2022–2030 identifies digital health as a way to expand access to care.
Chad established the National Telemedicine Programme in 2021 and launched its National Digital Health Programme in 2023, Youssouf said. The Ministry of Health is also developing a legal and regulatory framework for digital health services.
“The objective is to promote innovative solutions that can improve access to healthcare, particularly in areas with limited medical and energy infrastructure,” Youssouf told Al Jazeera. “Solutions such as solar-powered telemedicine kiosks can contribute to this effort by bringing healthcare services closer to underserved populations.”
But putting a kiosk in a village is only the beginning.
The equipment has to keep working. Connectivity has to be available. Local operators need training. Doctors need to be there when patients call. And people who need care beyond the kiosk need a way to reach it.
Each kiosk costs about $10,000, according to Abakar. Telemedan sells the units to governments, public health programmes and partner organisations, which then operate them. The model means patients are not paying for the infrastructure itself.
Telemedan says it wants to reach one million people in rural communities across sub-Saharan Africa.
A solar-powered kiosk cannot replace a hospital. It cannot replace a doctor in every circumstance.
But it can shorten the distance between a patient and the health system.
“We want Telemedan to become a sustainable layer of healthcare infrastructure, not simply a collection of technology projects,” Abakar told Al Jazeera.

The note of caution comes as Beijing steps up efforts to counter “historical nihilism” – the official term for narratives that contradict or undermine the state’s official historical line – as well as pseudo-history, such as claims that Ancient Greece did not exist.
“History education in...
full_text:
Gaokao reforms could leave Chinese public vulnerable to pseudo-history, top academic warns
University dean’s cautionary words come as Beijing is increasingly on guard about historical views at odds with the official line
China’s secondary school students are dropping history as an exam subject, a trend that could leave the public more vulnerable to distorted narratives in the future, an academic at a top university has warned.
“History education in secondary schools is an important means of preserving historical, cultural, ethnic and national identity,” said Liu Linhai, dean of the school of history at Beijing Normal University, in a commentary in the state-backed China Teacher Paper.
“Its current weakening and even marginalisation should be a matter of urgent concern for policymakers, who should take coordinated and effective measures to address the structural problems affecting the subject,” Liu wrote.
Authorities in China have become increasingly alert to challenges to the orthodox view of the country’s history.
On Thursday, a newspaper published by the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences ran two front-page pieces framing pseudo-history as a “new variant” of historical nihilism.

title: Liberal plan to split Victorian appeals court attacked as ‘thought bubble’ that would politicise judiciary
summary:
Opposition leader Jess Wilson says new dedicated court of criminal appeal would set precedents for tougher sentences

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A radical overhaul of Victoria’s highest court, proposed by the Liberal party to increase sentences, has been criticised by legal and human rights groups who warn it would politicise the judiciary.

The opposition leader, Jess Wilson, on Sunday announced that if elected in November the Coalition would split the court of appeal in two, creating a dedicated court of criminal appeal alongside a separate court of civil appeal.

Continue reading...
full_text:
A radical overhaul of Victoria’s highest court, proposed by the Liberal party to increase sentences, has been criticised by legal and human rights groups who warn it would politicise the judiciary.
The opposition leader, Jess Wilson, on Sunday announced that if elected in November the Coalition would split the court of appeal in two, creating a dedicated court of criminal appeal alongside a separate court of civil appeal.
It would appoint additional judges with expertise in criminal law to the new court of criminal appeal.
The overhaul would be introduced alongside tougher bail and sentencing laws, which the Coalition has committed to enacting before the end of the year if it wins government.
Together, the measures would help set new legal precedents which the Coalition said would ultimately lead to tougher sentences for serious offences.
“It’s time for a new approach,” Wilson said on Sunday. “Our new criminal court will empower specialist criminal law judges to ensure sentencing of criminals meet community expectations. Each sentence they hand down will form part of case law going forward, helping to establish appropriate consequences for criminal actions.
In Victoria, judges are appointed by the governor on the recommendation of the attorney general. The shadow attorney general, James Newbury, said “nothing will change” about that process, though a “strong background in criminal matters will be a key focus” when making appointments.
“[It] will mean that criminal matters are dealt with by specialist judges who will be tough on crime, who will be tough on criminal offences,” he said.
Newbury said he had “consulted in a way that Victorians would expect” with judges and the courts about the policy, though he said it would be inappropriate to discuss the consultation publicly.
Legal and human rights groups, however, have criticised the proposal.
Gemma Cafarella, the president of Liberty Victoria, described it as a “dangerous and ignorant thought bubble designed without the input of experts”.
She said in “properly functioning democracies” parliaments make the laws and courts apply them, with the two systems kept seperate.
“Governments shouldn’t choose judges to get the outcomes they want,” Cafarella said. “This is a move that would politicise the criminal courts, and it must be rejected.”
She said the comments by the Coalition were by implication an “appalling political attack on the work of court of appeal judges”.
The Australian Lawyers Alliance criminal justice spokesperson, Greg Barns SC, said there was “no clear evidence” the court of appeal structure was failing, “aside from the longstanding issue of underfunding”.
“This is a disturbing example of the risk of undermining the independence of the judiciary,” he said. “It sends a signal that the opposition is willing to interfere with judicial independence for political purposes.”
The Alliance’s director, Susan Accary, said they were “not persuaded” splitting the courts would improve the quality of justice or address delays in the system.
Tom Ballantyne, president of the Law Institute of Victoria, said it was unclear how the proposal “adds anything” to the court of appeal, as it “already has access to numerous judges with extensive criminal expertise”.
“Anything that could undermine the independence of the courts and its judges could have significant consequences and would be a significant concern to the community,” he said.
Earlier this month One Nation’s Victorian leader, Warren Pickering, said the party wanted to make “bleeding heart judges accountable” and “get rid” of those he believes fail to meet community expectations.
Crime continues to be a major issue in the lead-up to the November election, with the Labor government having already passed controversial “adult time for violent crime” and tougher bail laws. It is also undertaking a review of sentencing.
The premier, Ben Carroll, on Sunday said the new policy showed the Liberal party was “floundering”.
He questioned how the opposition could “rewrite case law overnight”.
“It shows you the Liberal party today have no legal expertise,” Carroll said.

full_text:
One Nation MP David Farley has conceded the minor party’s net migration target is “not too different” to Labor’s, echoing an earlier claim over which he was counselled by his party leader, Pauline Hanson.
Appearing on the ABC’s Insiders program on Sunday morning, Farley argued skilled workers and backpackers were critical to keeping Australia fed, and argued they should be considered as a separate category to migration “in its true form”.
The minor rightwing party, led by Hanson, has struggled to define its migration policy, with inconsistent messaging over whether its target figure represents net overseas migration (Nom) or permanent migration.
The member for Farrer said One Nation’s Nom target remained 130,000. But he said that figure did not include skilled workers, backpackers and Pacific and Timor-Leste labour through the Pacific Australia Labour Mobility (Palm) scheme.
Farley said he expected there would be room for a “minimum” 100,000 additional people in the migration target to ensure critical industries had enough workers. Those included about 40,000 Palm workers and 70,000 skilled workers, including aged care nurses.
“A minimum of 100 [thousand additional migrant workers], but the 130,000 [target] is what we call the true Nom,” he told ABC’s Insiders on Sunday.
“I think the big difference is [that] we’re focusing on: what are the skills we need as a nation, where do we need these migrants to be.
“The raw number is not too different [to the government’s], but the reality is, where do we need them? We don’t need them in the great urban metroplex. We need them out to be productive, working in agriculture, engineering, mining.”
The Nom is calculated by the difference between the number of people entering and leaving the country – though it excludes short-term visitors such as tourists. It includes Australians moving abroad and returning, and is different to permanent migration, which measures longer-term visas offered for skilled workers and family members. For this financial year, there are 185,000 permanent places.
The Nom figure surged after the pandemic, during which it fell below zero, but has began to return to more typical levels in recent quarters.
The Nom was forecast to drop to 295,000 people last financial year but reached 301,000. The government forecasts it to drop to 245,000 in 2026-27 and 225,000 in 2027-28.
The Albanese government is preparing to announce changes to the migration system to achieve Nom targets. However, the home affairs minister, Tony Burke, cancelled a planned National Press Club appearance earlier this month over internal unrest on the final policy.
The Coalition has declined to provide an exact figure for its Nom target, but the opposition leader, Angus Taylor, has indicated it will be “well below 200,000”.
One Nation’s immigration policy is listed as offering a hard visa cap of 130,000 a year – a policy that would probably lead to a negative Nom. Barnaby Joyce, a former Nationals MP who defected to One Nation last December, has suggested the 130,000 number was instead a target for the Nom.
Farley’s electorate in south-western NSW relies on migrant workers for aged care and food processing. The Farrer MP said more than two-thirds of workers in his seat’s slaughterhouses and processing units were migrants.
“We need to have dexterity and flexibility in it. Managed properly, [the migration system] works well … we’re talking a system that’s critical to Australia. It’s critical to our food,” he said.
Before being elected, Farley said Australia’s net overseas migration of 306,000 last year was “probably not” too many.
Hanson later said she had counselled him on the comments, while Joyce described them as a slip-up during the “pressure of a campaign”.
On Sunday Farley also said he was “impressed” by Anthony Albanese after the prime minister reassured him in person of a planned bailout for rice mills in his electorate.
Farley was also asked about Hanson’s decision to appeal to the high court against a finding that she racially discriminated against Greens senator Mehreen Faruqi, and whether discrimination laws should allow people to offend, insult or humiliate someone based on race.
He said: “Well, I’m not convinced that we need to go and change anything at the moment.”

title: The ‘ordinary’ woman accused of assassinating a Russian commander in Crimea
summary:
Friends close to Margarita Reutt are shocked she could allegedly plant bomb that killed Ukrainian defector Robert Shageev, while others recall a stubborn grit to see any plan through

It was just after dawn in Sevastopol when a powerful explosion tore through a quiet square in a residential district of the Russian-occupied Crimean port city.

Hidden inside a rubbish bin, a bomb containing the equivalent of about 500g of TNT detonated on 13 August as Robert Shageev, the deputy commander of a Russian Black Sea fleet submarine brigade, walked past in naval uniform. He was killed on the spot.

full_text:
It was just after dawn in Sevastopol when a powerful explosion tore through a quiet square in a residential district of the Russian-occupied Crimean port city.
Hidden inside a rubbish bin, a bomb containing the equivalent of about 500g of TNT detonated on 13 August as Robert Shageev, the deputy commander of a Russian Black Sea fleet submarine brigade, walked past in naval uniform. He was killed on the spot.
Within hours, investigators had a suspect. Police detained Margarita Reutt, a 32-year-old resident of Sochi, the Russian resort city about 300 miles across the Black Sea from Sevastopol.
During a search, investigators said they had found a remote control they believed was used to detonate the bomb that killed Shageev, a former commander of Ukraine’s only submarine who switched allegiance to Russia in 2014 when Moscow annexed Crimea.
According to the security service, she confessed to the attack and said that a handler linked to Ukrainian intelligence had promised her a large payment in cryptocurrency and documents that would allow her to leave Russia afterwards.
The FSB also said Reutt showed no remorse.
Those assertions could not be independently verified, and Russian security agencies have previously publicised purported confessions from detainees before their cases have reached court. But several people previously accused by Russia of carrying out similar attacks against military figures were later found by reporters to have been involved in the operations Moscow had accused them of conducting.
What exactly drove Reutt to allegedly embark on such an audacious mission remains unclear. As with other cases involving accused Ukrainian intelligence operations, her trial is likely to take place behind closed doors, offering little opportunity for her to give her own account publicly.
But interviews with a dozen friends and acquaintances, combined with an examination of years of her social media activity, offer a portrait of a determined and adventurous woman whose attitude towards her country appears to have hardened gradually, with signs of a more striking change emerging in the months leading up to the attack.
“Rita believed that the country was going in the wrong direction,” said a longtime friend, using the diminutive form of her name. “But I am still shocked she went so far,” the friend added.
Russia quickly accused Reutt of carrying out the attack on the orders of Ukrainian intelligence. Kyiv has not commented on the bombing or Reutt’s alleged role in it.
Since the start of the full-scale invasion, Ukraine’s intelligence agencies have been linked to a string of assassinations and attempted killings of senior Russian military officers whom Kyiv has accused of involvement in the invasion. Ukrainian officials have occasionally acknowledged involvement in such operations, but more often have remained silent.
The attacks have involved an array of methods and recruits, from committed anti-Kremlin saboteurs to Russians promised large sums of money. In other cases, unsuspecting couriers and delivery workers have effectively been used as mules.
Usually, little is known about those accused of carrying out such attacks or how they prepared for them. Some have managed to escape, or were never publicly identified by Russian authorities, while others were killed carrying out their operations.
The swift capture and naming of Reutt, however, offers a rare opportunity to examine the journey of a Russian citizen accused of turning against her own country.
Reutt, born Margarita Yakovleva, grew up in Yaroslavl, a city north-east of Moscow, where she took the surname of the grandmother who largely raised her after her parents divorced. Friends recalled a largely unremarkable childhood, remembering her as warm and sociable, but also unusually drawn to adventure and risk.
“Margarita was fearless. She would climb trees, jump off cars, do things most boys were scared of,” recalled one friend from her childhood.
That streak followed her to Novosibirsk, thousands of miles to the east, where she studied management and threw herself into university life. Reutt became a regular at a local parachuting club, with photographs showing her jumping from Soviet-era aircraft, often the only woman among groups of men in camouflage gear.
She also won prizes in amateur go-karting competitions and took up water polo, becoming goalkeeper for the university team and quickly distinguishing herself despite being new to the sport. “Margarita was so talented and never afraid of the ball,” recalled her water polo coach at the time.
There was little then to suggest hostility towards the Kremlin. In Novosibirsk, Reutt became a well-liked member of a patriotic volunteer group that searched for the remains of Soviet soldiers killed during the second world war, part of a nationwide movement dedicated to recovering and reburying the war dead.
After graduating, Reutt moved south to Sochi, the Black Sea resort that became her home. She briefly tried her hand at running a travel agency before joining Vitauct in the early 2020s, an alternative medicine company specialising in longevity.
“She was the most ordinary person,” said Gennadiy Garbuzov, the company’s founder, who struggled to reconcile the woman he knew with the allegations now facing her. “There was nothing to indicate she would do this. She must have fallen under someone’s influence.”
On the surface, her online life was similarly unremarkable. She posted frequently about health and animal rights and took to Telegram forums to discuss alternative medicine.
Reutt also travelled widely. Leaked records from travel databases seen by the Guardian and photographs posted online show frequent trips abroad, including to Turkey, Thailand and Sri Lanka, where she often shared photographs of herself in bikinis at beach resorts.
“Margarita just seemed to be living her life and had lots of plans for the future,” said another colleague at Vitauct.
“She was good-looking and popular,” the colleague added.
In October 2025, Reutt travelled to Minsk for her sister’s wedding. Photographs from the celebration show her smiling among relatives and catching the bridal bouquet. To one friend she painted an idyllic picture of her life in Sochi, traversing mountains, waterfalls and canyons. “You can explore endlessly here, everything is lush and green,” she wrote to the friend.
But beneath that outwardly happy life, another side of Reutt was becoming visible. She increasingly expressed concerns about environmental problems plaguing Sochi, and started to become involved in local volunteer initiatives, friends said.
After a large oil spill in the Black Sea in December 2024, when two Russian tankers were wrecked in a storm, Reutt travelled to Anapa to join volunteers cleaning mazut, a heavy fuel oil, from contaminated beaches.
Exactly when dissatisfaction with her surroundings hardened into something more political is difficult to establish. Friends described a growing estrangement from Russia that deepened after the country launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
“The war came as a shock,” said one friend, who recalled Reutt becoming increasingly outspoken in public about the fighting in Ukraine. “I told her once to keep quiet, otherwise she would get us both into trouble,” the friend said.
By July 2025, her anti-war feelings had spilt into public view. While travelling on a Samara-Adler train, Reutt was fined under Russia’s sweeping law against “discrediting” the armed forces after reportedly shouting “Serves you right, Russians!” when news broke of a Ukrainian drone strike on a railway station in the Rostov region.
The following February, Reutt posted the results of a genetic test showing she was 98% Russian, adding a hashtag declaring that she was “ashamed to be Russian”.
Yet to friends and acquaintances, Reutt appeared to carry on much as before. She picked up occasional jobs, appeared in video clips made by friends and continued to travel. As recently as March

full_text:
The new leader of Iran’s top security body has warned its neighbours against joining new US efforts to squeeze Tehran’s economy, and threatened US commercial interests in the region, as Donald Trump doubled down on his fanciful view that the strait of Hormuz was a new US territory.
Mohsen Rezaei, the hardline new leader of Iran’s supreme national security council, told state television that Iran would target oil-shipping routes out the Gulf – alternatives to the strait of Hormuz – if its neighbours joined what he called the “economic war” waged by the US. Those neighbours would be “considered an enemy” and “we will target their interests”, he said.
Rezaei was a commander-in-chief of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) for most of the 1980-88 war with Iraq and was named this month in a series of senior appointments widely seen as hardening Tehran’s political and military stance.
His interview with broadcaster IRIB is his most extensive public statement since his appointment.
Rezaei also claimed the Islamic republic had more cards to play in the war, saying “we have not yet attacked any American economic interests”.
“So far, we have only targeted military bases, but if they want to impose economic sanctions on us, the United States has oil and economic companies around Iran and elsewhere, and we will strike them,” Rezai said in the interview, broadcast on Saturday.
Last week, Trump announced a new campaign to isolate Iran’s economy, threatening “tremendous economic consequences” on any country that helps or does business with Tehran, as the US president’s unpopular war drags toward the six-month mark without any significant sign of resolution.
Trump’s efforts to finish the war he started along with Israel on 28 February have foundered after a ceasefire agreement signed in June collapsed – leaving Iran in control of the strait of Hormuz, a waterway that was the conduit for one-fifth of the world’s oil supplies before the conflict.
Washington has called on other governments to join its efforts to isolate the Iranian economy, notably China, among Iran’s top strategic partners. However Beijing has criticised the initiative, arguing that US sanctions would not resolve the conflict in the Middle East.
One of Iran’s major trading partners, the United Arab Emirates, announced on Tuesday last week that it was suspending all trade and financial transactions with Tehran until further notice.
The US treasury has for months been carrying out Operation Economic Fury, aiming to cut off Iran’s funding with targeted sanctions, while a naval blockade in the strait of Hormuz has sought to block Iranian ports from exporting oil vital to keeping the country’s economy afloat.
The US president has in recent days repeatedly raised the concept of declaring the strait a US territory. “We control it with the blockade, and I like the idea of declaring it a territory,” he told reporters on Monday when asked about that comment.
On Friday, the US president told a crowd in South Carolina: “We don’t even know if we won, because I view the strait of Hormuz as an American territory right now.”
On Saturday night, Trump again shared on his social media platform a map graphic showing the Gulf and describing the strait of Hormuz as a “new US territory”.
Rezaei said in his interview that discussions continued with cross-strait neighbour Oman over management of the waterway, and said fees would be imposed.
French president Emmanuel Macron and Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman are expected to discuss plans to develop alternative routes to the strait of Hormuz during the Saudi leader’s two-day visit to Paris that starts on Sunday, according to officials in the presidency who weren’t authorised to speak publicly.
Proposals include increasing trade through Omani ports outside the Gulf, expanding or doubling pipelines in Saudi Arabia and elsewhere, and developing new rail links, the officials said.
France and Saudi Arabia have formed a taskforce on energy and logistics connections between the Middle East and Europe that is scheduled to meet at the ministerial level on Monday. The officials said the work would focus on identifying the most strategic projects, securing financing and establishing roles for French companies.
With Associated Press and Agence France-Presse

title: 俄羅斯最有錢女人大失血：電商龍頭 Wildberries 三分之一倉儲被無人機炸成灰
summary:
俄羅斯最大電商平台 Wildberries 過去一個月遭烏克蘭無人機連環轟炸，三分之一倉庫化為廢墟，貨物損失估 […]

〈俄羅斯最有錢女人大失血：電商龍頭 Wildberries 三分之一倉儲被無人機炸成灰〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
俄羅斯最大電商平台 Wildberries 過去一個月遭烏克蘭無人機連環轟炸，三分之一倉庫化為廢墟，貨物損失估計高達 59 億美元。保單普遍拒賠、銀行體系跟著承壓。
（前情提要：一顆 18 美元晶片，讓烏克蘭無人機在 GPS 幹擾、遙控中斷下，仍可自主鎖定目標）
（背景補充：普丁慘了？俄羅斯前高層投書：菁英正在切割、GDP 腰斬、支援率下跌，系統崩解倒數）
一家囊括俄羅斯線上零售 45% 市佔、日均處理 700 萬筆訂單的電商巨獸，一個月內被無人機炸掉三分之一倉庫、59 億美元貨物付之一炬，這是俄羅斯最大電商平台 Wildberries 眼下的處境。
自 7 月中旬起，烏克蘭已對 Wildberries 發動至少 21 次以上的無人機攻擊，累計燒毀超過 150 萬平方公尺倉儲空間，佔其總倉儲面積四分之一以上；根據公開彙整的逐次打擊紀錄，單月內至少 9 名員工在爆炸中喪生。
從英語教師到俄羅斯女首富
Wildberries 創辦人塔季揚娜金（Tatyana Kim）出身俄羅斯北韓族家庭，曾是一名英語教師。2004 年，她與前夫弗拉迪斯拉夫·巴卡爾丘克（Vladislav Bakalchuk）一起創業，最初只是賣歐洲服裝目錄上的商品，如今已成長為全國近 9 萬 5000 個提貨點的零售巨頭。
金曾談起創業初衷：「這個想法源於我自己的需求，結果被數十萬人所需要。如果某個產品或服務能讓你的生活更輕鬆，你就走對了方向。」
普丁下令入侵烏克蘭後，西方品牌陸續撤出俄羅斯市場，Wildberries 的地位不減反增。根據 Wildberries 與 Russ 合併後的 RWB 集團財報，2025 年營業額達 6.1 兆盧布（約 750 億美元）、淨利 1750 億盧布（約 21.5 億美元）；The Moscow Times 的分析指出，Wildberries 2026 年預估囊括俄羅斯線上零售 45% 市佔率（對手 Ozon 為 32%），客群覆蓋俄羅斯三分之二成年人口，全國逾 200 座倉庫、總倉儲面積約 550 萬平方公尺。
一個月 21 次打擊，十大物流樞紐倒了七座
烏克蘭的打擊並非隨機掃射，而是有計畫地鎖定物流節點。7 月 18 日，莫斯科州 Elektrostal 一座 23 萬平方公尺倉庫遭全毀，造成 1 死 37 傷；同日坦波夫州 Kotovsk 倉庫也傳出 7 死。此後攻勢幾乎沒有間斷：
- 7 月 22 日：克拉斯諾達爾 15 萬平方公尺倉庫全毀
- 7 月 24 日：聖彼得堡 Shushary 倉庫停止營運
- 8 月 5 日：圖拉州 Aleksin 19.45 萬平方公尺倉庫全毀
- 8 月 11 日：沃羅涅日新園區全毀（2025 年 11 月才啟用，可存放 9000 萬件商品）
- 8 月 16 日：莫斯科州 Koledino 20 萬平方公尺倉庫全毀
TechTimes 報導指出，烏克蘭網軍（HUR）8 月 10 日至 15 日兩度入侵 Wildberries 支付系統，搭配約 600 架無人機同步攻勢，一度癱瘓其十大物流樞紐中的 7 座。
8 月 22 日凌晨，戰火正式也燒向第二大平台 Ozon。Euromaidan Press 報導，烏克蘭自製的 FP-1 無人機擊中薩馬拉州 Chapayevsk 的一座 Ozon 倉庫並引發大火，這是烏軍首次確認擊中 Ozon 設施。
無人機製造商 Fire Point 表示，該倉庫是 Ozon 規模最大的倉庫之一，日處理訂單逾 21.5 萬筆。Ozon 證實有人受傷、疏散超過 500 名員工，已將配送與訂單改道其他設施；薩馬拉州長 Vyacheslav Fedorishchev 證實數人送醫。與 Wildberries 不同，Fire Point 並未主張這座 Ozon 倉庫涉及軍用物資補給。
59 億美元損失只是保守估計
Data Insight 估算，Wildberries 累計損失已達三分之一倉庫空間、59 億美元（約 4800 億盧布）貨物，分析師謝爾蓋·塞姆科（Sergei Semko）形容「最大的倉庫幾乎已經空了」。
Forbes 俄羅斯估計賣家端損失介於 2149 億至 2796 億盧布（26.4 億至 34.4 億美元），倉庫重建成本則估計落在 1050 億至 2230 億盧布（12.9 億至 26 億美元）之間。
保單不賠、銀行喊話，40 萬賣家求助無門
損失規模驚人，但真正棘手的是「誰來買單」。約 80% 的倉庫建物與庫存從未投保；更關鍵的是，Wildberries 在 7 月 11 日生效的新條款，直接把無人機襲擊排除在賠償責任之外。
金本人公開表態：「對我們倉庫的恐怖攻擊屬不可抗力……這些損失依法不予賠償」，並要求受影響賣家改向官方管道與政府紓困求助。
保險公司 Ingosstrakh 隨即把無人機襲擊險的費率調高 3.3 倍。金融面的壓力也開始外溢：7 月 25 日 VTB 銀行股價下跌 2.5%，市場開始擔心 Wildberries 的償債能力；俄羅斯央行隨後要求 Sberbank、VTB 等大型銀行提供債務重組方案，截至 8 月 10 日，Sberbank 已收到約 2000 件貸款重組申請。平台上逾 40 萬名賣家至今多數求償無門。
烏克蘭真正要打的，不是倉庫
澤倫斯基將打擊目標定義為「涉及向俄軍供應無人機零件、導航裝置與其他軍用硬體的物流中心」；基輔認為 Wildberries 佔俄羅斯零售總額約 10%、同時向俄軍供貨，是合法的軍事目標。
但烏克蘭總統顧問 Podolyak 的說法更直白，攻擊意在「擾亂軍事補給、製造民眾不滿，並透過對 VTB、Sberbank 等主要銀行造成壓力，引發俄羅斯經濟連鎖效應」，換句話說，倉庫只是手段，金融體系與民心士氣才是真正的標的。數字也印證了這個判斷：7 月底俄國軍用商品銷售明顯下滑，防彈衣銷量減少 24%、四軸飛行器配件重挫 36%、夜視裝置下滑 20% 至 40%；平台廣告投放量 6 月到 7 月下滑 63%，廣告價格最多降 15%。
這場攻勢也讓「商業基礎設施是否算戰場」的界線變得模糊。Wildberries 與 Ozon 合計佔俄羅斯 GDP 約 8.5%、僱用 400 萬人，物流骨幹一旦被癱瘓，牽動的不只是消費者買不到貨，更是保險定價、銀行授信與財政赤字的連鎖反應。
當 80% 倉庫從未投保、平台又以「不可抗力」拒賠，風險最終轉嫁給數十萬中小賣家。Ozon 8 月初起已把高價商品分散到各地提貨點，這正是烏克蘭想看到的結果：讓戰爭代價直接寫進俄羅斯消費者的購物車，以及每一間銀行的資產負債表。

title: 'We're not going to run from it': Sydney Marathon laughs off medal error
summary: Runners will receive a medal at the 2026 Sydney Marathon with an engraving of a German stadium.
full_text:
'We're not going to run from it': Sydney Marathon laughs off medal error
- Published
The organisers of Sydney Marathon have laughed off a mistake which saw a German stadium etched on to medals for participants, saying "we're not going to run from it".
Questions arose after the event's official social media account unveiled the design of this year's medal earlier in the week, which had mistakenly etched Allianz Arena, based in the German city of Munich, instead of Sydney's Allianz Stadium.
A spokesperson for the Sydney Marathon told the BBC: "A little too much international flavour has found its way onto the back of the finishers medal, with an incorrect depiction of the stadium."
It was "an unfortunate error," they added.
Recognisable Sydney landmarks feature on the double-sided medal, including the Opera House and Harbour Bridge, which are part of the 42.2km (26.2 mile) course.
Users on social media noticed the shape of the stadium engraved on the medal appeared to be carved in the wrong likeness.
Munich's Allianz Arena is sculpted by thousands of diamond-shaped inflatable cushions, while Sydney's similarly named Allianz Stadium has a flatter facade smoothed with long bronze fins.
Sydney Marathon confirmed runners would receive the medal depicting the incorrect city's stadium, noting: "It's a beautiful medal, and now a little more unique."
"It's certainly given everyone something to talk about this weekend, mostly in good humour."
Germany's Allianz Arena also poked fun at the mistake, writing on Instagram: "Oh wow, we didn't have that on our bingo card!"
"Perhaps they tried to find something else they had in common: Allianz Arena -- Sydney Opera -- Unique Architecture -- Both are worth a visit!"
The reverse side of the Sydney Marathon medal shows a gold and indigo pattern designed by First Nations artist Ambrose Killian, widely commended for its ornate pattern.
He confirmed to the BBC that he was not involved in designing the other face of the medal engraved with the wrong stadium.
Some 40,000 runners will take part in the event on 30 August, following more than 120,000 ballot entries.
Organisers praised record participation and fundraising for this year's event.

title: 免費爽用 Ox Alpha 教學：神秘模型寫程式媲美 Claude Fable 5，身份疑是智譜 GLM
summary:
免費、100 萬 Token 上下文的匿名模型 Ox Alpha 這兩天讓開發者圈炸鍋，開發者測試跑分甚至超越 […]

〈免費爽用 Ox Alpha 教學：神秘模型寫程式媲美 Claude Fable 5，身份疑是智譜 GLM〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
免費、100 萬 Token 上下文的匿名模型 Ox Alpha 這兩天讓開發者圈炸鍋，開發者測試跑分甚至超越 Claude Fable 5 與 GPT-5.6 Sol。目前身份也幾乎確定是智譜 GLM 的多模態版本。
（前情提要：每天 100 兆 Token 隨你燒！中國神秘模型 Ox Alpha 宣布免費一週）
（背景補充：中國八週連發 5 款 AI 模型，更便宜 token 把美國中段班逼上絕路）
這兩天開發者社群都在討論一支名叫 Ox Alpha 的匿名模型。它 8 月 20 日前後悄悄上架 OpenRouter，沒有公司出面說明，但打出兩個很難忽略的規格：完全免費、上下文長度來到百萬 Token，還能直接吃文字、圖片、影片。OpenCode 官方帳號甚至喊出「我們每天有 100 兆 Token 的容量，讓我們看看你能怎麼用」這種話。
再次把討論點燃的是寫程式成績。開發者 Ben Davis 拿它跑 DeepSWE 測試，結果成績竟然壓過 Claude Fable 5 與 GPT-5.6 Sol。數字一傳開，社群嘗試熱度更高。
過往匿名放模型上架測水溫，在 OpenRouter 上已經是成熟套路。前四隻動物代號模型 Pony、Hunter、Elephant、Owl Alpha 最後分別由智譜、小米、螞蟻集團與美團認領，全部來自中國，所以社群一看到 Ox Alpha，第一件事就是開始猜它哪家中國品牌的？
幾乎確定是智譜 GLM
身份證據裡最硬的一條來自服務層。有人攔截到 Ox Alpha 洩漏出來的 Java 錯誤訊息，類別名稱是 com.wd.paas.api.domain.v4.chat.ChatCompletionRequest，錯誤回應逐字寫著 {"code":"1214","message":"Incorrect role information"}，跟智譜 AI（Z.AI）自家託管 GLM 模型的錯誤格式一模一樣；同一份權重換到 DeepInfra 上託管，吐出來的格式卻完全不同。
這代表指紋認出來的不只是誰的模型權重，是誰在背後跑這組伺服器。研究者 Chetaslua 據此把營運方是智譜的信心值標到 0.98。
先講清楚它到底多強
不過要補充說明的是，Ben Davis 貼出的測試成績是他自己挑出的 10 題 DeepSWE 子集，不是官方榜；同一輪測試裡，Claude Fable 5 拿 65%，GPT-5.6 Sol 拿 52%、Ox Alpha 拿 80%。
10 題的測試，每答對或答錯一題就能拉動約 10 個百分點，社群自己給的判準是：樣本少於 50 題的分數只能當訊號，不能當結論。如果 Ox Alpha 真的是 GLM-5.3 的多模態版本，合理的實力區間就是官方榜上 GLM-5.3 的 69%，跟 Claude Fable 5 的 70% 幾乎打平。
路線一：OpenRouter，三步就能打
如果想把握時間免費體驗，你可以有兩種方式：
第一種是先到 OpenRouter 帳號的 API key 設定頁建立一組金鑰，這是第一步。
第二步，model id 記好 stealth/ox-alpha，輸入與輸出定價都是 0；Base URL 是 https://openrouter.ai/api/v1，端點走 /chat/completions，跟 OpenAI 介面相容，換掉 base_url 就能打。
第三步，直接用 curl 測試：
curl https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENROUTER_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"stealth/ox-alpha","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
習慣寫 Python 的人，用 OpenAI SDK 換個 base_url 就能接上：
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI(base_url="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1", api_key="<OPENROUTER_API_KEY>")
resp = client.chat.completions.create(model="stealth/ox-alpha", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}])
路線二：OpenCode，不用寫程式
習慣在終端機裡工作的人，可以直接掛進 OpenCode。在 TUI 裡打 /connect，搜尋 OpenRouter、貼上 API key，再打 /models 挑出這支模型即可，或用旗標 opencode -m openrouter/stealth/ox-alpha 直接指定。想設成預設模型，寫進 opencode.json：
{"$schema":"https://opencode.ai/config.json","model":"openrouter/stealth/ox-alpha"}
清單裡找不到的話，手動掛一段設定也行：
{"$schema":"https://opencode.ai/config.json","provider":{"openrouter":{"models":{"stealth/ox-alpha":{}}}}}
OpenCode 自家閘道 OpenCode Zen 也內建了同一支模型，顯示名稱是「Ox Alpha Free (Unlimited)」，model id 是 opencode/x-preview-f-free。
接之前要知道的三件事
第一，速度不是旗艦等級。OpenRouter 官方統計吞吐量 P50 為 23 tokens/秒，延遲 P50 為 5.49 秒；另一份約三天期的監測數字接近，每秒 24 個 Token，延遲 5.81 秒。這個速度拿來做一問一答的即時對話會有感，比較適合丟一包長任務讓它自己跑完再回來看。穩定度倒是不錯，3 天內 uptime 有 99.99%，免費模型常見的排隊與斷線在它身上沒有特別明顯。
第二，結構化輸出要自己顧。它支援 response_format 的 JSON 輸出，也支援 tool calling，reasoning effort 可以在 low、high、max 之間切，預設走推理模式。但官方特別註明不做 JSON schema 強制，意思是它會回你一包 JSON，卻不保證欄位長得跟你定義的一樣。如果下游程式直接吃這包 JSON，驗證那一層要自己補上，不能省。
第三，資料政策要先看懂再丟東西。OpenRouter 模型頁上寫的字面是「Prompts and completions for this model are retained by the provider and are not used for training」，也就是保留但不訓練，不是零保留；OpenCode 官方帳號的推文喊的卻是零資料保留，兩邊字面對不上。
在身份還沒被官方蓋章之前，你送進去的東西實際上是交給一家不具名的供應商保管，丟私有程式碼庫之前，這一條要先想清楚。
Notes for this stealth model:
💰 It is free
🔑 This time, the provider does not train on your prompts or completions
— OpenRouter (@OpenRouter) August 20, 2026

title: 中國街頭驚現乞丐機器人，網有：不努力未來連乞丐都當不上（有影）
summary:
X 上最近廣傳多部影片顯示，中國街頭出現裝扮成人類乞丐的機器人，目前尚未證實是否只是擺拍，但網友笑宇樹機器人終 […]

〈中國街頭驚現乞丐機器人，網有：不努力未來連乞丐都當不上（有影）〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
X 上最近廣傳多部影片顯示，中國街頭出現裝扮成人類乞丐的機器人，目前尚未證實是否只是擺拍，但網友笑宇樹機器人終於有了落地場景。
（前情提要：宇樹科技 IPO 首日開盤暴漲 629%，為什麼 Unitree 人形機器人概念引爆資本市場？）
（背景補充：宇樹機器人招股書揭密：人形Robot出貨全球第一，商業化靠學校研究機構）
X上最近有部影片廣傳，可以看到中國街頭上有著一個裹著黑外套、戴橘色毛帽的乞討者，趴在人行道上不斷磕頭，面前擺著一個裝零錢的塑膠罐。眼尖的網友多看了兩眼才發現，它根本不是人，而是一個機器人。
网友发现，宇树机器人终于有了真正的应用场景，就是装扮成真人乞讨。🤣🤣 pic.twitter.com/LOU3rsIAAi
— 作家崔成浩 (@cuichenghao) August 23, 2026
網友的留言更精彩。有人說：「你送一盒米飯過去，站起來罵娘，那就是真人；繼續磕頭，那就是機器人。」也有人打趣：「哇，這個好。就和買一輛自動駕駛的車給我跑滴滴，我在家收錢一樣。」也有人反問：「都能買得起機器人了還用乞討嗎？」
不過要提醒：這次「機器人扮成真人乞丐」的影片，目前只在社群平台流傳，還沒有主流媒體查證報導，拍攝地點是否為福州、是否為擺拍、乞討罐裡有沒有真的收到錢？全都還無法核實。
六月就演過一次
其實這不是機器人第一次在街頭「乞討」。今年六月中旬起，福建福州、北京、四川成都的街頭就出現過類似畫面：宇樹的人形機器人跪地、雙手合十作揖，腳邊擺著捐款二維碼、紙牌和討錢的碗，反覆播放預錄語音，大意是「生活不易，機器人討生活，沒錢充電好幾天了，求捐電費」。
中国的机器人开始上街乞讨电费了(ಥ_ಥ) pic.twitter.com/7iV9TkFkFU
— 小牛 (@Xiaoniu6161) June 3, 2026
多家媒體指認機型是宇樹科技的 G1 人形機器人，官方標價自 13,500 美元起，電池續航約兩個小時。外界普遍認為這是行銷快閃或擺拍，畢竟機器人不可能自己決定去乞討，整套動作是事先編好的程式；也有人把它解讀成一種諷刺藝術，用高科技機器扮窮，本身就是個反差夠強的段子。
當時中國網友的反應也很直白：「乞丐也內捲」、「連這行都被搶」、「不努力連乞丐都當不上」。

title: 比特幣有新硬分叉：ECX 十月上線主網 1:1 發幣，你可以拿嗎？
summary:
比特幣今天（8/23）在區塊高度 963648 啟動 ECX 硬分叉的 alpha 測試，等於在原有比特幣帳本 […]

〈比特幣有新硬分叉：ECX 十月上線主網 1:1 發幣，你可以拿嗎？〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
比特幣今天（8/23）在區塊高度 963648 啟動 ECX 硬分叉的 alpha 測試，等於在原有比特幣帳本上複製出一條新鏈；但真正決定你手上多出多少 ECX 的關鍵快照，要等到 10 月 31 日的正式主網上線。
（前情提要：比特幣 BIP-110 分叉鏈落後 326 區塊、自我修復還要 6.3 年：礦工不買單）
（背景補充：比特幣結合 DeFi 共築未來？BIP-300 的下一步怎麼走）
比特幣今天（8/23）在區塊高度 963,648 時，開發者 Paul Sztorc（@Truthcoin）創辦的 Layertwo Labs 啟動一場醞釀多年的實驗，把他推了十年的 Drivechain 構想，用一次獨立硬分叉的方式端上檯面，代號 ECX（eCash）。
不過要提前說明的是，今天觸發的只是「alpha 演習」，真正的快照要等到 10 月 31 日的正式主網上線；直到那一刻，全比特幣網路的持有者手上才會被記上一筆等值的新資產。
另外也要補充，ECX 不會動到比特幣本身一分一毫：它是一條獨立網路，在指定區塊高度複製一份比特幣帳本，讓多數持有者在新鏈上獲得等量代幣，原本的 BTC 完全不受影響、不轉換、不鎖定。
— Paul Sztorc (@Truthcoin) August 23, 2026
1 枚 BTC 換 1 枚 ECX，原比特幣分毫不動
快照當下，若你自己保管 1 枚 BTC，新鏈上就會多出 1 枚 ECX，原本的 BTC 不會被轉走、鎖定或銷毀，兩條鏈上的資產完全獨立並存。
要注意的是，真正決定最終餘額的，只有 10 月 31 日、區塊高度約 973728 那一次主網快照。同時比特幣出塊時間本來就會浮動，官方版本一律以區塊高度為準，而非日曆日期，上文提到的日期還只是估算參考。
三階段時程表：8/23 alpha、9/20 beta、10/31 正式上線
專案刻意把時程拉成三段，希望保留時間讓開發者與基礎設施商抓漏洞：
- Alpha：8 月 23 日，區塊高度 963648。定位是「實彈演習」，可以跑軟體、挖礦、拿練習幣測試轉帳、試錢包、找漏洞，但這階段拿到的代幣叫 pECX（alpha ECX），不是永久資產。
- Beta：9 月 20 日，區塊高度 967680。這輪吃重的是交易所、錢包商、礦工與資產託管商的配合度，考驗的是基礎設施能不能撐住。
- 正式主網：10 月 31 日，區塊高度約 973728，恰好是中本聰白皮書發表 18 週年。這次快照才會產生永久 ECX 餘額，專案預計首批專用側鏈同步上線。
自己保管才拿得到，放在交易所就得看對方臉色
自我保管的人（私鑰握在自己手上），理論上快照後就能直接動用對應的 ECX；不過把 BTC 放在交易所或其他資產託管商的人，則完全得看那些平台自己決定要不要支援這次分叉、要不要幫用戶發放新資產，假如平台不支援，那你就是看得到吃不到。
實際怎麼領？
ECX 的整套領取設計刻意做得跟中心化空投不一樣：快照當下地址裡有多少 BTC，新鏈上就自動對應多少 ECX，不需要事先申請、不需要填寫任何表單，也不需要在任何地方註冊帳號。
實際操作路徑有兩條：一是把原本的 wallet 檔案直接在 BitWindow（ECX 版的 Bitcoin Core 前端，同時是進入全部 BIP-300 側鏈的入口）中開啟；二是用原本的助記詞，在會跟著分叉走的 SPV 錢包（如 Electrum、BlueWallet）裡直接還原。專案另外也提供 Apple（TestFlight）與 Android 版錢包供測試。
中本聰的 110 萬枚要怎麼處理
被歸類為「中本聰模式」的早期比特幣約有 110 萬枚，ECX 團隊把這批位址切成兩份處理：約 60 萬枚 ECX 仍照常分配給那些位址，另外約 50 萬枚則透過特殊交易改導向早期投資人與開發資金，支持者的說法是，這等於讓新網路不必辦 ICO 就能募到啟動資金。
再次強調的是，這個動作完全不碰比特幣鏈上、屬於中本聰的那批 BTC 本身。
別急著慶祝：還沒有真正的行情
實際上來說，ECX 目前還沒有任何既定市場價格，主網也還沒上線，測試期間即便有交易所搶先掛出期貨式報價，價格發現也會非常投機。
挖礦難度在上線瞬間會直接重置到最低，再逐步回復正常調整，早期挖礦條件可能劇烈震盪。比特幣本月初的 BIP-110 事件就是前車之鑑：那次同樣是想推限制鏈上資料的臨時軟分叉，卻拿不到有意義的礦工、節點與基礎設施支援，分裂出來的鏈挖了沒幾個區塊就停滯。
ECX 選擇在比特幣正常運作的同時，獨立去爭取用戶、礦工與資金，但交易所是否埋單、市場是否賞臉，都還是未知數。另外提醒一句：ECX 跟另一個同樣叫 ecash 的加密貨幣 XEC 完全無關，兩者不要搞混。
Drivechain 十年賭注
ECX 的真正目標是把 Sztorc 推了超過十年的 Drivechain 構想真正落地。
他在 2017 年提出 BIP-300，設計主鏈與側鏈之間的資產移轉機制；2019 年再提出 BIP-301，講的是盲合併挖礦（blind merged mining），讓礦工可以直接收側鏈手續費，不必真的去跑每一條側鏈的完整軟體。不過這兩份提案始終沒能在比特幣社群拿到足夠支援去走軟分叉。
Layertwo Labs 最終判斷，與其在共識戰場上再打一次，不如直接用獨立硬分叉把 Drivechain 願景付諸實踐。專案規劃首批上線 7 條專用側鏈，分別瞄準高吞吐支付（Thunder）、隱蔽交易（Zside）、去中心化身分（Bitnames）、代幣發行（Bitassets）、抗量子簽章（Photon）、預測市場（Truthcoin）與跨鏈交易（Coinshift）。
10 月 31 日的主網快照，只是這場賭注的起跑槍聲，不是終點。真正決定 ECX 能不能活下來的，是快照之後那幾個月：側鏈能不能真的跑起來、軟體夠不夠穩定、交易所願不願意上架、有沒有足夠礦工參與去驗證合併手續費模型真的划算。
對手上握有比特幣私鑰的一般人來說，眼下能做的其實很單純：記住三個區塊高度、顧好私鑰、跟著官方指引走，其餘的留給時間去驗證。

title: Police officers killed in wrong-way crash mourned in 'unimaginable loss'
summary: PC Matthew Blades, PC Tom Clough and five young people were killed when a car drove the wrong way on the A66 and struck the police vehicle.
full_text:
Police officers killed in wrong-way crash mourned in 'unimaginable loss'
- Published
Two police officers killed in a wrong-way crash on the A66 near Middlesbrough have been remembered as "brave officers protecting our communities" in what has been described as an "unimaginable loss".
PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, were killed when a Volkswagen Passat with five occupants said to be in their late teens to early 20s, driving the wrong way, struck the Cleveland Police vehicle at about 03:39 BST on Saturday.
The teens, who were also killed, have not been named.
The BBC understands a police pursuit of the car had ended before the crash, with the police vehicle just happening to be in the South Bank area.
The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) is now investigating.
Chief Constable Victoria Fuller said on Saturday it was an "incredibly sad day for Cleveland", adding: "No one should leave their home and not return safely."
Fuller said she and her deputy chief constable visited the officers' families to "offer our condolences, support one another, and begin to come to terms with this unimaginable loss".
Politicians, including the prime minister and home secretary, have remembered the officers, with Andy Burnham saying he was "devastated" by the news.
Anna Turley, MP for the Redcar constituency where the crash happened, said the officers "went to work to keep people safe and they should have come home to their families".
She added: "Their loss will be felt deeply by their loved ones, fellow officers and right across the communities they served."
David Taylor and Stephen Martin, councillors for the Eston ward, said they were "deeply saddened" by the "unimaginable tragedy".
Tees Valley mayor Ben Houchen called the case "a horrible and tragic incident" in a statement on Facebook.
"Our police officers are heroes who put everything on the line to protect us, and I know all of Teesside will want to pay tribute to the officers and other emergency service workers involved for the bravery they have shown in responding to this incident."
Cleveland Police Federation chairwoman Lauren Somerville said the loss of the officers was "unfathomable", adding: "Words cannot describe the pain the Cleveland Police family are feeling today."
When someone dies following police contact, it is mandatory for the case to be referred to the IOPC, which is now investigating.
The watchdog said on Saturday that "at this early stage, we understand Cleveland Police sighted a suspicious vehicle and a pursuit began."
Security footage from a house on Lime Road in Middlesbrough appears to show a car being pursued by police vehicles three minutes before the crash.
The BBC understands the pursuit ended prior to the crash, and the police vehicle occupied by PC Blades and PC Clough just happened to be in the area at the time.
IOPC Director of Investigations Nicola Marfleet called it a "tragic incident" and said her "thoughts are with family and friends and all those affected, including the emergency services in attendance."
Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp also shared his condolences, adding the IOPC "must be given the time and space to complete their investigations without speculation".
The A66, which is the major artery through Teesside and the location of the crash is surrounded by industrial units and factories, remained closed on Sunday.

title: Life after Salah - why Isak and Wirtz must step up for Liverpool
summary: Liverpool are preparing to begin a season without Mohamed Salah for the first time in a decade - but they haven't replaced him yet. This is why.
full_text:
Life after Salah - why Isak and Wirtz must step up for Liverpool
- Published
No player has scored more goals on the first matchday of a Premier League season than Mohamed Salah for Liverpool.
But when the Reds begin their 2026-27 campaign under Andoni Iraola at Newcastle on Sunday (kick-off 16:30 BST) , Salah will be playing for Trabzonspor against Istanbul Basaksehir in the Turkish Super Lig, some 2,100 miles away.
It will be the first time since 2015 that Liverpool will start a season without any of Salah, Sadio Mane or Roberto Firmino in their squad.
Between 2015 and 2026, that trio scored a combined 488 goals (Salah 257, Mane 120, Firmino 111) for the Reds.
Salah netted 10 of those goals on the opening matchday - a Premier League record.
With the Egypt superstar out of the picture, the top scorer in Liverpool's current squad is Cody Gakpo with just 50 Reds goals.
When Liverpool signed Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike for a combined £320m last summer, the future was very much in mind.
It is impossible for one player to replicate Salah's achievements, with his goalscoring and creative burden needing to be shared.
Ekitike, 24, had an impressive start to life at Anfield before rupturing his Achilles tendon in April, and the hope is he will be fit for the second half of this season.
And both Isak, 26, and Wirtz, 23, will be expected to lead the way in this new Liverpool era after disappointing debut campaigns.
When it was confirmed in March Salah would leave this summer, Liverpool were expected to make another statement signing - but with the season about to begin they are yet to do so.
"We need a squad that is able to compete on all four fronts, that's the only way to try to be successful," captain Virgil van Dijk said this week.
"Let's see what the last couple weeks of the transfer window brings and then let's go for it."
Reds pivot from Diomande to Barcola
It has been more than five months since Salah's exit was confirmed and Liverpool's hunt to sign another top-class forward goes on.
They failed in their pursuit of 19-year-old rising star Yan Diomande, who went to Real Madrid from RB Leipzig for a fee worth up to £120m.
Ekitike's injury absence means another attacker is even more of a priority - and there is growing confidence a deal will be struck for Paris St-Germain's Bradley Barcola.
The 23-year-old France winger is understood to be open to the move. PSG initially sought a fee in the region of £145m while Liverpool want to pay something closer to the £100m mark.
Liverpool explored a move for Barcola - who primarily operates on the left - last summer but opted not to pursue it as they were keen not to block Rio Ngumoha's pathway.
With Salah departing a year earlier than expected, the landscape has changed.
At St James' Park last August, Ngumoha became the youngest goalscorer in Liverpool's history with a memorable 100th-minute winner.
The English winger turns 18 next week and will be able to sign a five-year deal then. He has been trialled down the right flank, where Salah played, in pre-season.
Iraola wants his wingers to be able to play on both sides and - judging by the signing of Victor Munoz from Osasuna - Liverpool want pacy options that are direct and have the ability to break down low blocks.
They had a £50m bid rejected for Brighton's Yankuba Minteh this week while a move has been explored for PSG's Ibrahim Mbaye.
On Sunday, the likelihood is Gakpo - who has attracted interest from Spurs - will start down the left while Ngumoha will play on the right.
Munoz - who looked lively against Como last week - can provide a spark off the bench while Iraola is also open to using Gakpo as a number nine.
Wirtz will operate primarily behind the striker and believes he is better equipped for the demands of the Premier League now.
With a season under his belt, there is a genuine belief among those at Liverpool that there is much more to come from the German, who scored seven goals and provided 10 assists last season.
The spotlight will also fall on Isak, who scored 62 goals in 109 games for Newcastle but only netted four times in an injury-hit debut campaign at Anfield.
Encouragingly, the link-up between him and Wirtz seems to have developed in pre-season.
'Isak has everything in his locker'
Iraola believes Isak, who cost a British record transfer fee of £125m, will be "very important" this season and is in "a very good place."
"We know his level and if we can keep him there he will score the goals and give us a lot of things," said Iraola.
"Probably my fight with him and my instructions are more in terms of without the ball and how he can help in his position when we are with the ball so he can open spaces for other players."
Former Liverpool striker Robbie Fowler also thinks Isak will be a "handful" for the opposition.
"I'm a massive fan. He's proven it in the Premier League before. For a number of reasons, including the injury, it didn't work out last year but he's an exciting player and he will score goals and be a handful," said Fowler.
"As a striker, the price tag wouldn't bother me because the focus should be entirely on performing. Alexander is world class and the price tag won't bother him either.
"He has everything in the locker, is exciting when he drives with the ball and he makes things happen.
"He excites the fans which is imperative for a club like Liverpool. Not only can he beat players - he can bring others into the game and he can score goals which is massive."
Without Salah - and as the wait for Barcola continues - where better to step up to the plate for Isak than at the place he once called home.

title: Pegula dethrones Swiatek to book Cincinnati final against Gauff
summary: The women’s all-American final will be followed by a men's title clash between Frances Tiafoe and Arthur Fils of France.
full_text:
Pegula dethrones Swiatek to book Cincinnati final against Gauff
The women’s all-American final will be followedby a men’s title clash between Frances Tiafoe and Arthur Fils of France.
Jessica Pegula rallied in the third set to topple defending champion Iga Swiatek and book a title showdown with Coco Gauff at the Cincinnati Masters tennis tournament.
World number three Pegula won a “crazy” match against Swiatek 7-5, 4-6, 6-4 on Saturday in the US city.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4CONCACAF asks Infantino to skip youth event amid FIFA governance crisis
- list 2 of 4Former world champion boxer Zolani Tete shot and killed in South Africa
- list 3 of 4Arsenal rout Coventry 3-0 to begin Premier League title defence in style
- list 4 of 4Argentina’s Paredes gets 10-game ban for World Cup final scuffle with Spain
Gauff powered past giant-killer Sara Bejlek 6-4, 6-1, ending the unseeded Czech’s dream run that included a fourth-round victory over world number one Aryna Sabalenka.
Their all-American Sunday night final will be followed by a men’s title clash between American Frances Tiafoe and Arthur Fils of France.
Fils charged into his first Masters 1000 final with a 6-3, 6-4 victory over French Open runner-up Flavio Cobolli in a match delayed for 45 minutes by rain and lightning.
Swiatek and Pegula then waited out another rain delay before their match, which was also briefly interrupted two games in.
“Crazy match today,” Pegula said after needing nearly three hours to subdue Swiatek, who was coming off her first title of 2026 in Toronto last week.
“A lot of back and forth, a lot of breaks,” she said. “Really windy, kind of odd conditions. I felt like we were playing well and then not playing well.
“It was really tough to kind of get a gauge on the match.”
The pair rode a rollercoaster of breaks and re-breaks before Pegula took a 5-4 lead in the final set, Swiatek saving three break points before double-faulting on a fourth.
Pegula quickly closed it out, firing a service winner on match point.
“I was just really happy with the way I was able to kind of handle just a lot that was going on today,” the 31-year-old American said. “I did a good job no matter what was happening.”
The first five games of what evolved into an epic went against the server as Pegula and Swiatek struggled to adjust to the conditions.
Swiatek blinked first as Pegula held at love for a 4-2 lead, but Swiatek won the next three games before Pegula broke again, finally taking the set when Swiatek smacked a volley into the net on set point.
They had exchanged two breaks in the second when Swiatek broke in the final game to square the match.
Tiafoe feeling ‘damn good’ on return to final
Tiafoe, runner-up to Jannik Sinner in Cincinnati in 2024, returned to the final with a 7-5, 6-3 victory over fellow American Brandon Nakashima.
Tiafoe saved three set points in the opening set, breaking Nakashima five times in all to earn the win in less than two hours.
“It feels d*** good,” Tiafoe said.
The American predicted a “h*** of a show” against Fils, whose 68-minute win over seventh-seeded Cobolli made him the youngest French Masters finalist since a 20-year-old Richard Gasquet in Toronto two decades ago.
Fils admitted he had been unsettled by the weather delay.
“You come on court more nervous because it’s a semi-final. The rain arrives, you wait and when you come back conditions are completely different,” he said.
“It was tough, but I’m happy with how I dealt with it.”

title: Kazakhstan parliamentary elections begin: What’s at stake?
summary: The Central Asian country heads to the polls on August 23.
full_text:
Kazakhstan parliamentary elections begin: What’s at stake?
The Central Asian country heads to the polls on August 23.
Kazakhstan heads to the polls this week in a snap parliamentary election that is expected to strengthen President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s rule over the country. The last parliamentary elections were in 2023.
The election comes just weeks after Kazakhstan, a nation of 21 million that borders Russia and China, revamped its legislative system by introducing constitutional changes and shifting from a dual-chamber parliament to a single-chamber one as it seeks to assert itself as a major democratic power in Central Asia.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3Kazakhstan’s train hospital brings healthcare to remote regions
- list 2 of 3Germany arrests Kazakhstan citizen accused of spying for Russia
- list 3 of 3Kazakhstan releases first tiger to restore extinct species
How does the election process work and what’s at stake?
Here’s what we know:
When is the election happening?
Elections for the 145 seats of the Kurultai, the country’s new unicameral legislature, will take place on August 23.
To enter government, parties must receive at least 5 percent of the overall vote.
Before July 1, when Kazakhstan’s new constitutional system came into effect, the parliament was bicameral, with the Mazhilis (lower house) and Senate (upper house). On the day the new system came into effect, President Tokayev signed a decree calling the snap election.
According to national media outlet Astana Times, under the previous system, “legislation passed through the Mazhilis before moving to the Senate. Under the new model, the Kurultai concentrates legislative consideration, and adopted laws are then sent to the President.”
Under the new constitutional system, presidents will only be permitted to serve a single, seven-year term. However, when his current, second term as president is up, Tokayev will be able to run for a third seven-year term of office, since the introduction of the new legislature resets his time in office.
He won the last presidential election, in 2022, with more than 80 percent of the vote, having run largely unchallenged, as all five of his competitors were unknowns.
International observers will attend the parliamentary election on Sunday.
The OSCE Parliamentary Assembly announced last week that nearly 80 parliamentarians and staff from about 30 countries would be deployed to observe the election.
Who is contesting in this year’s election?
Seven political parties are fielding candidates in this year’s elections.
These include the newly formed Adilet party, Auyl, Aq Jol, the People’s Party of Kazakhstan, the Nationwide Social Democratic Party, Baytaq, and Respublica.
Amanat, the party that has dominated Kazakh politics under various names since the 1990s, officially voted to dissolve itself into Adilet – which means “Justice” – a new party led by top aides to Tokayev, in June this year, largely to distance itself from Amanat’s former leader, the previous President Nursultan Nazarbayev.
Nazarbayev, who was once close to Tokayev and considered his mentor, was the country’s president from 1991 to 2019. While he led economic modernisation of the country, his rule was defined by corruption, civil unrest and authoritarianism. He was elected president five times in widely criticised votes.
In the run-up to the election on Sunday, Adilet has been running on the campaign message of “Just Kazakhstan”, pledging to raise household incomes, strengthen the country’s economy and improve public services, infrastructure and digitalisation.
Around Almaty, Kazakhstan’s largest city, election posters – mostly in support of Adilet – have been ubiquitous for weeks, the Reuters news agency reported.
Opinion polls suggest the new party is likely to win a large majority of the vote, with a number of smaller opposition parties, which analysts also consider broadly loyal to Tokayev, also likely to enter parliament.
The Aq Jol Democratic Party is running on a campaign pledging support for entrepreneurship, while the Auyl party is advocating for stronger rural communities and the Baytaq Green Party is campaigning on the environment.
Kazakh political analyst Rustam Burnashev told Reuters that while this snap election offers Tokayev a chance to remove figures associated with his predecessor, Nazarbayev, from the political stage, major reform of the political system is unlikely.
Despite the new Adilet party having been formed to distance itself from Nazarbayev’s legacy, analysts say little is likely to change materially.
“All the parliamentary candidates are known,” Burnashev said. “Nor can one say that the parliament itself will be a transformative one.”
Although Kazakhstan has enjoyed rapid economic growth in recent years, tax rises and inflation have hit living standards.
Atapsha, a fruit seller who declined to give his full name, told Reuters that he would cast a vote, but without any particular expectations.
“I am 73 years old. I’ve been waiting for things to get better for 73 years, but so far, nothing has really worked out. Still, I hope that this year things will finally improve.”
What’s at stake?
In 2022, Tokayev launched the “New Kazakhstan” package of reforms for the political system. A referendum was held on the legislative changes, which came in in July.
Analysts say the upcoming elections will determine if the country’s new leaders can adhere to the renewed unicameral legislature and uphold its foreign policy.
Besides these changes in the country’s legislative makeup, the elections come at a time when Astana is trying to showcase itself as a democracy and key power in Central Asia.
To this end, Tokayev has focused on revamping the country’s infrastructure and economy and expanding ties with both China and the European Union.
The country has also been beefing up relations with the United States in recent years. Last November, Kazakhstan signed a $4.2bn agreement with the US locomotive parts maker Wabtec. According to the US Department of Commerce, the deal will provide Kazakhstan with 300 kits to build locomotives for the Kazakh national rail company, Kazakhstan Temir Zholy.
US President Donald Trump took to Truth Social to trumpet the deal, referring to it as “the largest Railroad Equipment Purchase in History”.
Traditionally close to Russia, the country has preferred to play a neutral role in Moscow’s war on Ukraine and has called for peace. It has also offered itself as a venue for peace talks in the US-Iran war.
In an article published in April by the Belfer Center for Science and International Affairs at Harvard Kennedy School, Nargis Kassenova wrote: “Kazakhstan has begun positioning itself as a middle power.”
According to the Bureau of National Statistics, Kazakhstan’s gross domestic product (GDP) increased by 6.5 percent to about US$335bn in 2025 compared with last year, using the consumption method of calculations.
“While a ‘lightweight’ by conventional standards, it has assets that make it significant for the rest of the world. Its geostrategic location at the heart of Eurasia makes it both an important connector and buffer between Europe, Russia, the Middle East, South Asia, and East Asia. It is also a regional leader in Central Asia,” she wrote.
Oil-rich Kazakhstan accounts for about 2 percent of the daily world oil supply, with the bulk of its exports shipped to European countries via the Caspian Pipeline Consortium to Russia’s port of Novorossiysk. The pipeline and tankers serving it have periodically come under attack by Ukrainian drones, causing disruptions in exports.

title: Washington pushes ‘America First’ agenda in Apec talks ahead of Chinese leader’s visit
summary:
The United States has pledged to take an “America First” approach to the latest round of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation talks, which are taking place in China weeks before President Xi Jinping’s visit to America.
The US State Department said: “US leadership in Apec is a key dimension to pursuing America First policies that foster prosperity and advance economic growth in the United States and across the region by breaking down barriers for US business, boosting fair and reciprocal trade and...
full_text:
Washington pushes ‘America First’ agenda in Apec talks ahead of Chinese leader’s visit
Washington says it wants to ‘break down barriers’ for its companies in talks being held in the run-up to Xi Jinping’s visit next month
The US State Department said: “US leadership in Apec is a key dimension to pursuing America First policies that foster prosperity and advance economic growth in the United States and across the region by breaking down barriers for US business, boosting fair and reciprocal trade and supporting American job growth.”
It added that the delegates, led by Casey Mace, the senior official for Apec affairs, would seek to create more opportunities for American businesses in fields such as agriculture and fisheries, energy, transport, health and food security.
The US also pledged to push to boost services exports and supply-chain innovation, as well as leading discussions on trade and labour-related matters.
Earlier this year, Xi hosted his US counterpart Donald Trump in Beijing, a trip that resulted in plans for US-China boards of trade and investment, although the latter has yet to get off the ground.
The meeting of Apec senior officials is the third of its kind this year and the largest yet, according to China’s foreign ministry.

title: 區塊鏈協會嗆聲銀行公會：「改幾個字」實為拖死 Clarity Act 的障眼法
summary:
參議院 9 月 15 日將就 Clarity Act 程式投票，需 60 票過關，而銀行公會在此刻主張「小幅修 […]

〈區塊鏈協會嗆聲銀行公會：「改幾個字」實為拖死 Clarity Act 的障眼法〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
參議院 9 月 15 日將就 Clarity Act 程式投票，需 60 票過關，而銀行公會在此刻主張「小幅修改」已協商的條款。區塊鏈協會執行長 Mersinger 反批這是拖延殺法案：兩處改動（實質相似標準、刪除 solely）都會根本改變法案內容，並以 FDIC 資料反駁存款流失疑慮。
（前情提要：重磅！美國 Clarity Act 清晰度法案成功透過參議院銀行委員會！下一步將送全院表決）
（背景補充：美國 Clarity Act 清晰度法案迎關鍵四週，川普「百億加密收入」成通關阻礙）
美國銀行家協會（ABA）執行長 Rob Nichols 日前投書強調，美國銀產業「想強化 Clarity Act、而不是扼殺它」。但區塊鏈協會執行長、前美國商品期貨交易委員會（CFTC）委員 Summer Mersinger 隨即公開反擊：銀行公會口中的「幾處文字修改」實為重大政策變更，此刻重開協商只會拖死法案。
她在投書中直言，這齣「討論」只是以拖延來殺死立法的障眼法。
九月中程式投票：60 票門檻與緊縮的立法院曆
Mersinger 點出時間壓力：9 月 15 日參議院將表決是否就 Clarity Act 展開辯論，需要 60 位參議員同意；隨後在秋季支出法案大戰席捲議程、期中選舉立法視窗關閉前，參院只剩不到三個完整工作週。
她強調，銀行公會要求重開的條款已協商數月，談判期間公會代表全程在場，重開協商不會讓法案更好，只會重啟一場沒人有時間收尾的談判。
- 9/15 程式投票需 60 票才能進入辯論
- 投票後到期中選舉前的立法視窗不到三週
- 重開條款協商被質疑是「以討論之名行拖延之實」
「實質相似」與「solely」：兩個字改動都是真政策變更
Nichols 把 ABA 兩項主張包裝成「小幅修改」：一是將法案現行標準替換為「實質相似」（substantially similar），二是刪除「solely」一字。Mersinger 認為兩者皆非小事。
「實質相似於利息」是具彈性的法律標準，監管者若有意，幾乎可把任何回饋客戶經濟價值的計畫都解釋成「實質相似於利息」。銀行自己就經營這類計畫，包括隨消費金額攀升的現金回饋、按帳戶餘額分級的忠誠度方案，沒有一家銀行會接受自家獎勵機制被這句話綁架。
「solely」則出自 GENIUS Act，該法禁止發行方「solely 基於持有、使用或留存」穩定幣而支付收益，這個字把禁令限定在「只為持有幣本身」的獎勵。刪除後，條款將擴及國會刻意排除在外的行為，直接改變法案實際作用範圍。
存款流失證據戰：FDIC 資料打臉銀行說法
Nichols 主張 GENIUS 透過後未見存款外逃、因此「無關緊要」，理由是監管尚未完全落地。Mersinger 反批：這是要求參議員根據預測行事、卻忽視目前唯一真實世界的資料。最新FDIC 資料顯示，GENIUS 生效後美國存款每一季都成長，法案上路以來三個完整季度，國內銀行存款增加逾 8,000 億美元。如果相反的證據永遠能被一句「言之過早」打發，就沒有任何證據能定案，末日預測將自動勝出。
真正與存款競爭的對手與加密無關：貨幣市場基金靠支付儲戶真實且具市場競爭力的報酬，吸走數兆美元資金。銀行通常以調升自身利率回應，從未要求國會限制貨幣市場基金能提供的收益上限。
消費者保護的真義：穩定幣有防線，平台卻沒有
穩定幣雖不受 FDIC 存款保險保障，GENIUS 仍為持有人設下防線：要求一比一準備金（現金與短天期公債）、禁止挪用準備金放貸、要求執行長與財務長認證的每月揭露，並在發行方倒閉時賦予持有人對準備金的優先受償權。
但美國有 6,700 萬人持有數位資產，穩定幣以外的領域，目前沒有任何聯邦框架要求平台把客戶資產與自有資金隔離、揭露財務狀況、或禁止與客戶對做。Clarity Act 將這些標準寫入法律：畫出 SEC 與 CFTC 的管轄界線、要求服務美國客戶的平台註冊、強制客戶資產隔離，並訂定揭露與利益衝突規則。
Mersinger 提醒，ABA 的修正案不會保護消費者免受任何現行條文未涵蓋的風險，反而會移除消費者眼前的選項；真正保護消費者的條款就在同一部法案裡，等著同一場投票。
市場影響與後續觀察
Clarity Act 的成敗牽動的不只是美國，亞洲多國也在觀察美國聯邦框架的最終樣貌；若 9 月程式投票失敗，加密監管的全球風向球將再度懸空，業者只能繼續面對州級碎片化監管。對穩定幣發行商而言，GENIUS 的準備金、揭露與優先受償設計已成為事實標準，無論 Clarity Act 走向如何，這套規範很可能被各國立法者直接引用。
後續觀察重點：一是 9/15 程式投票能否跨過 60 票門檻；二是 ABA 是否收斂「重開協商」訴求；三是若法案延宕，CFTC 是否會如過去那樣以自身規則填補立法空窗。

title: 比特幣多空論戰！機構樂觀看漲，為何 Peter Schiff 堅稱是「假突破」？
summary:
比特幣重返 7.5 萬美元、創 6 月以來高點，資金與市場情緒同步回溫；不過 Peter Schiff 認為，美國財政部回購帶來的利多被市場高估，這波可能只是「假突破」。

〈比特幣多空論戰！機構樂觀看漲，為何 Peter Schiff 堅稱是「假突破」？〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
作者：Fenrir，加密城市
比特幣一度突破 7.5 萬美元，24 小時漲逾 7％
比特幣本週強勢反彈，8 月 21 日上午一度突破 7.5 萬美元，最高來到約 75,528 美元。根據 CoinGecko 數據，截至上午 10 時左右，比特幣價格約報 74,784 美元，過去 24 小時上漲約 7.3％，期間價格介於 68,898 美元至 75,528 美元之間，短時間內大幅拉升逾 6,000 美元，創下 6 月以來高點。
這波急漲同步引爆大規模空頭清算。 CoinGlass 數據顯示，過去 24 小時全球加密貨幣市場共有 136,825 名交易者遭到爆倉，總清算金額約 12.3 億美元，其中空單爆倉約 10.5 億美元，多單則約 1.81 億美元，顯示這波行情對空方形成明顯擠壓。單以比特幣計算，24 小時爆倉金額就達約 7.84 億美元，以太幣則約 2.18 億美元；期間最大單筆爆倉發生於 Hyperliquid 的 BTC-USD 部位，價值約 2,513 萬美元。
ETF 資金回流，機構看好流動性改善
現貨市場也出現部分正面訊號。美國現貨比特幣 ETF 單日淨流入約 5.17 億美元，創逾 3 個月最大規模，其中貝萊德（BlackRock）旗下 IBIT 貢獻約 2.85 億美元。 Bitwise 研究分析師 Ishmael Asad 認為，這次上漲是目前最明確的築底訊號之一，財政部擴大公債回購、美國證券交易委員會提出新的加密資產監管架構，以及白宮近期推動加密政策，都有助於改善市場預期。
Risk Dimensions 投資長 Mark Connors 的看法更為積極。他認為，若美國財政部未來每月公債回購規模由目前的 40 億美元進一步增加至 100 億至 300 億美元，可望壓低長期債券殖利率，降低資金流向公債對比特幣形成的排擠效果。 Connors 將比特幣下一個重要目標設定在 18 萬美元，並預估至 2030 年的週期目標區間可能落在 18 萬至 36 萬美元。
多頭看 7.6 萬美元，跌破支撐恐重返 5 萬美元
技術面同樣出現明顯分歧。資深交易員 Peter Brandt 認為，比特幣完成底部型態後，原先偏空的市場結構已經改變，若站穩關鍵突破位置，下一階段可能挑戰 7.6 萬美元。隨著比特幣最高已來到約 75,528 美元，距離這項目標僅剩不到 500 美元。不過，相關技術模型也顯示，一旦突破失敗，價格可能重新回測約 5.3 萬美元，甚至讓市場再次討論 5 萬美元關卡。
Nansen 資深研究分析師 Nicolai Sondergaard 則將 6.9 萬美元附近的 200 日均線視為重要分水嶺。目前比特幣已重新站上該均線，MACD 動能指標也轉為偏多，但若價格重新跌破 6.9 萬美元，這次突破的可信度將明顯下降。 CryptoQuant 同樣保持謹慎，其牛熊指標尚未轉為多頭，比特幣約 8.3 萬美元的 365 日均線仍是更高層級的確認門檻。
彼得希夫唱反調，直指這波上漲是假突破
市場情緒快速轉暖之際，長期批評比特幣的經濟學家彼得希夫（Peter Schiff）再度站上空方。他在比特幣突破 7.2 萬美元後，將這波行情形容為「假突破」，認為財政部擴大公債回購改變市場對流動性的預期，短期刺激風險資產上漲，但投資人高估了寬鬆金融環境對比特幣的長期效果。
希夫認為，貨幣與財政環境轉向寬鬆確實有利於黃金，但比特幣未必能獲得相同且持續的支撐，因此再次公開呼籲投資人出售比特幣、轉向黃金。目前比特幣已進一步站上 7.4 萬美元，甚至突破 7.5 萬美元，使多空雙方對這次突破是否具有延續性的爭論更加激烈。 ETF 資金流向、現貨市場買盤，以及大規模空頭回補結束後能否承接目前價格，將成為後續行情的重要觀察指標。
（以上內容獲合作夥伴《加密城市》授權節錄及轉載，原文連結 ）

title: Infantino defies FIFA vice president, makes appearance in the Caribbean
summary: FIFA boss turns up at event after CONCACAF chief Montagliani asked him to reconsider amid the body’s governance crisis.
full_text:
Infantino defies FIFA vice president, makes appearance in the Caribbean
FIFA boss turns up at event after CONCACAF chief Montagliani asked him to reconsider amid the global football body’s governance crisis.
Gianni Infantino has defied a request by one of his FIFA vice presidents to stay away from an Under-14 football event in the Caribbean and instead made a rare public appearance during the global furore over his failed plan to sell future World Cup profits to private investors.
The FIFA president posted photos on his Instagram account on Saturday, showing his meeting with political and football officials from the Dominican Republic on the sidelines of a Caribbean Football Union (CFU) youth tournament in the Punta Cana resort.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4Mohamed Salah’s Trabzonspor debut ends in draw with Kasimpasa
- list 2 of 4Rights group urges FIFA to block Infantino re-election bid over term limits
- list 3 of 4WAFCON: Cameroon beat tournament debutants Malawi to win maiden title
- list 4 of 4FIFA President Gianni Infantino denies claims UEFA paid off alleged lover
On Friday, Infantino had been asked not to go by Victor Montagliani, the Canadian president of the Miami-based Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football (CONCACAF), to avoid being a distraction from the football games.
“I believe that considering the governance crisis surrounding FIFA as a result of your controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal, the media will focus on this situation,” Montagliani wrote in an emailed letter seen by The Associated Press news agency, “which will unfortunately significantly take away from the technical nature of the CFU youth competition.”
“As such, I respectfully ask you in the name of football to reconsider your attendance as it will unfortunately undermine the technical nature of this important youth development activity,” Montagliani wrote.
FIFA declined to comment on Montagliani’s request, though it noted that it directly funds regional bodies like the CFU with up to $5m from each four-year World Cup cycle.
Montagliani has aligned with fellow FIFA vice presidents Aleksander Ceferin from European body UEFA and Asian Football Confederation president Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa in seeking to end Infantino’s increasingly executive presidency, now in its 11th year.
They accused Infantino two weeks ago of “deception” in secretly planning over the past year to spin off FIFA’s multibillion-dollar commercial activities to a subsidiary 20 percent owned by investors led by Joshua Kushner, the younger brother of United States President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.
Infantino withdrew the project on August 1 amid a global backlash by football leaders and fans, and hours after his own chief operating officer published stinging criticism of the proposal and his leadership style in a statement to the AP. The Zurich-based COO, Kevin Lamour, was fired last week.
Caribbean member federations are seen as potential supporters for Infantino to peel away from their CONCACAF leadership. South American body CONMEBOL has backed Infantino as its best path to hosting more games at the 2030 World Cup it wants expanded from 48 teams to 64.
The FIFA leader has not taken questions publicly since the $20bn FFE project was revealed on July 28 by British daily The Times, and on Friday in Punta Cana he evaded a reporter from British broadcaster Sky News.
Asked by Sky reporter James Matthews whether he had betrayed the sport and should resign, Infantino said, “Thank you so much”, and made quips about both men being bald.
Infantino is aiming to be re-elected for a fourth and final term in office through 2031 at the FIFA election congress next March in Rabat, Morocco. FIFA has set a November 18 deadline for would-be candidates to enter the race.

title: Serena Williams teams up with Carlos Alcaraz in US Open mixed doubles
summary: The 23-time Grand Slam champion will not be playing singles, but could team up with her older sister Venus for doubles.
full_text:
Serena Williams teams up with Carlos Alcaraz in US Open mixed doubles
The 23-time Grand Slam champion will not be playing singles, but could team up with her older sister Venus for doubles.
Serena Williams will team up with Carlos Alcaraz to create a powerhouse mixed doubles pair on her return to the US Open.
The US Tennis Association announced on Saturday that Williams and Alcaraz had been given a wild card into the tournament. The mixed doubles main draw begins on Tuesday, with the winning team sharing $1 million.
