title: What will it take to stop the England hangovers?
summary: Yet again, England are dealing with a player involved in a late-night incident. Only strong action will ensure there are no more, writes Stephan Shemilt.
full_text:
What will it take to stop the England hangovers?
- Published
Yet again, the England men's cricket team is picking through the wreckage of a late-night misdemeanour.
The latest stain on the game's reputation is a result of pictures of fast bowler Brydon Carse in handcuffs and surrounded by police officers outside a nightspot in Derby. His Durham team-mate Matthew Potts is in the images, while former England captain Ben Stokes appears in the background.
If you're keeping score, we're now up to eight England players involved in incidents of this kind since Halloween last year.
Harry Brook was punched by a nightclub bouncer in Wellington, with Jacob Bethell and Josh Tongue present. Ben Duckett was filmed drunk in Noosa, then Stokes and Gus Atkinson were there when a member of England's security staff was struck in a London nightclub in June, breaching a curfew in the process.
To put it another way, there are 30 men currently on England central contracts. More than a quarter of them have been caught up in bother in the past 10 months. Of the four separate incidents, two have involved punches being thrown and another was a police matter.
In Carse's case, the time spent in handcuffs came days after new England Test captain Joe Root called on his players to be "really good role models, good human beings".
Root was speaking the day before England's first Test against Pakistan, for which Carse was part of the squad. The match was scheduled to still be ongoing when he found himself in the hands of the police.
It is understood that Carse was not arrested. Both the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) and the Cricket Regulator will work to establish what happened. There are early suggestions he was denied entry back into a nightclub, or he had a drink poured over him.
Carse was also not specifically on England duty at the time. He was released from the first-Test squad to play for Durham away at Derbyshire and was scheduled to report to Lord's for the second Test on Monday.
As of Sunday evening, he remains part of the squad for the second Test. England will take time to gather some information before a decision on his involvement is made.
Root warned his squad to "be adults" when he abolished the midnight curfew - in his first act as captain - that came into place after previous incidents. As part of that move, guidelines advising players about not drinking alcohol on the day before, during or after a game, or in public, have also been removed.
There is a duty of care towards Carse. Two years ago, the 31-year-old was banned for historical betting offences and rebuilt his career to become an England regular in all three formats. No bowler has more Test wickets for England than Carse's 58 since he made his debut in October 2024.
But there is also a deep sense of anger and frustration within the ECB at having to deal with another error of judgement by a high-profile player. Supporters will take their own view, among them a sense that the behaviour of these players is now beyond parody.
Does someone have to be left out of a squad or given a meaty suspension for the penny to drop? This might be the opportunity for Root to stamp his authority on a new era.
Naturally, there will once again be the debate about not denying players their freedom or stopping them from enjoying a victory.
For Carse, a Saturday night out came less than 48 hours before he is scheduled to report for England. He is only a tweaked hamstring away from playing in a Test at Lord's on Thursday.
Perhaps more damning is the kind of trouble this group of England players seem to find. Two punch-ups and a set of handcuffs. It also does not appear to have dawned on them that they are high-profile individuals, likely to attract attention, with footage finding its way to social media, as happened with Carse.
And what about Stokes, who, despite being retired, remains an employee of the ECB via his central contract.
As the former captain, should Stokes have been conscious about Carse being in that situation? What about the trouble in which Atkinson found himself alongside Stokes in June?
Three weeks ago, Stokes denied the England team has a drinking culture, but rather that the game itself has a problem. What has Stokes done to distance himself or those around him from that drinking culture?
Now there is a wait to see what happens next. The ECB only became aware of the incident on Sunday afternoon. The governing body will take a breath overnight and decide if Carse needs to be removed from the Test squad.
Perhaps, on Tuesday, director of cricket Rob Key will once again explain why the players he manages cannot keep themselves out of trouble. In the aftermath of the Stokes-Atkinson incident in June, Key denied that England have become a "national embarrassment". He may be asked again.
Key also might be asked about the whereabouts of new Test coach Stephen Fleming, who does not take up his post until the winter. Might Carse have been less inclined to step out of line had the new sheriff been in town?
Well, here is another situation for England to manage. Only strong action will ensure there are no more.

title: Raphinha and Lopez score braces as Barcelona trounce Elche 5-0
summary: Barcelona ‌begin their La Liga title ⁠defence ⁠and bid for a third successive crown with a 5-0 ⁠victory at Elche.
full_text:
Raphinha and Lopez score braces as Barcelona trounce Elche 5-0
Barcelona begin their La Liga title defence and bid for a third successive crown with a 5-0 victory at Elche.
Spanish champions Barcelona have cruised to a 5-0 win over Elche in their La Liga opener, with Raphinha and Fermin Lopez scoring twice each and Anthony Gordon setting up two goals on his debut.
After watching Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid defeat Espanyol 2-1 on Saturday with a late winner, Barca’s display on Sunday warned the Portuguese coach that the Catalans will not relinquish the title easily.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4Squad, formation, unrest: Key talking points ahead of Chelsea’s new season
- list 2 of 4Man Utd humiliated at Hull to open Premier League account
- list 3 of 4Fans and police injured in pitch invasion during ‘high risk’ German Cup tie
- list 4 of 4Arsenal rout Coventry 3-0 to begin Premier League title defence in style
Karim Adeyemi also found the net on his debut as Barca made light work of a vulnerable Elche side at Martinez Valero Stadium.
Hansi Flick started with several regular starters on the bench as they continue to get up to speed following the World Cup.
Teenage winger Lamine Yamal, a key part of the triumphant World Cup Spain squad, did start on the right but was far from his best, though it did not matter given Barca’s otherwise sparkling display.
Raphinha was cut down in the box by Victor Chust and stroked home the resulting penalty after 14 minutes to get Flick’s team on their way.
Eric Garcia was sharp at the back to ward off a threatening Elche attack, while Barca’s Gavi caught the eye in midfield – admittedly more for his pink haircut to celebrate Spain’s triumph than for his performance.
Rapid winger Adeyemi, playing on the left, started shakily but grew into the game and doubled Barca’s lead before the break after Raphinha unselfishly set him up.
In the second half, former Newcastle United winger Gordon, on as a substitute, teed up Raphinha for his second, and then supplied Lopez for Barca’s fourth in an electric and impressive cameo.
Youngster Xavi Espart played in Lopez, who endured a difficult summer after missing Spain’s World Cup triumph through injury, for his second to seal Barcelona’s comfortable triumph.
Flick’s high-line defence showed the occasional sign of its usual frailty, but goalkeeper Joan Garcia did well when called on to keep a clean sheet.
Raphinha told reporters after the game that “whether a game is easy or hard depends on us.
“If we start playing at the maximum level, we’re likely to win. It was a very tough game, but we did our job.”

title: US envoy Tom Barrack retracts comment that Syria’s Golan is occupied
summary: Ambassador to Turkiye says US policy of recognising Israel's claimed sovereignty over Syrian territory is 'unchanged'.
full_text:
US envoy Tom Barrack retracts comment that Syria’s Golan is occupied
Ambassador to Turkiye says US policy of recognising Israel’s claimed sovereignty over Syrian territory is ‘unchanged’.
United States Ambassador Tom Barrack has reasserted Washington’s position that Syria’s Golan Heights belongs to Israel after saying last week that the territory is occupied against “all of the international order”.
US President Donald Trump’s ambassador to Turkiye and envoy for Syria walked back that comment on Sunday, underscoring Trump’s policy of recognising Israel’s claimed sovereignty over the stretch of land in southern Syria.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3Trump has ‘run out of options’ in Iran war: Stephen Walt
- list 2 of 3Palestinian teen killed in Israeli raid buried in Occupied West Bank
- list 3 of 3Gaza’s hospitals are running out of oxygen as healthcare nears collapse
“United States policy on the Golan was set by President Trump in 2019 and is unchanged,” he told The Associated Press news agency in a statement.
Israel occupied the Golan during the 1967 Six-Day War and annexed the territory in 1981.
Until Trump backed the Israeli claim to the Syrian territory, no country had recognised the Golan as part of Israel.
The recognition sparked an international outcry. Legal experts warned that it could upend a core tenet of the post-World War II global order: the prohibition on acquiring land by force.
Former US President Joe Biden promoted the so-called rules-based order early in his tenure, but he failed to reverse Trump’s policy on the Golan during his four-year term.
Recently, Colombia’s right-wing government joined the US in backing Israel’s claim on the Golan.
In an interview with podcaster Mario Nawfal on Friday, Barrack appeared to acknowledge that the Golan is occupied Syrian land.
Barrack was asked whether Israel has plans to annex parts of southern Lebanon. He said regardless of intent, Israel knows that it would be difficult to claim Lebanese territory as its own.
“Saying that, in the Golan with Syria, they still occupy the Golan against the UN resolutions, against all of the international order, which has said the Golan is Syria’s,” Barrack said.
Israel’s advocates were quick to criticise Barrack’s comment. Far-right commentator Laura Loomer called on the envoy to step down.
“He should resign for his lack of understanding of US foreign policy,” she wrote in a social media post, sharing Trump’s 2019 proclamation saying that the Golan belongs to Israel.
Republican Senator Rick Scott also criticised the ambassador, saying Barrack was confirmed by the Senate to enact Trump’s agenda.
“It seems the Ambassador forgot that or failed to do his research, so here’s a refresher for him,” Scott wrote in a social media post that included Trump’s executive order on the Golan Heights.
“President Trump has been CLEAR about Israel’s sovereignty over the Golan Heights for years!”
Barrack had also been criticised for opposing Israeli air strikes on a Syrian airbase last week.
In his interview with Nawfal, Barrack suggested that the Israeli strikes in Syria were aimed at antagonising Turkiye, which is allied with the Syrian government.
“One theory is they were just baiting Turkiye, and it’s a very aggressive, but maybe well-received pre-election concept,” Barrack said, referring to US midterm elections in November.

title: How easy is it to find an NHS dentist? It depends where you live
summary: Nearly 600 practices in England have withdrawn from NHS dentistry over the last 10 years, as the service heads towards a two-tier system.
full_text:
How easy is it to find an NHS dentist? It depends where you live
- Published
Hundreds of dentist practices are abandoning NHS work as the service drifts towards a two-tier system, new analysis suggests.
Data analysed by the Nuffield Trust found that nearly 600 practices in England have withdrawn from NHS dentistry over the last 10 years. The decline has been particularly sharp in parts of the South West and East of England, raising concerns about growing inequalities in access to care.
The analysis suggests more than one in 10 dental practices that once offered NHS care no longer do so, leaving it near impossible for some communities to find NHS appointments.
NHS dental activity is 8% lower than it was pre Covid, while six in 10 adults have not seen an NHS dentist in two years. Of those who attempted to get a new appointment in the last two years, just 38% were successful, according to a Nuffield Trust Survey.
Cornwall, Devon and Northamptonshire have seen some of the biggest reductions in the number of practices offering NHS care. In Cornwall, more than a quarter of practices that previously offered NHS treatment have stopped doing so, making it one of the starkest examples of the shift away from NHS dentistry.
The findings come as ministers have pledged to tackle so-called "dental deserts", but dentists say the current deal is not viable. Many have handed back their NHS contracts because to work is loss-making.
In Somerset, fewer than one in five dental practices now offers NHS services. Alan, 83, who lives in the county, says he has given up trying to find an NHS dentist.
"I used to try, but getting a dental appointment anywhere near where I live would be impossible," he says.
Alan has only one tooth remaining after the others "crumbled out over the years" and says he has had to adapt what he eats, although he jokes that he has perfected a way of eating Brazil nuts.
Vivak Shah, who runs three dental practices in Northamptonshire, continues to offer NHS treatment but says it operates at a loss. He no longer takes on new NHS patients.
"Each year we struggle to decide what to do, and there is a limit to how much the private side can cover the NHS losses," says Shah.
He warned that if practices stop providing NHS treatment, many patients could be left in pain or forced to seek help elsewhere in the health service, including hospital accident and emergency departments.
"A contract handed back in one town attracts little national attention on its own but repeated across the country for a decade it amounts to the quiet transformation of dentistry into a two-tier service," says Mark Dayan, head of public affairs at the Nuffield Trust.
"Access to dental care increasingly depends on what people can afford to pay and where they live."
Jim Sykes is a dentist in Hexham. He handed back his NHS contract in 2024.
"It was a really hard emotional decision, but the NHS work was running at such a loss. I had to think of my team of staff and make it work," he says. Sykes asked if he could continue treating just children but was told he had to accept adults as well, or give up the NHS work.
"There has been a real breakdown in trust for me. Even if there was a new government offer, I would still be very nervous about entering a new NHS contract," he says.
Sykes says that none of his friends in his graduating class in dentistry still works in the NHS. "My friends have gone private, retired or teach - any pathway to avoid NHS dentistry."
Shiv Pabary, chair of the British Dental Association's General Dental Practice Committee, says the situation is "the direct result of choices made by successive governments". He warns that unless ministers "fix and fund NHS dentistry", more dentists could choose to reduce their NHS work or leave the service altogether.
Overall dentist practice numbers have risen in England over the last decade.
"This is not a shortage of dentistry but a shortage of NHS dentistry," says Dayan. "Practices will need to be incentivised back into NHS work in the places where the NHS footprint has thinned most."
While most parts of England recorded declines in practices offering NHS dental care, the reductions were smallest in North West London, the Black Country and North East London.
North East London was the only area to see any increase during the period, recording one additional practice offering NHS treatment compared with a decade ago.
Every other region of England saw the number of NHS dental practices fall.
Looking at the number of practices doing NHS work is not the same as looking at exactly how much health service capacity there is - practices can vary in size. But if you look at other measures such as the amount of treatment being done, the numbers are still down, although not as steep as the fall in practice numbers.
The government says that it is changing the dental contract and training more dentists in the areas most in need. The government says it will also make it a requirement for newly qualified dentists to practice in the NHS for a minimum period of at least three years.
Campaign group 38 degrees calls the current dental crisis "shameful", with people being "forced to pay money they can't afford or suffer with the pain, shame, and further complications that come from being denied vital NHS healthcare".
  - Published25 March

title: Burnham to visit Kyiv on first foreign trip and reaffirm UK support for Ukraine
summary: It comes after Moscow warned of "consequences" over the reported use of British drones by Ukraine.
full_text:
Burnham to visit Kyiv on first foreign trip and reaffirm UK support for Ukraine
- Published
Andy Burnham will mark his first foreign visit as prime minister with a trip to Kyiv on Monday to reiterate the UK's support for Ukraine and honour the country's independence day.
The prime minister will chair his first meeting of the "coalition of the willing", set up by the UK and France under his predecessor, Sir Keir Starmer.
He is also set to accept an award on behalf of the British people recognising the UK's support for Ukraine and to take part in independence day events.
Burnham will be reaffirming the UK's backing for Kyiv in the wake of escalating Russian strikes on Ukraine in recent weeks - including one on a shopping centre on Friday that killed at least 16 people.
Ahead of Monday's visit, Burnham said: "On Ukraine's 35th anniversary of independence, the Ukrainian people should be in no doubt: the UK is behind you today and for as long as it takes.
"I am proud of the contribution our country has made to Ukraine and I want the Ukrainian people to hear it directly from me that our support will not waver. After all, Ukraine's security is our security."
He said the friendship Ukraine shared with the UK would "long outlast Russia's illegal war", adding: "Russia should be in no doubt of our resolve. We will not back down until there is a just and lasting peace."
It comes after Moscow warned of "consequences" over the use of British drones by Ukraine in its recent ramping up of strikes on Russian infrastructure.
Kyiv has stepped up long-range attacks on Moscow and other Russian regions, targeting oil refineries and warehouses of the country's largest online retailer, Wildberries.
The Russian embassy in the UK has accused Britain of "deliberately opting for an escalation of the Ukraine crisis", saying "the deeper its involvement in the conflict... the higher the price it will pay".
In response, Burnham said last week: "We are not fair-weather friends, we will be there in Ukraine's hour of need and that won't change."
Asked on Tuesday about the Russian threat, Burnham maintained the UK was "providing support so that Ukraine can defend itself and that's been the British position all the way through this conflict, by previous prime ministers - it remains the case with me".
Burnham is also set to announce that the government has agreed to allow defence company MBDA to declassify information on UK components for the long-range Scalp missile – the French equivalent of the UK's Storm Shadow.
Both missiles use shared British and French technology, and President Emmanuel Macron is looking at setting up local assembly lines for Scalp missiles in Ukraine.
Zelensky was the first foreign leader to be welcomed to Downing Street after Burnham became prime minister in July.
The visit comes as Russia confirmed its ambassador to the UK, Andrei Kelin, had left his post in London in recent weeks.
The Kremlin is yet to put forward a replacement but Russia's embassy to the UK told the BBC it did not reflect an intention to downgrade diplomatic relations between the two nations.

title: Doctors said I was too young to have endometriosis at 13 - I had to take morphine to cope
summary: Grace, 14, feels doctors were dismissive of her pain. She wants others to know the symptoms.
full_text:
Doctors said I was too young to have endometriosis at 13 - I had to take morphine to cope
- Published
Every month, at about the time of her period, Grace has to be taken to hospital.
She is often in so much pain her parents have to carry her to the car. She can wait hours to be seen in A&E, only to be sent home in tears with more strong painkillers.
For a long time, Grace - who's now 14 and is from Yorkshire - felt doctors were dismissive of her pain. "I feel like I was seen as a girl who didn't want to go to school and was being dramatic," she says.
She was given multiple possible reasons for her symptoms: irritable bowel syndrome, a cyst, anxiety and "just a bad period". But, she says, "I knew it was more than that."
Doctors told her time and again that it could not be endometriosis - an incurable condition causing lesions and scarring on internal organs and around the body, external - because she was too young. Grace says her requests for further investigation were ignored.
'It's like heated barbed wire around my abdomen'
Grace's periods began when she was 11, and by 13, she was having excruciating pains around the time of menstruation. She describes it as if "heated barbed wire" were wrapped around her abdomen: "It's like my organs are being pulled apart."
She is often bedbound and, whenever she has exhausted the painkillers she has at home, she has to go in to hospital, where she is regularly given morphine. She has also been given co-codamol and tramadol.
Dependency on strong drugs like opioids worries her. "It's scary," she says, "because I don't want to have to rely on them for the rest of my life."
But the most frustrating thing for Grace, and why she contacted BBC Your Voice, is because she does not feel medical experts recognise that teenagers and adolescents can suffer from endometriosis.
Grace's GP did not diagnose her condition and nor did the first consultant she saw privately.
She says: "Even a specialist didn't believe me. And if a specialist won't listen to me, who will?" It was not until the family pushed for a second private opinion that she got a positive diagnosis.
Endometriosis, which occurs when tissue similar to the lining of the womb grows outside it, can cause debilitating symptoms, such as pelvic pain, heavy periods and fatigue. About 10% of women are affected by it, according to NHS data.
It can develop at any age once periods begin - and it is a common misconception that only older women suffer from the condition, says the charity Endometriosis UK,
Faye Farthing, a spokesperson for the charity, says the government, NHS and health practitioners need to improve menstrual health education for young people "if we are to ensure the next generation are not robbed of the future they deserve".
The charity says it can take a long time to diagnose endometriosis - an average of nine years in older women.
And in the early stages, for example with teenagers, it often doesn't show up on an ultrasound scan. However, new tests are being developed which will help spot the condition earlier.
Getting pregnant can be more difficult - even aged 14, Grace says she has been warned it is likely to affect her fertility. She's been advised she may not be able to have children after the age of 30 because of damage to her reproductive organs.
She feels rushed: "I have to have kids within the next 15 years, otherwise I might not be able to."
Paediatric gynaecologist Dr Gail Busby says nearly 80% of adolescents will have painful periods, but clinicians should recognise when a patient's symptoms are not normal - like missing school, missing PE every month or not going out with friends.
She says: "When you're in bed and your best friend is a hot water bottle - that's not normal."
Grace's case, showing symptoms at the age of 13, is not unusual, says Dr Busby, who sees girls both younger and older than Grace at her clinics. As well as her NHS work, she has opened a private adolescent endometriosis clinic in Manchester.
The impact of symptoms is not just physical. Girls like Grace are more likely to suffer with anxiety or depression because their pain affects what is an important time for educational, emotional and social development.
"We should enjoy adolescence," Dr Busby says, "but they can't do what they enjoy doing, what their peers are enjoying doing."
There is a history of endometriosis in Grace's family, but her mum Samantha says that did not make it any easier to get a diagnosis.
"When your child's on the floor in pain, it's very clear it's not just a bad period. But professionals say 'Oh we'll just put you on the pill for six months and see see how we go.'"
Grace has recently had a laparoscopy - keyhole surgery - to remove her endometriosis.
She hopes the procedure will help relieve her symptoms, at least temporarily. She has been advised to take a hormonal contraceptive to help slow monthly tissue growth and lessen the pain.
By speaking out, Grace hopes more teenagers will have the confidence to pursue a diagnosis. "I felt I was going crazy. That it was all in my head," she says. "But actually, you know your body best and your pain is real."
Related topics

title: Rumours swirled after a Vietnamese teen was run over - then came a stunning admission
summary: Confirmation of the circumstances around Do Ngoc Phuong Thuy's death have only spurred more questions.
full_text:
Rumours swirled after a Vietnamese teen was run over - then came a stunning admission
- Published
Until recently, there would have been little to distinguish Vietnam's so-called Justice Tree from the hundreds of others lining the streets of Hanoi. Then the bouquets started piling up.
It was here that former politician Nguyen Sy Cuong was driving his BMW in May last year when he veered into the opposite lane and smashed into a motorbike carrying a father and his teenage daughter.
The father, Do Viet Hung, suffered a broken leg but survived. The daughter, 18-year-old Do Ngoc Phuong Thuy, died in hospital 10 days after the collision which severed her right leg.
Fifteen months later, her death, and what many view as a suspicious silence surrounding it, has become a lightning rod for discontent among Vietnam's youth.
In early August, a legion of anonymous social media users started publishing millions of posts with the hashtags #NguyenSyCuong and #BMW across Facebook, Instagram, Threads and X. The users identified themselves as Gen Z – and they demanded accountability.
Initial discussions circled around whether the former politician was in fact the one who had caused the accident, and why authorities had only released sparse information.
Some pointed to reports that the driver of the BMW had the initials NSC and was born in 1961, leading to speculation that he was a former member of parliament. Others claimed the incident had been swept under the rug due to the influence of powerful figures. Many reported that their posts had been deleted by social media platforms at the request of the Vietnamese government – providing screenshots of notifications as evidence.
Expressions of outrage and calls for a proper investigation grew in number, volume and force.
Meanwhile, masked flower bearers started to appear, gravitating towards the scene of the incident and laying vibrant bouquets at the base of what has now been dubbed the Justice Tree. Police quickly arrived to get rid of the flowers, prompting mourners to create a virtual equivalent of the tree online - where hundreds of thousands of people have since sent tributes and paid respects.
Pressurised by more than a year's worth of growing suspicion and a rush of online attention, the issue had become too big to ignore.
Then, last Monday, the government made an extraordinary admission.
State broadcaster Vietnam Television (VTV) televised an official statement from authorities, confirming what had happened on the day of the incident. Former National Assembly deputy Nguyen Sy Cuong was indeed driving his car down Nguyen Huy Tu Street on 30 May, 2025, when his vehicle suddenly swerved across the road and into an oncoming motorcycle.
VTV cited police and prosecution sources who said that because Nguyen Sy Cuong "sincerely confessed and actively and fully remedied the consequences of his actions", Do Ngoc Phuong Thuy's family had submitted a petition to exempt him from prosecution. The report did not specify what form this remedy took, but Nguyen Sy Cuong was cleared of all criminal liability.
While such a decision is lawful under Vietnam's legislation, lawyers have questioned whether the criminal proceedings were conducted in accordance with due process – or conducted at all. Social media users have pointed out that Nguyen Sy Cuong is married to a minister in the current government, suggesting the pair may have wielded their influence to cover up the story. Some users have also cited other examples, including several fatal traffic incidents, when the law appears to have been applied differently.
Such online pressure had yielded results in the past.
In March this year, a 66-year-old man driving under the influence of alcohol in Hanoi collided with seven other cars and three motorcycles in a chain-reaction crash that killed one woman and seriously injured two others.
In the wake of that incident, it emerged that the driver, Nguyen Van Sau, was a retired police colonel who had previously served as deputy director of a department under the Ministry of Public Security. Fearing that authorities were actively erasing culpability, the victim's family appealed for help. Social media users in turn amplified the issue, and after three months Nguyen Van Sau was charged with "violating regulations on participation in road traffic".
- Who is To Lam, the ex-cop who wants to revamp Vietnam's success story? 
  - Published23 January
- British teen dies in reported Vietnam motorbike fall 
  - Published8 April
Many now feel that a similar groundswell may be the only way to deliver justice for the teenager who died last year. But their efforts have been met with friction.
Do Viet Hung, the teenager's father, appeared in VTV's broadcast to thank internet users for their sympathy, but said the family was satisfied with the investigation's findings, and asked people to leave them alone. Notably, he also warned people "not to be drawn into the influence of reactionary elements".
Also appearing in the broadcast was a senior police official, who similarly suggested that people were leveraging the incident to stoke dissent.
The Ministry of Public Security had "uncovered highly dangerous plots and intentions by hostile forces, reactionaries and bad actors to incite unrest and cause disorder", the official said.
"The ministry advises the public, especially young people, to remain fully alert and highly vigilant."
Similar rebukes have also started emerging on social media, with some claiming that conspiratorial forces were manipulating young people in Vietnam to stoke political discontent, manipulate public opinion online and rally people in real life ahead of the country's national holiday on 2 September.
Others have accused Gen Z Vietnamese of plotting a "colour revolution" – a term used to refer to mostly nonviolent protest movements that use specific colours or flowers as their symbol.
This is a familiar line of critique from Vietnamese authorities, who have previously labelled people's grievances or resentments as being untrue, unreasonable, or stemming from information fabricated by some "anti-government" or "reactionary" organisation.
Many in this case have said such accusations are baseless, insisting they are simply seeking justice for the victim of a fatal traffic accident. But the growing outrage has inevitably become a flashpoint amid broader, simmering grievances felt by Vietnam's youth.
Despite the Vietnamese government's tightening control over people's online freedom of expression – through measures ranging from intimidation and fines to criminal prosecution – public opinion in some corners has started to swerve against the Communist Party line.
On platforms such as Threads and Reddit, where anonymity is more normalised, many young people have expressed discontent towards various social issues: from the expansion of police power and land reclamation projects to exam cheating scandals and stricter regulation of online communication.
Such grievances echo those condemned by other Gen Z-led movements across the broader Asia region.
In countries like Bangladesh, India and Nepal, youth-led anti-government uprisings have over the past 12 months rallied immense support against the various pressure points of corruption, nepotism, economic inequality and democratic backsliding. Unofficially dubbed "the Asian Spring", the expanding influence of these movements has spread from Iran, Mongolia and the Maldives to the Philippines and Timor-Leste.
But protests in Vietnam have rarely, if ever, reached such fierce extremes. Vietnamese authorities have historically proven effective at detecting and stifling dissent before it boils over into action. Virtual places of mourning, anonymous social media posts, and online protests seem to be the most strident action many civilians here can afford to take.

title: Landslide at waste mound in Guinea capital kills 30, government says
summary:
Dump site in Conakry, which minister had just promised to move, collapsed after heavy rain in west African state

A ⁠landslide at a huge waste dump in Guinea’s capital has killed 30 people, the government said on Sunday, after heavy rains overnight prompted it to ⁠collapse, engulfing nearby tents and shacks.

The incident occurred less than a week after the government announced plans to close the ⁠site and relocate the waste because of the threat it posed, especially during the rainy season, which causes landslides and fatal flash ⁠floods each year in crowded, underdeveloped cities across parts of West Africa.

full_text:
A landslide at a huge waste dump in Guinea’s capital has killed 30 people, the government said on Sunday, after heavy rains overnight prompted it to collapse, engulfing nearby tents and shacks.
The incident occurred less than a week after the government announced plans to close the site and relocate the waste because of the threat it posed, especially during the rainy season, which causes landslides and fatal flash floods each year in crowded, underdeveloped cities across parts of West Africa.
The landslide took place at about 2am (3am UK time) in the Gbessia commune of Conakry, according to a government statement.
The death toll was 30, with six people seriously injured and 16 more lightly injured, the statement said.
Rescue workers were using excavators and other tools to clear the site of the landslide, which witnesses said was large enough to bury an apartment building along with more precarious dwellings.
One woman, Cire Diallo, told reporters at the scene that her five children were killed. “I have lost all my children. All I can do is put my trust in God,” she said.
Guinea holds the world’s largest bauxite reserves and richest untapped iron ore deposit at Simandou, where a massive mining project was launched in November. But the west African country has poor infrastructure and widespread poverty, with 3.7 million of its 15.1 million people living on less than $4.20 a day, according to a World Bank report published in April.
On Thursday Guinea’s minister of territorial administration, Djénabou Touré Camara, announced that the government was closing the landfill because it was unsafe and said the waste was to be relocated outside Conakry.
The prime minister, Amadou Oury Bah, visited the landfill on Sunday to assess the damage and supervise the response, the government statement said, adding that people should “remain calm, show solidarity, and strictly follow the instructions of rescue services and the competent authorities”.

title: Burnham to visit Ukraine with promise of boost for Kyiv’s long-range missiles
summary:
PM will use independence day trip to announce sharing of classified information about Storm Shadow components

Britain will boost Ukraine’s capacity to make its own long-range missiles, Andy Burnham will announce on Monday, as he travels to Kyiv for the country’s independence day on his first foreign visit as prime minister.

Burnham will arrive in the Ukrainian capital on Monday morning at a crucial time in the war, with Kyiv braced for another wave of Russian missile attacks and the country’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, facing his most direct domestic challenge.

Continue reading...
full_text:
Britain will boost Ukraine’s capacity to make its own long-range missiles, Andy Burnham will announce on Monday, as he travels to Kyiv for the country’s independence day on his first foreign visit as prime minister.
Burnham will arrive in the Ukrainian capital on Monday morning at a crucial time in the war, with Kyiv braced for another wave of Russian missile attacks and the country’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, facing his most direct domestic challenge.
The UK prime minister will use the trip to announce that the UK government will allow the European defence company MBDA to declassify information about UK-made components of the Anglo-French Storm Shadow/Scalp missiles to help Ukraine build its own version.
While the announcement will probably take years to have an impact on the war, it is likely to escalate tensions with Moscow at an already fraught moment in UK-Russian relations.
Burnham said in a statement on Sunday night: “On Ukraine’s 35th anniversary of independence, the Ukrainian people should be in no doubt: the UK is behind you today and for as long as it takes.
“I am proud of the contribution our country has made to Ukraine and I want the Ukrainian people to hear it directly from me that our support will not waver. After all, Ukraine’s security is our security.
“The friendship between our two countries will long outlast Russia’s illegal war. In both the fight and in the rebuilding to come, we will stand with Ukraine and deliver opportunities for people across both our countries.
“Russia should be in no doubt of our resolve. We will not back down until there is a just and lasting peace.”
Burnham will announce in Kyiv that the UK will help France set up assembly lines in Ukraine for long-range missiles, which the French president, Emmanuel Macron, promised last month.
Macron spoke to Zelenskyy on Saturday to promise to deliver separate interceptor missiles, which could help counter the recent barrage of high-speed Russian missile attacks on Kyiv.
Meanwhile, European leaders have condemned Friday’s drone attack on a busy shopping centre in central Ukraine, which killed 16 people in Zelenskyy’s home town of Kryvyi Rih.
The Ukrainian military has run out of US-made Patriot interceptors, and the US president, Donald Trump, recently backtracked on a promise to let Ukraine build its own.
However, Zelenskyy said over the weekend he still wanted to buy more US-made Patriots, adding that Ukraine was happy to pay for them rather than receive them as military aid. “I wanted to secure 300 Patriot missiles for the winter package,” he said. “The request from our air force is 360.”
He added that he had reached an agreement with France on at least one air-defence system this year, and with Germany on the supply of about 600 interceptors in 2027-28.
Macron posted on X on Saturday: “It is crucial to provide Ukraine with all the necessary means to defend its skies and thwart this aggression … It is essential that all countries with capabilities at their disposal also join this effort.”
The British announcement is a small step in a much larger and longer-term project that could lead to Ukraine making its own long-range versions of the Storm Shadow cruise missile in several years’ time.
But the move is likely to trigger further criticism from Moscow at a time when tensions between the UK and Russia are already high.
Last week, Russia accused the UK of deliberately escalating the conflict by allowing Ukraine to launch attacks with British-made drones, warning that the deeper Britain’s involvement, “the higher the price it will pay”.
This weekend it emerged that Russia had withdrawn its ambassador in London without naming a replacement, prompting speculation it was downgrading its diplomatic presence in the UK.
Burnham has insisted that Russian threats will not weaken British support for Ukraine, saying last week: “We are not fair-weather friends. We will be there in Ukraine’s hour of need, and that won’t change.”
The prime minister will on Monday use a meeting of the coalition of the willing, which comprises 34 countries that have promised to help secure Ukraine in the event of a peace deal with Russia, to underline that commitment.
The meeting will be co-chaired by Burnham and Macron, who will join remotely via video link. Friedrich Merz, the German chancellor, will also take part in the call as the leaders discuss ways to help Ukraine repel the recent wave of long-distance attacks.
While there, Burnham will attend independence day events, the details of which are being kept secret amid concerns of a major Russian attack, and receive an award in recognition of the UK’s support for Ukraine.
Zelenskyy is facing the most concerted internal political challenge of his presidency after the call for an election by his former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov.
The Ukrainian president responded to Fedorov’s dramatic announcement for the first time this weekend, telling reporters on Saturday that holding elections, which have been suspended since the war began, risked splitting the country.
“I believe that if we want to destroy the country, then during such a war we can move in the selection of elections,” he said in a briefing to selected journalists that was held on Saturday, but details of which were reported on Sunday.
“I believe that during such a war, elections in general are big risks. Elections right now are a tsunami for the state that will split Ukraine,” he added.

title: We are so back! Bitcoin’s 23% rally on US debt policy: Hodler’s Digest
summary: The US may face a debt crisis within three years according to Ray Dalio, and debt-related issues helped fuel a rally in Bitcoin that could mark the beginning of a new cycle.
full_text:
We are so back! Bitcoin’s 23% rally on US debt policy: Hodler’s Digest
The US may face a debt crisis within three years according to Ray Dalio, and debt-related issues helped fuel a rally in Bitcoin that could mark the beginning of a new cycle.
Bitcoin suddenly surges: Is the bear market over?
Confidence has returned to crypto markets after Bitcoin saw a sudden rally to gain more than 23% this week to trade around $77,559 at the time of writing. The price briefly topped $79,000 on Friday.
Charting platform Barchart highlighted on Thursday that Bitcoin’s (BTC) price had crossed above its 200-day moving average for the first time since November 2025.
The 200-day moving average is widely used to gauge longer-term market trends, with moves above the indicator viewed as a sign of bullish momentum. Many now believe/hope the cycle has finally flipped positive.
Ethereum gained 31%, Solana gained 28% and XRP surged an astonishing 53%.
The Bitcoin and Ether ETFs took more than $2.61 billion in inflows between them last week, and Micheal Saylor’s Bitcoin investments via Strategy have crossed the breakeven point of $75,385 — officially returning him to the status of far-sighted Bitcoin visionary, rather than degenerate financial engineer. Polymarket odds of Bitcoin reaching $90,000 before 2027 hit 48%.
Bitcoin’s weekly price chart. Source: CoinMarketCap
The rally in crypto prices was also reflected in the share prices of publicly listed crypto related firms including Canaan, Metaplanet, Coinbase and Robinhood which all saw double digit gains.
US debt policy sees rush to crypto and precious metals
The US debt pile crossed $40 trillion this week, and there’s absolutely no plan to balance the budget or to pay it down apart from a vague aspiration to grow the economy. The annual cost of paying interest on the debt has exceeded the cost of Medicare and is second only to social security as the Government’s largest expense.
The Kobeissi Letter attributed the rapid gains in precious metals and crypto to a combination of inflation, deficit spending and US Treasury policy. Record government deficit spending and the Treasury Department’s pledge to at least double the size of certain debt buyback operations to $4 billion helped drive the rally in both asset classes, Kobeissi argued.
The founder of the Bridgewater Associates hedge fund, Ray Dalio, believes investors should allocate around 15% of their portfolios to gold and “a bit of Bitcoin” to position for the impending fallout from the US’s debt problems.
“My guess, which I suppose will be a bad one, is that [a US debt crisis] will come in three years, give or take two, if the course we’re on is not changed,” said Dalio.
White House meeting with crypto leaders seeks CLARITY
US President Donald Trump has once again called for the passage of the CLARITY Act, following a meeting with crypto company executives including Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong and Gemini co-founders Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss. Trump said.
He urged members of Congress to pass “a fair version” of the bill to keep the US “ahead of China.” The market structure bill, passed by the House of Representatives in July 2025, is up for a procedural vote on September 15 that will require 60 votes in favor.
“It’s very bipartisan, I would say,” said Trump. “Lot of Democrats support.”
However Democrat Senators appear unlikely to pass the bill without further concessions on ethics provision by Trump. “I think, unfortunately, what the President means is fair to him,“ said Senator Ruben Gallego. “The president doesn’t just get to decide what level of regulation he gets.“
Trump also managed to goose the price of Hyperliquid by 20% at the meeting by revealing: “I understand that Mike [Selig, CFTC chair] is also working to bring Hyperliquid into the United States in a fully compliant and legal fashion.”
SEC unveils proposal that could spark new ICO boom
The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has proposed new rules for the cryptocurrency industry that could put pressure on lawmakers to pass the CLARITY Act or spark a new Initial Cryptocurrency Offering boom.
Currently open for a 60 day comment period, the rules offer exemptions to crypto projects that allow the issuance of up to $5 million in tokens during a four-year period, and up to $75 million during a 12-month period with stricter reporting and structure rules. There is also a safe harbor proposal exempting cryptocurrencies from being treated as ”investment contracts.”
Commissioner Hester M. Peirce said that a “whole generation has struggled” with the SEC’s application of, “a set of inapt rules to crypto.” She added the SEC’s new crypto guidelines mark an important step toward “putting clear, sensible, enforceable rules in place for crypto offerings.”
CFTC chair vows to create its own crypto rules too
Michael Selig, who chairs the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), said the commission would move forward on crypto regulations if the CLARITY Act fails to pass the Senate. Selig said he had already directed staff to allow registered and non-registered entities to offer “crypto asset trading on a leveraged or margined basis” and explore developer protections.
“We’re going to give CLARITY its breathing room for a vote, but if the Democrats cannot support a bipartisan work product, which reflects compromises from both sides of the aisle, and ultimately send a fair version of the bill to the President’s desk, then rest assured, I will direct CFTC staff to move swiftly to propose these new rules for the industry,” said Selig.

title: 加密U卡月消費首破 10 億美元：穩定幣刷進日常、雜貨佔大宗
summary:
Paymentscan 追蹤資料顯示，7 月加密卡消費達 10.4 億美元、較去年同期成長逾兩倍，超過 1,0 […]

〈加密U卡月消費首破 10 億美元：穩定幣刷進日常、雜貨佔大宗〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
Paymentscan 追蹤資料顯示，7 月加密卡消費達 10.4 億美元、較去年同期成長逾兩倍，超過 1,000 萬筆交易中七成由美元穩定幣融資，平均單筆金額從 59 美元升至 86 美元，顯示卡片用途正從「大額出金」轉向日常雜貨、外送與叫車等小額消費。
（前情提要：加密 U 卡單月消費破 7.5 億美元、880 萬筆交易：穩定幣刷進日常消費）
（背景補充：穩定幣的未來不是交易，而是日常支付）
加密貨幣刷卡消費正式跨過 10 億美元門檻。追蹤 7 月資料顯示，加密卡單月消費金額達 10.4 億美元，較去年同期成長逾兩倍；在超過 1,000 萬筆的追蹤交易中，約七成由美元穩定幣支援，Paymentscan 資料指出，平均單筆金額也從一年前的 59 美元上升到約 86 美元，代表消費者不再只用卡片搬移大額資產，而是拿它買雜貨、叫車、點外送。
加密卡的運作方式是讓使用者以穩定幣或其他加密資產，在既有支付網路上消費，商家端完全不需要直接接受加密貨幣：持卡人把資金存入發卡商或留在自保管錢包，結帳瞬間折演算法幣，商家收到的是當地幣別。換句話說，穩定幣並未取代 Visa 或 Mastercard 的清算地位，而是成為「卡片背後的金流來源」。
穩定幣結構洗牌：USDC 獨佔半壁、歐元穩定幣出局
美元穩定幣是這波刷卡成長的最大推手。7 月交易資金裡，USDC 佔 50.8%、USDT 佔 20.3%，而去年同期分別約為 48% 與 7%，USDT 的佔比一年內幾乎翻了兩倍。與此相對，歐元穩定幣 EURe 的處境呈現劇烈退潮：它在 2024 年初曾吃掉追蹤市場近 88% 的刷卡量，但到了今年 7 月只剩不到 2%，顯示卡片資金有極高的「幣種替代」彈性。
更細部的資料指出，7 月加密卡平均單筆消費 86 美元 vs 去年 59 美元，加上 2025 年 7 月全月金額 3.06 億美元對比今年 10.4 億美元，消費頻率與筆單價同時上升，方向與「日常小額採購」的敘事一致。不過 8 月資料尚未完整，動能是否延續要等下一輪財報與追蹤資料。
前三名吃下 77%：一筆自報資料的警訊
這塊快速成長的市場，地理上高度集中：RedotPay 7 月貢獻 3.951 億美元成交量，EtherFi 以 1.003 億美元居次，KAST 以 8,960 萬美元排第三，三家合計佔追蹤總量約 77%。值得留意的是，Paymentscan 對 RedotPay 的數字是「平台自報」而非鏈上直接觀測，匯總資料的真實精度存在折扣。
RedotPay 向客戶端表示，其使用者規模過去六個月增加超過 33%、現已突破 800 萬人；Ether.fi 執行長 Mike Silagadze 則確認自家 1.003 億美元純屬刷卡量，不含約 3,000 萬美元的法定貨幣轉帳，而該額度在產品上線兩個月後的 2025 年 7 月還不到 1,000 萬美元。Ether.fi 的存款多以 USDC、USDT 為主，法定幣轉帳約佔兩成。
拉丁美洲實測：雜貨、外送、USDT 都是日常
更清楚的「日常化」證據在拉丁美洲。Oobit 指出，巴西活躍使用者平均每月消費約 400 美元、拆成約 20 筆交易，其中雜貨店就佔該區活動的 35%；阿根廷則有 72% 的 Oobit 付款以 USDT 進行，餐飲食物類佔交易 41%。Oobit 巴西暨拉美主管 Prota 說，穩定幣正在一口氣做兩件事，先幫人們保住資產價值，再讓同一筆餘額轉作日常開銷。
大型交易所的卡片也都出現類似軌跡：Binance 表示旗下刷卡使用者數從上市季度到 2026 年第二季平均增加 53%、平均量增 80%，最大宗用途是叫車、外送、雜貨、餐廳與網路訂閱；Kraken 的 Krak Card 每週付款筆數較去年同期翻倍至每使用者 8.3 筆，59.3% 的消費落在商店與零售，且有半數交易並非以卡片的歐元或英鎊面額融資。
持有遠大於消費：穩定幣卡的「冰山一角」效應
不過，卡片的成長也不應過度解讀。Coinbase 回報，其信用卡與簽帳卡合計交易量中僅約 16% 與 USDC 有關；Coinbase One 活躍卡戶每月消費約 3,000 美元，對照公司全產品線持有約 200 億美元 USDC（年增 44%），明顯「持有遠多於花費」，穩定幣主要仍是儲蓄與跨境工具，卡片只是冰山露出水面的一角。
基礎設施端則持續卡位。Visa 6 月表示全球已有超過 160 個穩定幣關聯卡片計畫上線或開發中；Visa 合作夥伴 StraitsX 表示其卡片基建 2024 年第4季到 2025 年第4季交易量成長 40 倍，且低人均 GDP 市場的總交易毛額（GTV）在 2025 年 3 月到 2026 年 2 月間約成長 600%，遠高於高 GDP 市場的 150%。Oobit、StraitsX 在東南亞與拉美的進度，都在印證同一個方向：穩定幣金流正在往「普羅日常生活」遷移。
市場觀察
把數字攤開看，真正的訊號不是「加密又能刷卡」這種老話，而是金流性質的轉變：過去吃加密卡的場景以出金、套現、大額轉移為主，現在平均單筆 86 美元、一比數十筆的小額消費，意味著穩定幣在某幾個市場已經具備「抽象貨幣」的雛形。但同一套資料也提醒我們別過度樂觀：前三名集中 77%、龍頭資料自報、Coinbase 持幣與消費落差懸殊，顯示「穩定幣實體消費」仍在早環節，追蹤樣本與真實市場之間還有一段可量化的距離。
對臺灣與亞洲使用者而言，短期內最有感的未必是實體刷卡，而是跨境日常金流：東南亞低 GDP 市場 600% 的 GTV 成長，指向外匯、匯款與替代性借貸正被這類卡片快速吃掉；臺灣行動支付與金融卡滲透率高，穩定幣卡多半在境外以「多幣種卡片」形式切入旅遊與跨境工作者場景，本地銀行若跟進推出穩定幣儲值卡，將直接面對的是 KYC 身份驗證與虛擬貨幣監理（VASP）法令的合規成本，而非技術門檻。
後續觀察的重點有二：其一，8 月完整資料出爐後，7 月的高點是偶發還是趨勢，將由「平均單筆金額與筆數是否持續走升」決定；其二，一旦美國穩定幣政策環境明朗，美元穩定幣在卡片資金盤的優勢可能進一步擴大，而 EURe 從 88% 崩潰至 2% 的歷史告訴我們，幣種之間的「替換速度」可以非常快。

title: Fed 研究揭密：加密投資人靠「信念」進場，看到比特幣漲就加碼
summary:
克利夫蘭聯邦準備銀行最新研究顯示：美國人買加密貨幣，關鍵不是人口結構或風險胃口，而是對未來報酬的「信念」。持倉 […]

〈Fed 研究揭密：加密投資人靠「信念」進場，看到比特幣漲就加碼〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
克利夫蘭聯邦準備銀行最新研究顯示：美國人買加密貨幣，關鍵不是人口結構或風險胃口，而是對未來報酬的「信念」。持倉者平均預期年報酬 22%、非持倉者僅 7%，且只要讓受試者看到比特幣過去 12 個月漲幅，希望配置就會跳升近五成、實際購買隨之增加 2.5 個百分點。
（前情提要：是你嗎？Fed統計：年輕男性、亞洲人、高收入族群，最愛投資加密貨幣！）
（背景補充：機構研究：11% 美國人因「炒幣財富自由」辭職，且多來自低收入階層）
為什麼加密貨幣的價格行為，跟股票、債券、黃金如此不同？克利夫蘭聯邦準備銀行一份最新研究論文給出一個頗具挑釁性的答案：美國人購買加密資產，關鍵不在人口結構或風險偏好，而在於他們對加密貨幣未來報酬的「信念」。這份題為《Do You Even Crypto, Bro? Cryptocurrencies in Household Finance》的工作論文，由研究人員 Michael Weber、Bernardo Candia、Olivier Coibion 與 Yuriy Gorodnichenko 共同撰寫，樣本是每波多達兩萬五千個美國家庭的接力調查。
研究指出，加密貨幣特有的高波動與「漲勢吸引新買家」的現象，可能形成一個自我強化的回饋迴圈：上漲的價格強化樂觀預期，再把更多投資人拉進市場。這份論文同時以隨機資訊實驗證明，光是讓受試者得知比特幣（BTC）過去的漲幅，就足以同時推高他們想要的加密配置比例與後續實際購買金額。
持有者預期年報酬 22%，非持有者僅 7%
調查結果顯示，加密貨幣持有者與非持有者對報酬的預期落差極大：願意給出預測的人當中，持倉者平均預期未來一年報酬率達 22%，非持倉者卻只有 7%；持倉者也普遍認為加密資產的風險比非持倉者眼中來得低。
更關鍵的是，期望報酬對「是否持有」的解釋力異乎尋常。研究者發現，個人預期加密報酬率每上升 1 個百分點，其持有加密貨幣的機率就提高 0.8 個百分點：報酬與風險兩項期望合計，對持有行為變異的解釋力，高過年齡、收入、性別等可觀測特徵的總和。這與傳統資產完全相反，對股票、債券與黃金而言，人口與財務特徵通常遠比報酬預期更能解釋持有與否。
- 未滿 40 歲者的持有率，比 60 歲以上族群高出 13 個百分點
- 男性比女性更可能持有加密貨幣，差距約 4 個百分點
- 高收入與較富裕的家庭參與率更高
研究者也引述 2021 年聯邦儲備調查指出加密貨幣認知基礎的薄弱：當年 87% 的非持有者坦言，不知道未來一年該對比特幣預期什麼報酬；即使是持有者，這個比率仍高達 54%。
隨機實驗：秀出比特幣過去漲幅，散戶就忍不住加碼
論文最重要的市場含義，來自 2025 年實施的隨機資訊實驗。研究者把受試家庭隨機分成幾組，分別提供比特幣、股票、GameStop 或通貨膨脹的資訊，其中一組只看了比特幣過去 12 個月的報酬。結果，這組受試者期望的加密資產配置比例平均提高 2 個百分點，但對照組原本只有 4.3% 的配置意願而言，等於跳升約 47%；後續實際發生的加密購買行為，也增加約 2.5 個百分點。
效果集中在那些「因為資訊不足所以沒買」的人身上，已經認定加密是壞投資的受試者，對這項資訊幾乎沒有反應。作者描述此結果為「讓家庭得知比特幣近期報酬，確實會誘使一部分家戶開始購買加密貨幣」。
加密收益像彩券：財富進門，但只花在耐久財
研究還觸及「幣價上漲對實體消費的外溢效果」。當比特幣價格翻倍，全部資產都押在加密市場的家庭，購買耐久財（冷氣、冰箱、電子產品等）的機率增加 1.4 個百分點，相對增幅約 7%；但一般日常消費幾乎不受影響。研究者因此下了犀利的對照：加密貨幣的收益，在家庭資產負債表上比較像「賭博收入」或中了樂透彩，而不是「永久財富的增加」。
後續觀察
這份研究為加密市場的波動提供了一個不太舒服的解釋路徑：波動的根源，有一部分其實來自投資者之間的意見分歧與「學習」過程，而非基本面本身。作者在結論中直接給出預言：「投資者之間缺乏共同的資訊與信念，意味著價格波動在可預見的將來，仍將是這一類新資產最顯著的特徵。」
把這套機制投射到臺灣，臺北街頭的情境一點都不陌生：散戶的加密資訊多半來自社交群組、社群媒體與各大平台的行情通知，偏偏這些管道的內容高度「報喜不報憂」，正如實驗中「只展示過去漲幅」的操作。對監管者與教育機構而言，研究也指出了界線：對「資訊不足」的人補充正確知識是有效的擴大市場認知基盤途徑，但對已經把加密歸類為「壞投資」的族群，任何資訊恐怕都難以動搖，這點與金管會長期以來「恐嚇式」風險警示的效果相同，可能是同一侷限的背面。
後續觀察的重點有兩個：其一，若比特幣進入深度回檔，同一回饋迴圈將反向執行，糟糕的報酬資訊將加速散戶離場，波動率可能反過來自我實現；其二，下一波零售需求的規模，恐怕不完全取決於比特幣漲到多少，而取決於市場讓潛在買家「看到」了怎樣的過去價格。某種程度上，投資人真正交易的，是市場刻意或無意間遞送的歷史故事。

title: Tether 砸 1.2 億美元烏拉圭挖礦案熄火：與國營電力契約談判僵持遭斷電
summary:
穩定幣巨擘 Tether 在烏拉圭投入約 1.2 億美元的比特幣挖礦計畫，最終在 2025 年遭國營電力公司 […]

〈Tether 砸 1.2 億美元烏拉圭挖礦案熄火：與國營電力契約談判僵持遭斷電〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
穩定幣巨擘 Tether 在烏拉圭投入約 1.2 億美元的比特幣挖礦計畫，最終在 2025 年遭國營電力公司 UTE 斷電、同年 11 月正式收掉營運。報導指關鍵在於雙方對「供電額度」的契約定義歧異，隨左翼新政府上任而僵持；Tether 並未放棄南美，反而轉向投資再生能源業者與發展挖礦基建。
（前情提要：Tether 烏拉圭比特幣礦場傳「欠鉅額電費」停挖，官方回應：與政府洽談中）
（背景補充：最大比特幣礦工夢》Tether合作南美農業公司Adecoagro，匯入再生電力挖礦）
穩定幣巨擘 Tether 在烏拉圭的比特幣挖礦計畫，近期被證實正式熄火。這樁被視為進軍南美市場代表作、估計投入約 1.2 億美元的案子，從 2023 年 5 月高調進場，到 2025 年 7 月遭烏拉圭國營電力公司 UTE 切斷電力而中斷，最終在同年 11 月正式結束營運，背後是一場對「供電額度」定義互異的契約紛擾。
契約歧見：是「保底供量」還是「硬性上限」？
據路透社報導與取得的多份檔案，Tether 與 UTE 的核心分歧，在於礦場所享有的電力額度：Tether 主張雙方談定的供電量是「最低門檻、日後還可上調」，UTE 則認定那是「硬性上限」，不能再增。兩座位於烏拉圭的礦場，初期運作順暢、穩定獲利，但在用電需求攀升後，不時一連數日用電不足。
- Tether 官方至今沒有公開此案實際投資金額，僅有知情人士估計約 1.2 億美元（約合新臺幣 36 億元）
- 前承包商形容，烏拉圭被 Tether 視為進軍南美市場的敲門磚
- 多方訊息指出，2025 年 3 月烏拉圭左翼政府上臺後，談判態度轉趨強硬
換屆成為轉折：新董事態度更硬
關鍵轉折發生在 2025 年 3 月烏拉圭迎來左翼政府，新任 UTE 董事對契約談判態度明顯轉趨強硬。Tether 設立的在地法人 Microfin，在政府交接後約兩個月內停止繳交電費，並於 6 月告知 UTE 有意終止契約。在修訂契約遲遲未獲簽署、電費又持續欠繳之下，UTE 於 2025 年 7 月 25 日直接切斷電力；同年 11 月 25 日，Tether 正式通知烏拉圭勞工主管機關將結束營運、裁員多數員工，正式退場。
緣起與布局：看好再生能源，卻難敵電力成本
時間拉回 2023 年 5 月，Tether 宣布進軍烏拉圭，當時形容當地是「完美平台」，理由是充沛的再生能源與成熟電網，加上政治穩定、吸引外資。前承包商透露，烏拉圭被 Tether 視為進軍南美前的試點，有望複製到巴拉圭、巴西與阿根廷。
2025 年 6 月，執行長 Paolo Ardoino 仍公開喊話，要成為「全球最大比特幣礦工」；Tether 一度宣稱已在烏拉圭、巴拉圭、薩爾瓦多等地落實 20 億美元以上的能源與挖礦基建，但一個月後 UTE 就斷了那兩座礦場的電力。
擴張未止：從挖礦轉向 AI 資料中心
值得注意的是，退出烏拉圭並不代表 Tether 放棄南美。它後續收購再生能源業者股權、發布開源挖礦作業系統、投資挖礦業融資公司，並與多家業者開發模組化挖礦系統；旗下 USDT 流通量逾 1,830 億美元，仍是穩定幣龍頭。
更深層的訊號在於產業結構：分析師 Nicolas Ribeiro 直言，挖礦業「極度動態」，礦場頻繁遷移；而電網穩定、網路基建良好的烏拉圭，反而更適合 AI 資料中心而非挖礦，因為挖礦極度倚賴廉價電力，而烏拉圭電價偏高，他直接點出「烏拉圭並不適合挖礦」。
市場意義與後續觀察
對加密產業而言，Tether 的烏拉圭案透露三個訊號：其一，比特幣挖礦已非「買礦機、吃低價電」的簡單生意，與政府、電力業者的談判策略可能直接影響礦場存續；其二，新興市場雖有吸引力，但能源監管與政壇週期風險更難估；其三，AI 算力商機的資源排擠，正持續打擊純挖礦業的經濟性。
後續可觀察：Tether 是否仿效投資再生能源公司的路線，以控股能源公司而非自建礦場的方式，重新切入南美；以及這場契約紛爭，能否成為其他礦業業者在新興市場落地時的重要借鑑。

title: SEC 發布「Reg Crypto」規則草案：代幣募資界線明朗，60 天意見期開跑
summary:
美國證券交易委員會（SEC）上週正式發布俗稱「Reg Crypto」的加密貨幣募資規則草案，擬為加密公司與開發 […]

〈SEC 發布「Reg Crypto」規則草案：代幣募資界線明朗，60 天意見期開跑〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
美國證券交易委員會（SEC）上週正式發布俗稱「Reg Crypto」的加密貨幣募資規則草案，擬為加密公司與開發者列出以發行代幣籌資的合規界線，並開放公眾 60 天陳述意見。業界肯定方向正面，但多位法務人士仍呼籲國會通過《Clarity Act》補足框架缺口。
（前情提要：【重要內容整理】美國國會眾議院舉行的加密貨幣與ICO監管聽證會）
（背景補充：a16z 監管團隊報告》一覽最新全球 Crypto 法規大事件整理：SEC、CFTC、司法部….）
美國證券交易委員會（SEC）上週正式發布俗稱「Reg Crypto」的加密貨幣募資規則草案，列出加密公司與開發者如何在不觸犯證券法的前提下，以發行代幣為自家新創籌措資金的具體條件。這是近年美國聯邦層級罕見的一次正式規則立案，也是 SEC 從零散員工意見、轉向制度化監理的訊號。
Reg Crypto：代幣募資終於有白紙黑字界線
草案的核心，是替「用發幣為公司籌資」這條路徑（也就是過往常見的募資代幣模式）訂下合規框架。根據新創預計籌募的規模與營運方式，草案提供不同條件與分級規則，SEC 官方公告全文列出細節，並從即日起開放公眾 60 天陳述意見。
Cahill Gordon & Reindel 律師事務所合夥人 Lewis Cohen 直言：「這走了很長一段路，方向性絕對正面，SEC 投入的時間、努力與精力值得肯定。」但他也提醒，草案只是墊腳石，業界真正需要的完整框架仍寄託於國會立法。
川普聯手業界喊話：通過《Clarity Act》
美國總統川普上週三與多位加密與傳統金融業者高管同臺開記者會，公開呼籲國會通過《Clarity Act》。同臺者包括 SEC 主席 Paul Atkins、CFTC 主席 Mike Selig、Coinbase 執行長 Brian Armstrong 與 Kraken 執行長 Arjun Sethi 等人。
記者會次日，CFTC 創新顧問委員會接著登場。Selig 在場表示，若《Clarity Act》未能成為法律，CFTC 也已準備好主動啟動自家管轄的規則制訂工作。換句話說，SEC 與 CFTC 兩大聯邦監管機構都已把「正式法律」當作下一步，而非停留在口頭表態。
為什麼重要：從「員工意見」到「正式立案」
川普政府上任以來，SEC 對加密貨幣多數時候以工作人員聲明、政策指引處理，並未真正展開正式立法程序。「Reg Crypto」是少數進入正式規則立案的案子，象徵監督從空中喊話走向實際落地。但草案仍需要時間完成最終程序，業者再需時間合規，這中間的窗口，恰好是《Clarity Act》能否在國會過關的關鍵期。
市場觀察與後續看點
對想發幣募資的新創而言，這份草案等同把過往「能不能發」的灰色地帶，變成「該怎麼發才合規」的具體指引，有望降低 ICO 募資的整體法律風險，吸引更多項目方把代幣發行當作正規資金管道。可後續有兩個觀察點：其一，60 天公眾日結束後，SEC 能否在任期內完成最終規則並放行合規代幣；其二，若國會最終通過《Clarity Act》，它以更高的立法位階蓋過這份草案，將讓 Reg Crypto 的規定退居次位，兩條路線的競速，決定美國代幣募資的長期遊戲規則。亞洲市場也值得留意：臺灣與日本的監理做法多以「證券商法規納管」為主，未如美國單獨訂立代幣募資草案，各國差異這輪政策將如何推進，值得持續追蹤。

title: AI 代理成加密「下個十億用戶」？USDC 搶下機對機支付先機
summary:
AI 代理正成為支付系統的全新客戶群：它們自主為資料、算力與線上工具付費，穩定幣（尤其 USDC）在微小額度高 […]

〈AI 代理成加密「下個十億用戶」？USDC 搶下機對機支付先機〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
AI 代理正成為支付系統的全新客戶群：它們自主為資料、算力與線上工具付費，穩定幣（尤其 USDC）在微小額度高頻的機對機支付中取得先機，Coinbase、Cloudflare、MoonPay、Visa 與 Mastercard 相繼搶建軌道。Coinbase x402 協議至今已處理逾 1.65 億筆支付，累計金額 5,000 萬美元，其中約 99% 以 USDC 支付。
（前情提要：解讀Crypto+AI Agents：下個十億用戶的真正突破口？）
（背景補充：Stripe 啟動 AI Agent 全自動支付測試：透過 x402 支援 Base 鏈 USDC 付款）
隨著 AI 代理從對話機器人進化成能獨立執行多步驟任務的軟體，加密貨幣產業苦等多年的「下一個十億用戶」可能正在以意想不到的形態出現，不是缺乏銀行帳戶的開發中國家人口，也不是想逃離惡性通膨的避險者，「用戶」本身可能就是一段程式。而這群「程式用戶」想買東西時，穩定幣率先拿到了它們的錢包。
Coinbase 開發的 x402 支付協議，本質上是替軟體設計的「付費牆」：代理索取資料或服務時，賣家回覆價格與收款資訊，代理付款、系統驗證無誤後交付結果。賣家不必開設帳號、代理也不必手動輸入卡號，全程無人介入。Coinbase 人工智慧產品主管 Lincoln Murr 直言：「現在的產品市場契合，就是代理到 API 的機對機支付。」
資料怎麼說：1.65 億筆、5,000 萬美元、99% 都是 USDC
Coinbase 今年稍早公布，x402 已處理超過 1.65 億筆支付、累計金額 5,000 萬美元；4 月的生態系統更新更記錄超過 48 萬個代理。Murr 估計其中約 99% 的交易以 USDC 結算，平均每筆金額約 0.3 美元。他坦言，目前的白熱化仍處「Napster 與 LimeWire 時代」，如同早期網際網路，人人都在實驗，卻還沒有人真正搞清楚商業模式；甚至有 25% 至 30% 的交易量，來自想爬公開排行榜的測試行為，而非真實購物需求。
以美元計，已揭露的交易規模仍然很小：7 月 30 日內 x402 移轉金額約 2,400 萬美元，大約只等於 Visa 一分鐘的處理量。但 Murr 認為結構本身值得注意：單一軟體代理完成一個任務時，可能向數十個服務各付一次費，把一整包月費訂閱拆成一連串幾美分的微支付。
為什麼是穩定幣：微支付經濟學的必然
這些早期付費場景正是加密貨幣的強項：全球可用、全天候運作、金額小到信用卡成本吃不消。Murr 指出信用卡收單成本約 2% 至 4%，當商品售價不到 1 美元、再加固定處理費時，卡組織的經濟模型完全失靈。穩定幣則能繞過這些摩擦，賣家或支付商可以直接吸收鏈上手續費。Cloudflare 錢包設計策略長 Stephanie Cohen 表示，穩定幣特別適合 AI 代理初期的大量微小額度、高頻支付場景，API 呼叫、資料、推論內容都屬於這類。
Cloudflare 還在規劃 Monetization Gateway，讓網站可以對單一頁面、資料集或線上工具逐筆收費，取代整套月費訂閱；Circle 的 Nanopayments 則先在測試網快速確認小額付款，之後再合併上鏈；MoonPay 的 PayBox 讓代理直接呼叫用戶的卡片與加密錢包，同時支援 x402 與 Visa 兩條軌道。
信用卡沒打算讓位：萬事達改走「可驗證憑證」
卡組織並非坐以待斃。Mastercard 推出 Agent Pay for Machines，以「可驗證憑證」（Verifiable Vouchers）為代理設定可購買的項目與額度上限：賣家核對規則、提供服務、事後批次請款，不必把每筆微支付都丟進完整清分流程。其代幣化與結帳服務執行副總 Sapan Mandloi 強調：「代理商務會是多軌道並存的環境，穩定幣是既有支付系統的互補，不是取代。」銀行的角色同樣在測試：星展銀行（DBS）與 Visa 2 月已示範代理用 DBS/POSB 信用卡購物，下一步將測試線上購物與旅遊訂房，這類大額消費仍需要退款與爭議處理機制，正好與 30 美分的 API 微支付形成對比。
轉錯帳戶怎麼辦：控制權比軌道更重要
付款只是問題的一半。代理可能誤解指令、選錯服務，甚至被惡意提示詞操縱，這讓「先限制代理再放行」成為 Coinbase、Cloudflare、Mastercard、MoonPay 與錢包商 Turnkey 共同的防線：餘額上限、白名單賣家、單筆限額與敏感操作需人工核准。Turnkey 共同創辦人 Bryce Ferguson 比喻：「就像自駕車早期需要人扶著方向盤，現在就是代理的這個階段。」Cloudflare 的 Cohen 也點出另一面：一筆幾美分的付款，反詐騙成本可能比詐騙損失本身還高，此時賣家聲譽比完整爭議流程更重要。
觀察與後續
整體而言，代理支付市場仍遠落後於最樂觀的預測：Cloudflare 錢包尚未全面上線、Mastercard 仍在早期試點、MoonPay 未公布使用規模、Turnkey 坦言活動量未到規模化，連最成熟的 x402 都有相當比例的交易來自排行榜測試。最大瓶頸其實在「把錢放進代理口袋」的第一步：Murr 坦言「申請錢包依然是巨大的痛點」。對臺灣與亞洲讀者的意義在於：當訂閱制逐漸被逐筆購買侵蝕，穩定幣在跨境與微支付領域的基礎設施價值會被反覆驗證，x402 的交易集中在 Base 鏈（Coinbase 的二層網路），這意味著鏈上微支付的真實需求正在被測量，而非停留在概念簡報。後續值得追蹤三件事：其一，Cloudflare 與 Mastercard 的產品何時從試點走向正式商用；其二，代理誤購的責任歸屬能否在產業內達成共識；其三，fiat onramp（法幣入金）是否成為代理資金來源的主流解方，這將決定穩定幣的「先機」能否轉成「格局」。

title: Term Finance 遭治理漏洞竊走 850 萬美元：七天鎖定期與 LP 否決齊失守
summary:
以太坊固定利率借貸協議 Term Finance 的金庫在週日遭治理漏洞攻擊，約 850 萬美元被不明攻擊者領 […]

〈Term Finance 遭治理漏洞竊走 850 萬美元：七天鎖定期與 LP 否決齊失守〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
以太坊固定利率借貸協議 Term Finance 的金庫在週日遭治理漏洞攻擊，約 850 萬美元被不明攻擊者領走。資安公司 PeckShield 追查到 2,843 顆以太幣（約 690 萬美元）與 168 萬顆 USDC（已兌換約 168 萬 DAI），並指向一個曾從 Tornado Cash 收到 2 ETH 的地址；CertiK 同樣估算損失約 850 萬美元。儘管 Term 的金庫設有七天時間鎖與流動性提供者（LP）的否決權，仍未能擋下這次攻擊。
（前情提要：快訊》借貸協議Euler Finance遭閃電貸攻擊！損失近2億美元、＄EUL重挫45%）
（背景補充：DeFi犯罪頻傳！今年迄今已損失超過 120 億美元，九成發生在以太坊和 BSC）
以太坊固定利率借貸協議 Term Finance 的金庫在週日遭治理漏洞攻擊，約 850 萬美元被不明攻擊者領走。開發者 Term Labs 在 X 平台上證實「我們已留意到一起影響 Term 金庫的治理漏洞」，並表示進一步調查後會公布更多細節，但未證實損失規模，也未點名受波及的金庫。
資安公司 PeckShield 在 X 上追蹤指出，攻擊者領走約 2,843 顆以太幣（估值約 690 萬美元）與 168 萬顆 USDC（約 168 萬美元），後者已被兌換成約 168 萬顆 DAI。資金最終流向一個 Etherscan 可追蹤的單一地址，該地址最初從混幣協議 Tornado Cash 收到 2 顆以太幣作為啟動資金。
資安監控機構 CertiK 另在 X 上估算損失約 850 萬美元，並指 2,843 顆 ETH 與約 160 萬顆 DAI 目前仍停留在上述地址。
治理架構為何攔不住？
Term 的 Strategy Vaults 是建立在 Yearn V3 基礎設施之上的 ERC-4626 代幣化金庫，把資金配置於 Term 的固定利率借貸市場與變動利率借貸協議之間。Yearn 事後在 X 上解釋：「雖然這些合約架在 Yearn V3 之上，但漏洞發生在環繞金庫的自訂治理包裝，這個攻擊向量不適用於標準 Yearn 金庫；存在於標準 Yearn 金庫的資金是安全的，未受影響。」
Term 金庫的治理結構把操作控制與存戶監督分開：「管理者」角色負責拍賣操作，「控制器」角色監督風險引數、協議配置與緊急功能；流動性提供者（LP）以 DAO 身分參與，可在七天時間鎖內表決否決排隊中的治理交易。依照 Term 的治理檔案，LP 成功否決後交易便無法執行。控制器可更動協議控制器、價格預言機、風險限制，也能暫停存款或策略活動。但 Term 至今未透露攻擊者動用了哪個角色，也未被解釋為何時間鎖與 LP 否決擋不住這些交易。
損失佔金庫 TVL 的三分之二
攻擊發生前，Term 金庫的鎖定總值（TVL）約為 1,245 萬美元，其中以太坊鏈佔約 880 萬美元。而這場約 850 萬美元的損失，約等於金庫產品在全部鏈上 TVL 的三分之二，幾乎把金庫在以太坊上的 TVL 搬空。
宏觀而言，Term Finance 整體在攻擊前的 TVL 約 2,580 萬美元，另有約 379 萬美元活貸；金庫只是產品之一，卻成了這回被擊穿的核心。
並非首次：2025 年 oracle 誤設曾釀 160 萬美元損失
Term Finance 過去也曾處理過類似的損失：2025 年 4 月，其 tETH 市場因 oracle 設定不當導致異常清算，損失約 160 萬美元，協議最終尋回其中逾 100 萬美元，剩餘由協議財庫補足。
治理攻擊：DeFi 長期弱點
DeFi 協議長年對治理攻擊缺乏抵抗力，攻擊者可透過閃電借貸或廉價代幣發動。今年 3 月，一名攻擊者只花約 1,800 美元買代幣推動提案，就危及價值約 108 萬美元的 Moonwell 資產；2022 年，Beanstalk 則在一場閃電貸治理攻擊中損失約 1.82 億美元。
市場影響：多層防線是否淪為儀式感
這次事件最值得留意的不是金額本身，而是防線集中失守。一個同時具備七天時間鎖、LP 否決權、管理者與控制器分工的金庫，卻仍被單一治理漏洞擊穿，這代表「多層防線」的敘事與實際防護之間存在落差。對主打固定利率、安全可靠的 DeFi 借貸協議而言，金庫層被直接突破，動搖的是整個協議的使用者信任。
後續觀察重點有二：其一，Term Labs 是否會公布攻擊者實際利用的角色與交易路徑，將決定這套治理架構能否真的阻止後續，還是紙上防線；其二，追回進度，2025 年 oracle 事件的回收比超過六成，但本次資金繞經混幣與穩定幣匯兌路徑，追回難度更高。治理漏洞這類攻擊若能持續繞過自定義治理層，恐怕不是重修檔案能搞定，而需重新設計治理控制的分離與邊界。

title: Australian shark attack victim grateful for 'second chance at life'
summary: Leah Stewart was mauled by a shark in June, suffering multiple bites to her arms and legs.
full_text:
Australian shark attack victim grateful for 'second chance at life'
- Published
An Australian woman bitten by a shark at a popular Sydney beach earlier this year says she has been given a "second chance at life" and will be making the most of it.
Leah Stewart, 35, was mauled by a shark during a morning swim at Coogee Beach in June, suffering multiple bites to her arms and legs, amid a spate of attacks in Australia.
The mother-of-one was placed in an induced coma and had several surgeries, including having one of her arms amputated.
In an online post on Monday, she thanked her supporters who have raised more than AU$550,000 (US$394,000; £289,000) for her, saying her recovery has been "incredibly difficult" but she is making "remarkable" progress.
"After what has been an incredibly difficult few months, I'm so happy that I've progressed enough to build some independence, and I can finally see some light after all of this," Stewart wrote, in her first comments since the attack.
"I want you to know that I feel like I've been given a second chance at life, and I'm not going to waste it."
Stewart said she had been "overwhelmed" by the support from family, friends and "even strangers", adding that the "you've inspired me to get better, not bitter".
An online fundraiser for her would now be closed, she wrote, with the money raised giving her the chance to recover at home as well as "options for further medical treatment down the road".
"I still have a long way to go, but my recovery has been remarkable, and a huge part of that is because of the absolute army of love, support, prayers and encouragement surrounding my family and I from all over the world."
There have been a spate of shark attacks in Australia this year, with four attacks over a two-day period in January, including one on a 12-year-old boy who later died from his injuries.
In May, a man was killed by a shark in Queensland while spearfishing and in Western Australia, a father-of-two died after he was attacked by a 4m (13ft) shark.

title: Review launched into how pub and hotel business rates calculated
summary: The review of how rates are calculated in England and Wales could lead to reform of the system.
full_text:
Review launched into how pub and hotel business rates calculated
- Published
A review is being launched into the way business rates are calculated for pubs and hotels in England and Wales, and could lead to a reform of the system.
The Treasury says business rates expert Jerry Schurder will lead the review into rate valuations and report back in March 2027, with the government calling for the views of landlords, hoteliers and business owners to feed in to the process.
Last month, Andy Burnham announced a 20% cut in business rates for pubs, social clubs and live music venues in England, to come into effect in April.
Pub groups have argued they face disproportionately higher rates bills, but other businesses have called for a wider reform of the rates system.
According to the British Beer and Pub Association (BBPA), 161 pubs closed in the first three months of this year across England, Scotland and Wales, equating to the loss of around 2,400 jobs.
Rising business rates are cited as one issue facing the sector, although there have also been complaints that increases in National Insurance and the minimum wage have made staff costs more expensive.
James Murray, financial secretary to the Treasury, said the new review would look at "a rethink of valuations - so that we can build a fairer system for the future".
Emma McClarkin, chief executive of the BBPA, said: "For years pubs have paid a disproportionately higher business rates bill which has ground down their ability to keep the doors open, so this review is sorely needed and hugely welcome."
The BBPA says pubs are valued differently for rates than retail venues. Instead of being based just on floor area, they are judged by a measure called Fair Maintainable Trade - which means when a pub's turnover increases, so does its rates bill.
Schurder is a former business rates policy lead at advisory firm Newmark UK, and his review will feed into the next rates revaluation in 2029.
His appointment was welcomed by Craig Beaumont of the Federation of Small Businesses (FSB) who said he would bring "crucial heavyweight business rates expertise into the Treasury".
However, Beaumont said the government needed to address the wider business rates system and exempt more smaller firms by increasing the rates relief threshold for small businesses.
Tom Ironside from the British Retail Consortium also welcomed the review but said it was "vitally important that the needs of retailers are not overlooked".
Shadow Chancellor Sir Mel Stride said the review was "far too late for a sector this Labour government has already done its best to kill off".
"Tax hikes on business premises and jobs, alongside job-destroying regulation in the Employment Rights Act, have left many hospitality businesses on the brink," he said.
Liberal Democrat Treasury spokesperson Daisy Cooper said reform of business rates was "long overdue", but also called for an emergency VAT cut and a reverse to jobs tax changes "which have hammered hospitality in particular".
Last year, under the previous chancellor Rachel Reeves, the government had said it would scale back business rate discounts that had been in force since the Covid pandemic and announced that there would be no discount at all from April this year.
That, combined with big upward adjustments to rateable values of pub premises, left landlords with the prospect of much higher bills.
Following criticism from the hospitality industry, the government cut business rates for pubs and music venues by 15% earlier in 2026.
The 20% discount in England announced in July will apply on top of the existing support.
However, the government said the rates discount would not apply to the "very largest" live music venues, and there was some confusion among some businesses as to whether they would be classed as a pub and therefore eligible for the relief.
Details about which businesses are eligible are expected to be announced at Chancellor John Healey's first Budget in the autumn.

title: Why students are being paid £2,000 to play computer games
summary: Roehampton University offers students £2,000 a year to play esports alongside their studies.
full_text:
Why students are being paid £2,000 to play computer games
- Published
As parents across the country prepare to wave their children off to university, conversations about family finances and the cost of living are growing ever more frequent - and fervent.
Yet every year, millions of pounds worth of scholarships and bursary funding goes unclaimed by students - with many unaware the extra help exists.
So roll up the next generation of gamers, who this year can apply for as esports scholarship from the University of Roehampton - with more than 100 handed out so far.
But can the students balance their studies and their esports? And is the scholarship set to catch on?
Esports, meaning electronic sports, is the name for competitive video gaming.
It is different from standard video gaming as esports includes spectators, much like traditional sports.
Gamers compete against one another in high-stakes tournaments for cash prizes and trophies.
- Do esports students do more than play games? 
  - Published22 June
What's the scholarship about?
Roehampton is offering esports scholarships to undergraduate and postgraduate students who show that they can balance academic progress and video-gaming excellence.
"This scholarship is about recognising talent in a field that has a growing popularity both around the world and among our students," University of Roehampton registrar Mark Ellul said.
Scholars are expected to compete in weekly university tournaments as well as representing the university at in-person events.
Roehampton requires minimum rankings in major games for the scholarship, but will consider applications from those close to the threshold who meet other criteria, such as having large followings on streaming platforms like Twitch.
Former esports scholar Cameron Dray found out about Roehampton through the esports scholarship. Inspired by similar initiatives at American universities, he looked into whether anything similar was on offer in the UK.
Initially, the university was offering just £1,500, but due to the team's performance and rise in popularity, the amount was raised to £2,000.
"This money was crucial to me as it gave me the opportunity to study in a very expensive city without the need for part-time work," Dray said.
"There were requirements that came alongside the scholarship, but none that were unexpected or not transparent when applying," he added.
What to know about student finance
Dray encouraged students to make use of every scholarship, bursary and opportunity available to them.
He said: "Many of these funds are available to more students than they realise, and everyone should be taking full advantage."
The average graduate in England leaves university with debts of more than £47,500. Scholarships such as Roehampton's can reduce student debt and provide additional financial support.
Thomas Cole, an esports player nicknamed Pac who specialises in the racing game Trackmania, said universities offering unique scholarships, including esports, encourages students academically by reducing the level of financial stress they might face.
"Uni students being paid to play a game alongside doing their studies, it's definitely cracking. If I had gone to uni, I would have loved that," he says.
"If it doesn't let the academic side suffer, then I think being offered something like that really spurs on people to be better in gaming," he says.
Tom Allingham, student money expert from the Save the Student personal finance site, regularly advises incoming first years to seek out scholarships and learn more about what their university offers.
"Unfortunately, I don't think there is enough awareness on scholarships," he said.
"There is a lot of funding that goes unclaimed because students don't know that they're eligible for it," he added.
Save the Student helps share various scholarships and bursaries on their website.
"What we try to get across is you can get extra funding for so many different reasons."

title: 'I didn't speak the Queen's English': Why people worry about their accents
summary: A survey on attitudes towards accents suggests that so-called "accent bias" is still an issue in many workplaces.
full_text:
'I didn't speak the Queen's English': Why people worry about their accents
- Published
Growing up in Manchester, Mia Tanswell didn't give her accent much thought - until her first week at university in Loughborough.
"I knew people were going to notice that I was northern and that I didn't speak the 'Queen's English'," the 22-year-old says.
"Definitely in seminars I would sometimes feel like my accent would sound a bit less intellectual than other people, especially if I was the only northern student in the classroom."
She's not alone. Fresh polling seen by the BBC suggests many workers still see so-called "accent bias" as a problem.
The survey found one in 10 people in Britain feel anxious or self-conscious about their accent in high stakes professional settings such as speaking up in a business meeting.
The research, conducted by the organisation More in Common of more than 3,300 adults across England, Scotland and Wales, found accent-related anxiety in work settings like these was highest among Geordies - from the region around Newcastle - and those with an east London - or Cockney - accent (at 19%), followed by people with a Welsh accent (at 18%).
Around 5% of respondents believed their accent had cost them a promotion, pay rise or senior role. "Brummies" - people from Birmingham - were the most likely to feel this, at 13%.
Respondents with a West Country accent reported the highest rate of having their accent mocked or criticised by colleagues, at 15%, followed by 13% of those with a Geordie accent.
The poll was commissioned by Common Ground, an organisation which aims to promote social cohesion. Its founder, Lara Newman, has worked in construction, property and the built environment industry for more than 30 years, and says she changed her own accent to get ahead in the workplace.
"I am incredibly realistic about what would have happened had I gone to university or gone into the workplace with a strong west country accent," she says. "I felt like that was going to be an issue for me."
Common Ground aims to support people from disadvantaged backgrounds into work but she says one of the layers creating a barrier to them is accent.
"I think there is a problem in the sense that [an accent] implies a level of education or otherwise. It implies class," she says.
'I wish it was more Welsh'
Martha Powell, 24, from Newport in south Wales is proud of her accent.
"I love my accent, if anything I wish it was more Welsh," she says.
But she still fears people "make assumptions" based on her accent so at networking events she gravitates towards others with a Welsh accent.
"I wish I would be able to stand out a little bit more, but I think I adapt my accent depending on where I am in the country."
Softening an accent is common, the survey results suggest, with 13% of Britons polled admitting to changing the way they speak to sound more professional, with Cockneys and Scots more likely to do this.
A foreign, rather than a regional accent, can also be a barrier. When Benjaimin Aidomoan came to the UK four years ago from the Czech Republic aged 16, he didn't speak a word of English.
He picked up the language, but four years on says his accent has made job-hunting more difficult.
"You can just see on many people's faces, that the expression and the way they are looking at you and the way they are talking to you kind of changes," he says.
Benjaimin, who now works in a restaurant, believes most employers do look beyond accents.
"It's about who you are, how you present yourself, what is your attitude and how hard you're willing to work," he says.
'We don't judge'
Most employers would say that is at least their ambition, to treat applicants and employees equally, regardless of their accent.
Charlotte Davies, career expert at LinkedIn, says while there is still progress to be made "the direction of travel is encouraging".
"Hiring is increasingly about skills, not background or polish.
"Your accent is part of your story, and the workplaces getting this right, treat that as a strength, not something to smooth out," she says.
Sian Jackson, a partner at law firm Mills & Reeve, says her company has recently changed its approach to encourage more local hiring and a diversity of accents.
"We don't judge, we scrutinise based on capability beyond somebody's accent, or appearance. Like any other prejudice or bias it's about being conscious of it so you can then set it aside," she says.
"We feel we've come a long way as a firm, but we are behind nationally compared to things like gender, so there is more progress to be made on accents."
